title: 50 Major Achievements Attributed To President Tinubu's Administration Since 2023
main_content:
Thread Title: 50 Major Achievements Attributed To President Tinubu's Administration Since 2023

Main Post: 50 Major Achievements Attributed to President Tinubu's Administration Since 2023The following is a compilation of 50 achievements attributed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's administration since 2023.1. Fuel Subsidy Elimination: Abolished the decades-long petrol subsidy in May 2023 to save trillions of naira for public investments. The author also credits the policy with addressing longstanding problems in the sector.2. Foreign Exchange Unification: Collapsed multiple FX windows into a market-driven system to stabilise foreign direct investment inflows. The author says this also addressed problems associated with FX round-tripping.3. Debt Burden Reduction: Reduced Nigeria's debt-service-to-revenue ratio from a reported 97% to below 50%.4. Foreign Exchange Debt Clearance: Cleared more than $10 billion in legacy foreign-exchange liabilities to improve investor confidence.5. Increase in External Reserves: Rebuilt Nigeria's external reserves, taking them beyond $42 billion, described as the highest level since 2019.6. Trade Surplus Expansion: Achieved a reported ₦7.46 trillion trade surplus in Q2 2025.7. Manufacturing Export Growth: Recorded a reported 173% increase in manufactured-goods exports through changes to trade-corridor regulations.8. Non-Oil Revenue Growth: Diversified government revenue, with reported non-oil revenue growth of 24.7% in Q1 2025.9. Broader Tax Base: Increased the tax-to-GDP ratio from below 10% to 13.5%, while the author states that the changes did not increase the tax burden on low-income families.10. Higher FAAC Allocations: Increased Federal Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) monthly distributions by 90%, with distributions reaching a reported record of ₦3.007 trillion.11. Stock Market Growth: The NGX All-Share Index increased from approximately 53,000 points to more than 250,000 points during the period cited.12. Tax Reform Bills: Enacted four comprehensive tax bills intended to simplify taxation and modernise national tax administration.13. Net Exporter Milestone: Moved Nigeria's trade position toward becoming a net exporter for consecutive quarters, according to the compilation.14. Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway: Commenced construction of the 700-kilometre coastal highway linking major maritime and economic areas. The author also highlights the Sokoto-Badagry Super Highway and its potential to open up areas such as the Oke-Ogun and Ofiki axis.15. Electricity Sector Reform: Implemented the Electricity Act 2023, allowing states and private-sector participants greater opportunities to generate and distribute electricity.16. Zungeru Hydropower Project: Launched the 700MW Zungeru Hydropower Project to provide additional electricity to the national grid.17. Grid Capacity Expansion: Added an emergency 625 megawatts of electricity to the national grid on May 3, 2024.18. Second Niger Bridge Access Roads: Completed important access roads associated with the Second Niger Bridge to improve connectivity across the Southeast. The author also notes the ongoing rehabilitation of the First Niger Bridge, including CCTV installation.19. Port Modernisation: Upgraded major ports, including Lekki, Apapa, Tin-Can and Onne, to improve their capacity to handle large maritime vessels.20. Port Revenue Growth: Increased reported national port revenue from approximately ₦424 billion in 2023 to ₦893 billion in 2024 through operational and customs improvements.21. Abuja Metro Rail: Completed and commenced commercial operations on the Abuja Light Rail, including an initial period of free passenger rides.22. Railway Infrastructure Protection: Strengthened monitoring and surveillance around railway infrastructure with the aim of improving safety across national rail networks.23. National Road Rehabilitation: Repaired, reconstructed or expanded more than 2,700 kilometres of interstate roads and expressways.24. Abuja Urban Development: Continued major urban-renewal and infrastructure projects in the Federal Capital Territory, including several flyovers and road projects.25. Student Loan Scheme: Established the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to reduce financial barriers to higher education.26. NELFUND Disbursements: Provided tuition and other educational support to more than 1.6 million students, with hundreds of billions of naira channelled to tertiary institutions. The author states that ₦322 billion had been disbursed as of 12 September 2026.27. 3MTT Digital Skills Programme: Launched the 3 Million Technical Talent programme to develop a large pool of digitally skilled Nigerians and strengthen the technology sector.28. Digital Youth Training: Trained and certified more than 100,000 young Nigerians in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and other emerging technologies.29. Consumer Credit Expansion: Activated the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CrediCorp) to expand access to affordable consumer credit for vehicles, household assets and other essential purchases.30. Youth Credit Programme: Launched the #YouthCred initiative for young Nigerians aged 18–39, including NYSC members.31. Creative Economy Development Fund: Established the Creative Economy Development Fund (CEDF) to provide financing and capital support to artists, actors, filmmakers, musicians and other content creators.32. Nigeria Youth Investment Fund: Restructured and expanded the NYIF to provide additional financing and support for young entrepreneurs and businesses.33. National Minimum Wage: Signed a revised National Minimum Wage Act, increasing the federal minimum wage from ₦30,000 to ₦70,000.34. CNG Initiative: Introduced CNG-powered buses and established conversion centres as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs following the removal of the petrol subsidy.35. Conditional Cash Transfers: Expanded social-protection programmes providing direct financial assistance to millions of vulnerable households.36. Primary Healthcare Revitalisation: Strengthened and rehabilitated Primary Health Care centres nationwide through the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund and other interventions.37. Cancer Treatment Infrastructure: Commenced development of oncology treatment centres across Nigeria's geopolitical zones.38. Passport Backlog Reduction: Undertook an emergency intervention to clear a large backlog of pending international passport applications.39. MSME Loans and Grants: Disbursed billions of naira in grants and financial support to hundreds of thousands of micro, small and medium-sized businesses following the removal of the petrol subsidy.40. Agricultural Growth Programmes: Expanded agricultural-support programmes and distributed mechanisation equipment and other inputs to farmers to improve food production.41. Tractor Deployment: Acquired and deployed more than 2,000 agricultural tractors to promote mechanised farming and strengthen agricultural cooperatives.42. Dry-Season Farming Support: Provided financing and agricultural inputs for dry-season wheat, rice and maize production to increase food supply and moderate prices.43. Mining Sector Monitoring: Established specialised monitoring and enforcement arrangements aimed at addressing illegal mining and protecting Nigeria's mineral resources.44. Coal Sector Development: Increased activity and investment in the coal-mining sector, contributing to reported growth in mineral production.45. Local Government Financial Autonomy: Supported the Supreme Court judgment affirming the financial autonomy of Nigeria's local government councils and their direct access to statutory allocations.46. National Security Operations: Intensified military and security operations against terrorism and banditry, with the administration reporting significant reductions in the activities of armed groups and the departure of numerous high-profile members from such groups.47. Surrenders by Insurgent Groups: Continued intelligence-led security operations that contributed to the surrender of thousands of Boko Haram and ISWAP members and their associates.48. Military Personnel Welfare: Implemented salary adjustments and improved allowances and logistical support for members of the armed forces.49. National Identity System Expansion: Expanded National Identification Number (NIN) registration, with more than 118 million Nigerians enrolled in the national identity system.50. Regional Development Commissions: Established new regional development commissions to accelerate development across different parts of the country, alongside institutional changes aimed at strengthening regional development planning. The author notes that the Niger Delta Development Commission was established earlier for the South-South region and that other regions have subsequently received comparable development commissions.Compiled by Ayoade Davidson Ojeniyi FCA — 12 September 2026.Note: The figures and descriptions above represent the author's compilation and assessment of the administration's record. Individual statistics and claims may be subject to further verification and interpretation.

main_content:
Thread Title: "No Political Ambition Worth Sacrificing Your Liberty"-omarana Warns ADC Members

Main Post: ... alleges plot to forge ADC documents, warns of legal actionThe Omarana Campaign Organisation has raised an alarm over an alleged plot by "disgruntled elements" within the African Democratic Congress, ADC, to forge party documents in Adamawa State in a bid to challenge the candidacy of its governorship flagbearer, Amb. Engr. Omar Suleiman.In a press statement issued in Yola, the campaign said it had received "credible intelligence" that some individuals are attempting to manipulate party records at the ADC Secretariat and are allegedly mobilizing party agents and election officials to append signatures to documents they intend to use in legal proceedings.The campaign organisation said the alleged scheme involves efforts to "manufacture, alter or forge party documents" to create a false narrative around the ADC governorship ticket in Adamawa."We consider these allegations extremely serious," the statement read. "We are aware of the activities reportedly taking place around these individuals, and we are carefully documenting relevant information available to us."The campaign further alleged that some of those involved are "accommodated at a hotel within the Area 1, Garki axis of Abuja.""Let it be known that political intrigues carried out in secrecy do not necessarily remain secret. The dark activities being planned and executed will, in due course, come to light," it warned.The Omarana Campaign cautioned party officials, agents and election officials against lending their names or signatures to "questionable documents.""Anyone who knowingly participates in the falsification of documents, presentation of false evidence, forgery, alteration of official records or the making of false statements under oath may expose himself or herself to serious legal consequences under applicable Nigerian laws," it stated."No political ambition is worth sacrificing one's liberty, reputation and future," the statement added, alleging that those who sponsor such schemes "often disappear when the consequences arrive."The campaign said the alleged plot was an attempt to create confusion around the ADC ticket, but insisted it would not derail its focus."Our mandate is bigger than internal political manoeuvring. Omar Suleiman's candidacy represents a commitment to building an Adamawa where government works, institutions work, young people have opportunities," the campaign said.It described the "Omarana Agenda" as centered on competence, development, accountability, inclusion and "an Adamawa That Works."The organisation urged supporters to "remain calm, disciplined and law-abiding" and said disputes should be resolved through "lawful and constitutional channels" rather than violence or intimidation.The statement called on ADC stakeholders to protect the party's credibility and not allow it to become "another victim of the politics of desperation, manipulation and do-or-die ambition.""A political party that seeks to present itself as an alternative must demonstrate integrity not merely in its speeches, but in its conduct," it said.The campaign also called on relevant authorities to take seriously any credible information concerning attempts to falsify political documents."Our destination is not the courtroom for manufactured controversies. Our destination is the people," the statement concluded. "Omarana is coming. For Today. For Tomorrow. Towards an Adamawa That Works."Efforts to get reactions from the ADC State Secretariat and other parties mentioned were ongoing at press time.-

title: 'No Vacancy In Aso Rock For The Next 4 Or 5 Years': Oba Of Lagos Backs Tinubu
main_content:
Thread Title: 'No Vacancy In Aso Rock For The Next 4 Or 5 Years': Oba Of Lagos Backs Tinubu

Main Post: The Oba of Lagos, Rilwan Akiolu, has declared that there is no vacancy in the Presidential Villa for the next four or five years, signalling his support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s bid for a second term in office.Akiolu spoke during a courtesy visit by the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) of the All Progressives Congress (APC), at the Oba Palace, Lagos led by its Director-General, Abdulaziz Yari.The monarch also urged politicians to ensure that the 2027 general election was peaceful and conducted in a manner that would benefit Nigerians.“For the next four or five years, there is no vacancy in Aso Rock,” he said.He urged members of the campaign council to be honest in their dealings and avoid actions capable of undermining peace and stability in the country.The monarch said the forthcoming election should not be approached through the Machiavellian principle that the end justifies the means, stressing the need for responsible political conduct.Yari said the delegation was at the palace as part of its first outing to seek the monarch’s blessing, prayers and advice ahead of its nationwide campaign activities.He said the council had earlier visited the Sokoto Caliphate before proceeding to Lagos to pay homage to the Oba.The DG appealed for continued support for Tinubu, saying members of the council believed the President deserved another term to consolidate what he described as the gains of his administration.According to him, the council was particularly convinced by the administration’s efforts to address economic challenges, insecurity and infrastructure development.He acknowledged that Nigerians were still facing economic difficulties but argued that some indicators showed improvement, particularly in the availability of funds and efforts to stabilise the economy.Yari also defended the administration’s handling of insecurity, saying Tinubu had continued to provide support and equipment for the military and police in the fight against insecurity.He recalled that Tinubu had previously supported the emergence of former President Muhammadu Buhari because of the security challenges confronting the country at the time.Yari said the support for Tinubu was not merely a matter of political reciprocity but was based on the belief that the President should be allowed to continue with his plans for the country.He assured that members of the council from the North would work to ensure that the President’s re-election bid received the necessary support in the region.Receiving the delegation, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu described the visit as significant, noting that the council had chosen to visit the Oba immediately after its engagement in Sokoto.Sanwo-Olu said the delegation was seeking the royal blessing of the Oba before commencing its wider political assignment across the country.He described the members of the council as eminent Nigerians who had served the country in various capacities, including as former governors, a former Senate President, former speakers and serving governors.The Governor said Lagos remained important to the political process, describing the state as both the commercial and economic nerve centre of the country and a major political centre.He said the presence of the council at the palace reflected the importance attached to the traditional institution and its role in the political process.Sanwo-Olu also acknowledged the presence of Lagos APC leaders, local government chairmen, members of the National Assembly and state lawmakers at the event.The visit was attended by other APC leaders and stakeholders in Lagos.[LINK]

Main Post: ... alleges plot to forge ADC documents, warns of legal actionThe Omarana Campaign Organisation has raised an alarm over an alleged plot by "disgruntled elements" within the African Democratic Congress, ADC, to forge party documents in Adamawa State in a bid to challenge the candidacy of its governorship flagbearer, Amb. Engr. Omar Suleiman.In a press statement issued in Yola, the campaign said it had received "credible intelligence" that some individuals are attempting to manipulate party records at the ADC Secretariat and are allegedly mobilizing party agents and election officials to append signatures to documents they intend to use in legal proceedings.The campaign organisation said the alleged scheme involves efforts to "manufacture, alter or forge party documents" to create a false narrative around the ADC governorship ticket in Adamawa."We consider these allegations extremely serious," the statement read. "We are aware of the activities reportedly taking place around these individuals, and we are carefully documenting relevant information available to us."The campaign further alleged that some of those involved are "accommodated at a hotel within the Area 1, Garki axis of Abuja.""Let it be known that political intrigues carried out in secrecy do not necessarily remain secret. The dark activities being planned and executed will, in due course, come to light," it warned.The Omarana Campaign cautioned party officials, agents and election officials against lending their names or signatures to "questionable documents.""Anyone who knowingly participates in the falsification of documents, presentation of false evidence, forgery, alteration of official records or the making of false statements under oath may expose himself or herself to serious legal consequences under applicable Nigerian laws," it stated."No political ambition is worth sacrificing one's liberty, reputation and future," the statement added, alleging that those who sponsor such schemes "often disappear when the consequences arrive."The campaign said the alleged plot was an attempt to create confusion around the ADC ticket, but insisted it would not derail its focus."Our mandate is bigger than internal political manoeuvring. Omar Suleiman's candidacy represents a commitment to building an Adamawa where government works, institutions work, young people have opportunities," the campaign said.It described the "Omarana Agenda" as centered on competence, development, accountability, inclusion and "an Adamawa That Works."The organisation urged supporters to "remain calm, disciplined and law-abiding" and said disputes should be resolved through "lawful and constitutional channels" rather than violence or intimidation.The statement called on ADC stakeholders to protect the party's credibility and not allow it to become "another victim of the politics of desperation, manipulation and do-or-die ambition.""A political party that seeks to present itself as an alternative must demonstrate integrity not merely in its speeches, but in its conduct," it said.The campaign also called on relevant authorities to take seriously any credible information concerning attempts to falsify political documents."Our destination is not the courtroom for manufactured controversies. Our destination is the people," the statement concluded. "Omarana is coming. For Today. For Tomorrow. Towards an Adamawa That Works."Efforts to get reactions from the ADC State Secretariat and other parties mentioned were ongoing at press time.-

title: State Police Constitutional Framework Near Completion - Bayo Onanuga
main_content:
Thread Title: State Police Constitutional Framework Near Completion - Bayo Onanuga

Main Post: STATEHOUSE PRESS RELEASE STATE POLICE CONSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK NEAR COMPLETION- PRESIDENCY Significant progress has been made towards establishing state police, with a constitutional amendment expected soon, following months of consultations among the Executive, the National Assembly and security authorities. The Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed this on Thursday while briefing State House Correspondents after a consultative meeting on state police convened by the Presidency, held at the State House, Abuja. Gbajabiamila said deliberations on the proposed state police framework began several months ago following a directive by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, noting that the process has gained considerable traction. He explained that establishing state police requires careful consideration of constitutional and legal issues and cannot be implemented hastily. "We started deliberations in the last three or four months on how to go about the establishment of state police as directed by Mr President. "Establishing state police is not something that you do with the snap of the fingers. There is a lot involved in terms of constitution and legalities, and thank God we have now gained a lot of traction. “Hopefully, the amendment will come shortly, and the details of the amendment will come after that," Gbajabiamila added. According to him, discussions have now advanced to the point of considering the necessary constitutional amendments, with the enabling legislation to follow afterwards. "Right now, what we are looking at is the constitutional amendment itself, and then the enabling law would follow thereafter. That is what we have been deliberating on in the last couple of hours," he added. The Chief of Staff highlighted broad national support for the initiative, emphasising that the debate is no longer about whether state police should be establishedbut about creating the appropriate legal and institutional framework for its operation. He said President Tinubu, who has consistently advocated for state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria's security architecture, would receive a comprehensive report on the meeting's outcome. The meeting is part of a series of consultations convened by the Federal Government to develop a workable framework for the establishment of state police, an initiative aimed at strengthening internal security, improving local intelligence gathering and enhancing the capacity of sub-national governments to address emerging security challenges across the country. President Tinubu has maintained in the last few months that state police is a necessary response to Nigeria's evolving security challenges, advocating that a decentralised policing structure would strengthen grassroots security, enhance intelligence gathering and improve the protection of lives and property across the country. The meeting was attended by the Deputy President of the Senate, Jibrin Barau, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, the Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi and the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, among other senior government officials.Bayo Onanuga Special Adviser to the President (Information and Strategy) June 04, 2026

title: Who Is Hon. Barr. Juliet Waazor Laba? Why The Lawyer, Governance Professional A
main_content:
Thread Title: Who Is Hon. Barr. Juliet Waazor Laba? Why The Lawyer, Governance Professional A

Main Post: WHO IS HON. BARR. JULIET WAAZOR LABA?Why the Lawyer, Governance Professional and Advocate for Inclusive Leadership Could Be the Voice Khana Constituency II NeedsRESCUE NYO-KHANA 2027Time to Rescue Our Constituency. Time for Effective Representation.In every political season, communities are presented with choices. But beyond political parties, campaign slogans and electoral promises, the fundamental question remains: who is prepared, competent and sufficiently connected to the people to represent their interests effectively?For the people of Khana Constituency II, that question deserves serious consideration as the 2027 general election approaches.One name increasingly demanding attention is Hon. Barr. Juliet Waazor Laba, a legal practitioner, Governance, Risk and Compliance Consultant, public policy advocate and politician whose professional background has been shaped by governance, regulatory compliance, institutional strengthening and community development.But who exactly is Juliet Waazor Laba, and why is her emergence significant to the political conversation in Nyo-Khana?A DAUGHTER OF KHANA WITH A PUBLIC-SERVICE HERITAGEJuliet Waazor Laba, formerly known as Juliet Waazor Korsi, was born into the family of Hon. Letam G. A. Korsi, a former Chairman of Khana Local Government Area and an elder statesman in Rivers State.Her profile describes her as passionate about good governance, community development and inclusive leadership.This background is important, not because political heritage alone qualifies anyone for public office, but because it places her within a tradition of public engagement while her professional career provides a separate foundation upon which her political aspirations can be examined.And that distinction matters.FROM THE LAW TO GOVERNANCEJuliet Waazor Laba is not entering public discourse without professional preparation.She obtained her Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) degree from Igbinedion University, Okada, Edo State, attended the Lagos Campus of the Nigerian Law School, and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 2018.Beyond the courtroom, her professional experience has taken her into the broader world of governance and institutional management.According to her profile, she is a Governance, Risk and Compliance Consultant, legal practitioner and public policy advocate, with more than eight years of professional experience spanning corporate governance, regulatory compliance, enterprise risk management, corporate advisory and institutional strengthening across private and nonprofit sectors.For a legislative office, these are not irrelevant qualifications.A legislature is not merely a place for speeches. It is a place where laws are made, institutions are scrutinised, public policies are debated and the interests of constituents are represented.The ability to understand law, governance, institutions and public policy can therefore be an important asset.THE POLITICAL JOURNEYJuliet's political journey has already tested her resilience.She joined active politics through the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and contested as the ADC candidate for the Rivers State House of Assembly, Khana Constituency II, in the 21 February 2026 bye-election.Her profile states that although the party was excluded from the ballot, she remained engaged with constituents and continued advocating accountable governance and sustainable development. She is currently the ADC candidate for Khana Constituency II for the 2027 general election.That experience presents an important political lesson: elections are not only about what happens on the ballot paper. They are also about the relationship a prospective representative builds with the people before, during and after an electoral contest.WHAT DOES JULIET WAAZOR LABA STAND FOR?Her stated public-service agenda is anchored on issues that directly touch the future of the constituency:- Transparent governance- Youth and women empowerment- Quality education- Environmental sustainability- Economic development- Effective legislative representationThese are not merely campaign vocabulary.For Khana Constituency II, the real test will be whether such broad objectives can be translated into practical legislative priorities and measurable outcomes.Her profile further states that through mentorship, leadership development and community engagement, she has empowered and mentored young people and women, helping them develop knowledge, confidence and opportunities to reach their potential.That emphasis on people is particularly important in a constituency where the future of young people, the participation of women and the strength of local communities must remain central to any meaningful development agenda.WHY “RESCUE NYO-KHANA”?The slogan “RESCUE NYO-KHANA 2027 — Time to Rescue Our Constituency. Time for Effective Representation” is, at its heart, a call for voters to examine what kind of representation they want.“Rescue” in this context should not be understood as a declaration that one individual can solve every problem confronting a constituency.Rather, it should represent a political commitment to renewed attention, stronger advocacy, responsible representation and a closer relationship between the legislature and the people.The House of Assembly representative is not a governor, commissioner or local government chairman. The office has specific constitutional responsibilities.Therefore, effective representation should be measured by the ability to make and scrutinise laws, participate meaningfully in legislative debates, raise constituency concerns, advocate for development and maintain a functional relationship with constituents.This is where Juliet's legal and governance background becomes part of the argument for her candidacy.A LAWYER IN THE LEGISLATUREA lawyer in the legislature is not automatically a better legislator.But legal training can provide useful tools for legislative work—particularly in understanding statutory provisions, interpreting legal frameworks, examining policies and participating in the law-making process.Juliet's professional experience in governance, risk, compliance and institutional strengthening adds another dimension.If properly deployed, those skills could help her approach legislative representation with an emphasis on accountability, institutional responsibility and policy outcomes.That is the promise voters should examine.Not personality alone.Not political noise.Not empty slogans.But capacity, character, ideas and the willingness to serve.THE CASE FOR A NEW CONVERSATION IN KHANA CONSTITUENCY IIThe 2027 election provides an opportunity for constituents to ask fundamental questions.What kind of representative do we want?Someone who is accessible?Someone who understands the law?Someone who can engage institutions?Someone who can articulate the concerns of women and young people?Someone who understands community development?Someone who can distinguish between political patronage and genuine representation?These are the questions that should guide the conversation.And on the basis of the profile available, Hon. Barr. Juliet Waazor Laba brings a combination of legal training, governance experience, public-policy advocacy and political commitment that deserves serious consideration.THE ROAD TO 2027Politics is ultimately about service.The people of Khana Constituency II deserve a representative who understands that a legislative mandate is not a personal trophy but a public trust.Juliet Waazor Laba's stated commitment to transparent governance, empowerment, education, environmental sustainability, economic development and effective legislative representation provides the framework upon which her candidacy can be judged.But the ultimate judgment belongs to the people.They will determine whether her professional background, political experience, policy agenda and commitment to community engagement amount to the kind of representation they want in the Rivers State House of Assembly.For supporters of the RESCUE NYO-KHANA 2027 movement, however, the message is straightforward:It is time to place representation under scrutiny.It is time to demand competence.It is time to demand accountability.It is time to demand accessibility.It is time to demand a stronger legislative voice.And above all, it is time for the people to recognise that the power of democracy ultimately rests with them.HON. BARR. JULIET WAAZOR LABA: A CANDIDATE TO WATCHWhether 2027 becomes the defining political moment for Juliet Waazor Laba will ultimately be determined at the ballot box.But one thing is already clear: she has entered the conversation with a professional profile built around law, governance, compliance, public policy and community development, and a stated agenda focused on the welfare and prosperity of Khana Constituency II and Rivers State.The responsibility now is for her to continue taking that message to the people, listening to their concerns, presenting practical solutions and earning their confidence.For those who believe Khana Constituency II requires a renewed approach to representation, RESCUE NYO-KHANA 2027 offers a simple proposition:TIME TO RESCUE OUR CONSTITUENCY.TIME FOR EFFECTIVE REPRESENTATION.The people will decide.RESCUE NYO-KHANA 2027. NyoKhana Voice Must be heard comes 2027.I am Distinguished Comrade Nubor Optimist Goteh, a dependable Member of RESCUE NYO-KHANA 2027.

title: Mrs. Obi Vs Mrs. Buhari: The Hermès Bag Controversy And Selective Accountability
main_content:
Thread Title: Mrs. Obi Vs Mrs. Buhari: The Hermès Bag Controversy And Selective Accountability

Main Post: In 2016, we published and criticised reports that then-First Lady Aisha Buhari carried a crocodile-skin Hermès bag allegedly worth millions of naira. The post generated public discussion, but we were not subjected to the level of insults and personal attacks that increasingly characterise political conversations today.Recently, we raised a similar question about a crocodile-skin Hermès bag reportedly carried by Mrs. Margaret Obi. Instead of responding with facts or reasonable arguments, some of Peter Obi’s supporters attacked us with uncouth and unprintable comments.This raises an important question: should accountability depend on the political affiliation of the person involved?If it was legitimate to question the lifestyle of President Muhammadu Buhari’s family, it must also be legitimate to scrutinise the lifestyle of Peter Obi’s family. We cannot demand transparency from our political opponents while treating questions about our preferred candidates as insults or propaganda.Accountability must be based on principles, not personalities. No politician, political spouse or public figure should be placed above legitimate public scrutiny. Supporters are free to dispute a report, challenge its authenticity or provide evidence showing that a claim is false. What they should not do is attempt to silence questions through abuse, intimidation and personal attacks.The conduct of those surrounding a leader matters. A president cannot be everywhere or personally supervise every activity within an administration. He must depend on his family, aides, ministers, advisers and political associates. If those close to him display wastefulness, abuse influence or lack financial discipline, their conduct can undermine his credibility and affect public confidence in his government.This does not mean that every personal possession belonging to a politician’s spouse was purchased with public money. Such a conclusion requires credible evidence. However, citizens and the media still have the right to ask reasonable questions, especially when political leaders build their reputations around modesty, prudence and responsible management of public resources.Peter Obi has presented himself as a frugal leader who opposes waste and unnecessary luxury in government. It is therefore unsurprising that the public may examine whether the conduct and lifestyle of those around him reflect the values he promotes. The proper response is clarification—not insults.Toxic political loyalty is dangerous because it gradually turns supporters into defenders of everything associated with their preferred candidate. They condemn an action when it involves an opponent but excuse the same conduct when it involves their political camp. That is not accountability; it is hypocrisy.Nigeria will not progress if every politician is surrounded by supporters who attack anyone asking difficult questions. Leaders need supporters who can defend them with facts and also correct them when necessary. Blind loyalty weakens democratic accountability and eventually damages the leader it seeks to protect.Those who criticised Mrs. Buhari’s reported luxury bag in 2016 should not be afraid to raise similar questions about Mrs. Obi today. The same standard must apply to Buhari, Tinubu, Atiku, Obi and every other political leader.Public accountability cannot be selective. If our principles change according to the politician involved, then they were never principles in the first place.Source: Ralph E. Odua (Raf Politico), as published by Masses Mandate Movement on Facebook, September 2026. Rewritten and edited for forum suitability; the views and claims remain those of the original author.

Main Post: Ambassador Reno Omokri has claimed that the rapid expansion of public rail infrastructure in Lagos directly triggered Uber's decision to exit the Nigerian market. Speaking on Channels Television, Omokri argued that new transport options cut deep into the ride-hailing company’s profits. He said the success of the Lagos Blue Line and Red Line trains gives people a much cheaper way to travel. According to Omokri, these new train lines dropped Uber's profit margins and forced the company out. In his words“Do you know why Uber left Nigeria? The business model Uber has is that they come into your country and bring about mass low ticket transportation so that they price out the regular taxis. This is what they have done successfully in several countries including the US and the UK. They tried that in this country and it was succeeding, but look at what was happening in Lagos. The infrastructural developments in Lagos has been so wide, so extensive that it is now possible for you to get from point A to Point B at the fraction of the cost using the Blue line, Red line and soon the green line is coming up also. In Abuja, you get from this your station to the airport by rail.So, Uber could not compete because of the advancement of infrastructure in Nigeria” This comes after Uber announced it is leaving Nigeria after 12 years of business. The company said the decision came after a review of its business operations but did not give specific reasons for the exit.[LINK]

title: Ekiti Origin Controversy: Hunye Welcomes Senator Adeola’s Lawsuit Threat, Says C
main_content:
Thread Title: Ekiti Origin Controversy: Hunye Welcomes Senator Adeola’s Lawsuit Threat, Says C

Main Post: Ekiti Origin Controversy: Hunye Welcomes Senator Adeola’s Lawsuit Threat, Says Courtroom is Arena of TruthABEOKUTA — The political temperature in Ogun State escalated significantly today as Hon. Abayomi Hunye pushed back against legal threats issued by Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola (APC, Ogun West), welcoming an imminent court battle over the Senator’s ancestral roots.The Spark: 24-Hour UltimatumThe face-off follows national television appearances by Hunye and former PDP chieftain Ambassador Folake Marcus-Bello, during which both figures publicly questioned Senator Adeola’s Ogun State indigeneship, alleging an Ekiti State lineage instead.In response, Senator Adeola—speaking through his Media Adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro—issued a 24-hour ultimatum demanding verifiable documentary proof of the claims or face immediate lawsuits for criminal defamation and libel. Adeola's camp characterized the statements as recycled, politically motivated slurs aimed at undermining his standing ahead of future political cycles."Courtroom, Not Media Gimmicks"Countering the ultimatum through a formal press statement signed by his Media Adviser, Femi Oyewale, Hunye dismissed the legal threat as a "media gimmick" and an attempt to silence opposition voices in Ogun West."We want to state categorically that we welcome the threat of a lawsuit with open arms. We are more than ready to meet Senator Adeola in a court of competent jurisdiction. Truth is an absolute defence against libel... The courtroom is where evidence is tested, not the pages of newspapers or sponsored broadcast interviews."— Femi Oyewale, Media Adviser to Hon. Abayomi HunyeHunye maintained that a public officer's state of origin is a constitutional matter directly impacting democratic integrity and representation. He assured supporters that his legal team is prepared to present documentary evidence regarding the Senator's background once formal proceedings commence.

title: A Good Outcome Can Hide A Bad Investment Process
main_content:
Thread Title: A Good Outcome Can Hide A Bad Investment Process

Main Post: A junior analyst recommends a position with weak supporting evidence. The trade works, the desk makes money, and the analyst receives praise. A colleague rejects a similar opportunity after careful research, only to watch the price rise without them.Who made the better decision?If we judge only the immediate outcome, the answer appears obvious. If we care about repeatability, risk and long-term performance, it becomes much less comfortable.This distinction shaped my analysis of Expedition Investment Management PTE LTD. I did not want to create another review built around an unverifiable deposit or a conveniently successful withdrawal. I used a professional sequence instead: establish expectations, test them against primary information and define only the conclusions supported by the evidence.Expectation: regulation should answer every questionMy original assumption was that confirming a regulatory record would settle the matter. Find the legal entity in an official directory, check its status and move on.That method is no longer sufficient.Corporate names, registration numbers and licence details are publicly accessible. A third party can reproduce them on a website, presentation or account-opening document. The information may be accurate while the party presenting it remains unrelated to the regulated entity.A useful due-diligence process must therefore connect four elements:the exact legal entity;the regulated activity;the official communication channel;the service actually being proposed.If one element does not match, the strength of the others cannot repair the gap.The evidence hierarchy mattersFor my Expedition Investment Management PTE LTD analysis, I began with the Monetary Authority of Singapore Financial Institutions Directory. The directory records the company as a Capital Markets Services Licensee for fund management.This is strong primary evidence regarding the legal entity and its regulatory status. It does not, however, authenticate every online platform using the company’s name.I then examined the business model described through the company’s official materials. Expedition presents itself as a Singapore-based quantitative investment manager managing private funds for institutional and accredited investors. Participation involves formal onboarding and subscription documentation.That description is materially different from the model of a public retail broker. The company says it does not operate a retail trading portal or mobile application and does not raise money from the general public.This clarification improved my assessment because the stated activity, target investor category and regulatory context were logically consistent.Process quality versus outcome qualityInvestment professionals understand that a profitable result does not validate every step that preceded it. The same logic should apply to corporate research.An online reviewer may claim that a payment arrived quickly. Even if the story is genuine, it does not independently establish the identity of the recipient, the regulatory protection available or the sustainability of the arrangement.A better process separates three questions:Was the organisation correctly identified?Was the decision reasonable given the information available?What outcome occurred after the decision?Combining these questions creates hindsight bias. A favourable result can make weak due diligence appear intelligent, while an unfavourable market movement can make a disciplined decision look foolish.This is one reason Why Consistency Is Becoming More Valuable Than Market Predictions. Predictions attract attention, but processes determine whether results can be repeated without uncontrolled exposure.The most useful finding was operational clarityExpedition Investment Management PTE LTD has published a detailed notice explaining how its identity should be verified. It identifies expeditioninvestment.com as its only official website and states that its authorised email addresses use the [USERNAME]-funds.com domain.The company also specifies activities and requests that do not originate from it. According to the notice, it does not:solicit investments through messaging applications or social media;promise guaranteed or unusually high returns;request transfers to accounts held in an individual’s name;demand taxes or commissions to release funds;ask for passwords, banking credentials or one-time codes;direct prospective investors to download a trading application.This is a positive feature because it converts a general risk warning into a usable control framework. Readers do not need to interpret vague corporate language. They can compare a communication, domain or request with a defined list.In institutional due diligence, clarity about exclusions can be as valuable as disclosure of capabilities. Knowing what a firm does not do helps identify proposals that fall outside its operating model.Result: a positive but limited assessmentThe verification process produced a favourable conclusion within appropriate boundaries.The company has an identifiable MAS directory entry. Its stated private-fund activity is consistent with a restricted institutional and accredited-investor audience. Its official materials clearly distinguish the company from public retail trading services and unauthorised channels.I did not test an investment, assess portfolio performance or interact with the firm as a client. I therefore make no claims regarding returns, execution, withdrawals or relationship management.The positive assessment concerns transparency. The company provides sufficiently precise information for an independent researcher to test whether a website, communication channel or proposed service is consistent with its published operating model.That is not the same as concluding that an investment is suitable. Regulatory status confirms oversight of specified activities; it does not remove market risk, guarantee performance or replace product-level due diligence.A practical framework for analystsMy preferred decision-making process in investing now includes six identity controls before any performance analysis:Locate the entity in the regulator’s database.Confirm the exact scope of the regulated activity.Identify the official website independently.Verify the individual representative where possible.Compare the proposed product with the documented business model.Confirm the legal recipient before transferring funds.Only after these controls should analysis move to strategy, liquidity, fees, valuation, operational risk and expected return.The order matters. There is little value in constructing a sophisticated return model for an opportunity whose identity has not been established.Final takeawayMy expectation was that a regulatory entry would provide the answer. The verification stage showed that it provides only one part of the answer. The result was a more disciplined and ultimately more positive view based on consistency between the legal entity, regulated activity, investor category and official communication rules.The broader lesson extends beyond one company. Strong analysis is not designed to produce a preferred verdict. It is designed to produce a verdict that another professional can reproduce using the same evidence.In markets, luck can reward weak decisions for a while. A documented process is what keeps the next decision from depending on luck again.

title: Arabambi sues UNN over Peter Obi's academic records
main_content:
Thread Title: Arabambi sues UNN over Peter Obi's academic records

Main Post: UNN sued over Peter Obi’s academic recordsPeter ObiA Labour Party (LP) chieftain, Abayomi Arabambi, has sued the University of Nigeria Nsukka (UNN) over the alleged refusal to release details of the academic record of Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC).Arabambi, in a fresh suit, said he had requested a certified true copy (CTC) of Obi’s certificate number D000198 in respect of a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy issued in 1984 in line with the Freedom of Information Act, but the institution turned down his demand.In the originating motion marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2144/2026 and filed by his lawyer, Anderson Asemota, on Sept. 9 at the Federal High Court in Abuja, said letters had been written to the university.The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that in the court documents made available on Saturday, the applicant, a former factional spokesperson for LP, named the VC and UNN as 1st and 2nd respondents.He is, therefore, seeking an order of mandamus compelling the respondents to perform their statutory duty under the FoI Act, 2011, by determining and responding to his request dated July 16 in accordance with the provisions of the Act.According to Arabambi in the affidavit setting out the facts, by a letter dated 16th July, 2026, the applicant requested a CTC of Certificate No. D000198, stated to have been issued by the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to Gregory Peter Onwubuasi Obi in respect of a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Philosophy in 1984.“The applicant also requested a Certified True Copy of the certificate, academic record or other official records upon which the said degree was predicated.“The said request was duly delivered to and received by the respondents on 6th August, 2026.“The applicant expressly made the request pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, and stated the public-interest and accountability basis for the request.“The respondents failed and/or neglected to provide the requested information within the period prescribed by the Act,” he said.Arabambi stated that the respondents did not communicate to him a written notice of refusal identifying the specific provision of the Act relied upon for refusing access.“The applicant consequently sent a reminder letter dated 31st August, 2026, reiterating the original request and again demanding the requested records.“The reminder letter was delivered to and received by the respondents on 1st September, 2026, as evidenced by the delivery receipt,” he said.Arabambi, in the affidavit deposed to by Chuku Maudlyn, a litigation secretary in the law firm of Messrs Neplus Ultra Attorneys, averred that the delivery receipt identified the receiver as the VC and the destination as the UNN.“As at the commencement of this action, the respondents have neither supplied the requested records nor issued a lawful written notice of refusal,” he said.The applicant, therefore, sought 19 reliefs.He prayed the court for a declaration that his written request made pursuant to the FoI Act, 2011, “constitutes a valid request for information within the contemplation of the Freedom of Information Act.”He sought an order of mandamus compelling the respondents to furnish him with a CTC of certificate number D000198 issued by the university if the said certificate exists in the custody, possession or control of the respondents.Arabambi also sought an order of mandamus compelling them to furnish him with the CTC of the existing official academic and institutional records relating to the said degree and the certificate, including where they exist and are within the custody or control of the respondents.He listed the documents he sought as relevant academic records, relevant graduation/degree-award records, relevant certificate-register entries, relevant Senate or academic approval award records, and any other existing official records upon which the said degree and/or certificate was based, among other reliefs.Giving grounds for his application, Arabambi submitted that as an applicant, he has a statutory right of access to information in the custody of a public institution.According to him, the respondents are subject to the Freedom of Information Act.He said the requested information concerns a certificate expressly represented to have been issued by the UNN.He says the respondents are consequently the institution whose official records are directly relevant to his request.Arabambi said Section 4 of the Act imposes a statutory duty to respond within the prescribed period, and that they had failed to comply with that duty.“The respondents did not communicate a lawful refusal identifying any applicable exemption.“The failure therefore constitutes a refusal and/or deemed refusal under the Act,” he concluded.NAN reports that at the centre of the applicant’s complaint is what he described as multiple variations of Obi’s name across documents submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and educational authorities.The case is yet to be assigned to a judge.[LINK]

title: Nassarawa 2027: APC Announces Ombudagu As Deputy Gov Shp Candidate
main_content:
Thread Title: Nassarawa 2027: APC Announces Ombudagu As Deputy Gov Shp Candidate

Main Post: LAFIA — Governor Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa State has announced Emmanuel Michael Ombugadu as the deputy governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state ahead of the 2027 general election.Sule announced the decision after an APC stakeholders’ meeting held at the Governor’s Lodge in Abuja on Monday.He said the aspirants had agreed to support whoever emerged, in line with the approach adopted by the party in selecting its governorship candidate.“We had a couple of people eminently qualified, and every one of them made a decision similar to what we did with the gubernatorial election, that whoever is selected among them, they would all rally and support that person.“So at the end of the decision, it was agreed that Honourable Emmanuel Ombugadu will be our deputy gubernatorial candidate of the party,” Sule said.The governor commended party stakeholders for attending the meeting despite the short notice, explaining that the venue was moved to Abuja because of his official engagements, including the North Central Development Commission summit where he served as Chief Host.He also cited his scheduled departure for the United Nations General Assembly session in New York.Sule urged APC members to remain united ahead of the 2027 general election, stressing the need for the party to approach the polls as a united force.“We cannot go into these elections divided. That is the reason we invited this meeting, so that we can keep together, make a decision together, and go together,” he said.Also speaking, the APC governorship candidate, Senator Ahmed Aliyu Wadada, expressed satisfaction with the choice of Ombugadu as his running mate, saying the decision reflected the position of the party leadership and zoning considerations.“I feel happy, I feel committed, and of course fulfilled to have him as my deputy gubernatorial candidate, because it is the decision of the party and the leadership,” Wadada said.He appealed to other aspirants who had sought the position to accept the outcome in the interest of party unity.“I call on all others too, particularly my brother Dr Kigbu, who everybody thought would get it, to accept this as the will of God. Together we shall weather the storm,” he said.In his response, Ombugadu thanked Sule and other party stakeholders for the confidence reposed in him, describing the decision as difficult but necessary for the cohesion of the party.“I feel highly elated, and I take it as the will of God for me to be in this capacity. I thank the Governor and all the stakeholders of the state for this very critical decision,” he said.Ombugadu acknowledged that some of his colleagues who also aspired to be selected had been aggrieved by the outcome, but said they had pledged their loyalty to the party.

title: Abuah Rallies Igbuzo Youths For Door-to-door Campaign, Backs APC Victory In 2027
main_content:
Thread Title: Abuah Rallies Igbuzo Youths For Door-to-door Campaign, Backs APC Victory In 2027

Main Post: By NewsbreezeThe Senior Special Assistant (SSA) to the Governor of Delta State on Youth Mobilisation, Chief Lucky Blessing Odiakachukwu Abuah, has called on youths in Igbuzo to begin an aggressive grassroots campaign in support of all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.Chief Abuah made the call while addressing youth executives drawn from various wards in Igbuzo during a strategic meeting held at his residence.Speaking to the gathering, the yogʻuth mobilization leader described Governor Sheriff Oborevwori as "the best thing that has happened to Delta State in recent times," citing the governor's developmental strides, people-oriented policies, and commitment to improving the welfare of Deltans through the MORE Agenda.According to him, the achievements recorded by the Oborevwori administration have laid a solid foundation for sustainable growth and development across the state, stressing that continuity remains critical to consolidating the gains already achieved.He urged the youths to immediately commence a door-to-door campaign across communities, emphasizing the need to mobilize support for APC candidates at all levels in the forthcoming elections.The task before us is to take the message of good governance to every household. We must work together to ensure victory for our party from the Presidency to the Governorship, Senate, House of Representatives, and the State House of Assembly. Delta State and Nigeria need continuity, stability, and progressive leadership, he stated.Chief Abuah assured the youths of his unwavering commitment to the mobilization exercise, promising to provide the necessary logistics, support structures, and manpower required to ensure the success of the campaign.The SSA further disclosed plans to launch another round of personal empowerment programmes aimed at uplifting people at the grassroots level. He noted that community empowerment has remained a major focus of his philanthropic activities long before his appointment into public office.He explained that through his Lucky Abuah foundation, he has consistently supported vulnerable persons, youths, women, and small-scale entrepreneurs across various communities, adding that the forthcoming empowerment initiative would further complement government efforts in improving the living standards of the people.Chief Abuah urged the youths to remain united, peaceful, and focused on constructive engagement, assuring them that greater opportunities await those who participate actively in community development and political mobilization.The meeting ended with a renewed commitment by the youth leaders to intensify grassroots sensitization and mobilization efforts in support of APC candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Democracy Is More Than Elections — It Is A Way Of Life
main_content:
Thread Title: Democracy Is More Than Elections — It Is A Way Of Life

Main Post: Today, as the world marks the International Day of Democracy, the Peace and Social Advancement Centre (PSAC) joins citizens and institutions across the world in reaffirming the values of participation, accountability, inclusion, justice and respect for human dignity upon which democratic societies must stand.Democracy is not sustained by elections alone. It is sustained by institutions that serve the people, leaders who are accountable to the people, citizens who participate responsibly, and a society where diverse voices can be heard without fear.For Nigeria, democracy must continually translate into good governance, responsive leadership, credible institutions, social justice and meaningful opportunities for citizens to participate in decisions that affect their lives.At PSAC, we believe that peace and democratic governance are inseparable. Where citizens feel excluded, institutions lose legitimacy; where dialogue is replaced by intolerance, social cohesion weakens; and where accountability is absent, public trust suffers.This year's observance therefore reminds us that democracy must not only be defended—it must be deepened.Let us build a democratic culture where we listen before we condemn, engage before we confront, participate beyond election day, and hold power accountable through lawful and peaceful civic action.Democracy belongs to all of us. Its strength depends on what we collectively make of it.Happy International Day of Democracy 2026.Peace and Social Advancement Centre (PSAC)Uniting Voices, Advancing Peace.#InternationalDayOfDemocracy #DemocracyDay #DemocraticGovernance #GoodGovernance #Peacebuilding #CivicEngagement #SocialCohesion #PSAC #UnitingVoicesAdvancingPeace

Main Post: U.S COMMENDS NIGERIA ON REMOVAL OF 12-YEAR CONDITION OF ENTRY The United States Government has commended Nigeria for its sustained maritime security reforms, which led to the lifting of the 12-year Condition of Entry imposed on vessels visiting the United States from Nigeria, saying the development will deliver tangible benefits to shipping operators, reduce shipping costs and strengthen trade between the two countries. In a letter addressed to the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, the U.S.Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, Frank Garcia Jr., congratulates Nigeria on the milestone, describing it as evidence of the country’s “sustained strengthening of port security and anti-terrorism compliance.” He says The United States values its maritime and economic partnerships with Nigeria and looks forward to continued collaboration in promoting secure, efficient, and mutually beneficial trade between our nations.Speaking on the development, Minister of Marine and Economy, credited President Bola Tinubu’s leadership and strategic support for the milestone, particularly the administration’s decision to prioritise the marine and blue economy as a key pillar of Nigeria’s economic transformation agenda.The letter provides a fresh endorsement from Washington following the United States Coast Guard’s decision, announced in August, to lift the long-standing security restriction on vessels arriving in the United States from Nigeria.[LINK]

title: ASUU Declares Indefinite Strike In LASU, Other Lagos Varsities
main_content:
Thread Title: ASUU Declares Indefinite Strike In LASU, Other Lagos Varsities

Main Post: The Academic Staff Union of Universities, Lagos State Government-owned Universities Joint Campus Group, on Tuesday declared a total and indefinite strike across the three state-owned universities in the state.The affected institutions are the Lagos State University, Lagos State University of Education and Lagos State University of Science and Technology.The union said the strike followed the expiration of the 14-day ultimatum issued to the state government on August 31, 2026, without a satisfactory resolution or concrete plan from the government.The declaration was contained in a statement signed by the Coordinator, Steering Committee, ASUU-LASU, Olusegun Babalola; Acting Chairman, ASUU-LASUED, Grace Abimbola; and Chairman, ASUU-LASUSTECH,Murisiku OnigemoThe union claimed that the action was because the state government allowed the September 13 deadline to lapse without initiating dialogue, despite its final warning on September 10 that “silence is no longer an option.”It said its principal demand remained the “full domestication and implementation of the December 2025 ASUU-FGN Agreement across all Lagos State-owned universities.”According to the union, the demand includes the implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and critical welfare provisions for serving and retired academic staff.The statement read, “Following the expiration of the 14-day ultimatum issued to the Lagos State Government on 31 August 2026, the Academic Staff Union of Universities Joint Campus Group—comprising Lagos State University, Lagos State University of Education, and Lagos State University of Science and Technology—hereby declares a total, comprehensive and indefinite strike action effective immediately.”ASUU said the strike would remain in force until meaningful engagement produced a satisfactory resolution and the state government signed, domesticated and implemented the applicable provisions of the 2025 agreement in full.“The Union remains entirely committed to constructive dialogue and to the swift restoration of normal academic activities as soon as these outstanding issues are addressed,” it added.ASUU said it took the action with a “heavy heart,” urging students and parents to remain calm, peaceful and law-abiding while efforts were made to secure a permanent resolution.It described the action as a “rescue mission for Lagos State education.”The union further said the strike had the full backing of the ASUU national leadership, adding that the national body had supported the steps taken by the branches, from letters to university administrations, governing councils and the state’sVisitors, to the issuance of the 14-day ultimatum.It also called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, alumni associations, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to support its demand.The Lagos State-owned universities join some other universities that have embarked on strikes, demanding that their state governments commit to implementing the 2025 FGN/ASUU agreement.

Dear op, if it were the Navy or Air Force, I could have told you to go ahead. I also left university many years ago in my fourth year. Though at the time, I joined through the Officer Cadet route I meant the Defence Academy. So, my advice to you is this. The Army is not even like the Navy or the Air Force. They recruit, advertise, and enlist people to join. So don't expect any fireworks or assume that everything will work out in your favour when things don't go your way.Of course, we have people who go on courses to study nursing, for example. One of my godsons, who was a corporal, recently went on a nursing course in Lagos, at the Nigerian Army School of Nursing, and today he is a nurse. He is anticipating doing a Short Service Commission to become a commissioned officer. But the chances are slim, like I told him, because we have nurses who even have MSc and are still serving in the ranks. I remember I had an instructor when I was a cadet in G-branch who had a PhD but was still Warrant Officer.So, I advise you to finish your degree. But if you have the opportunity to join the Navy or the Air Force, I can advise you to go for it. That is where I believe you may have better opportunities.In the Navy and Air Force, as long as you are willing to go to school and you have a good rapport with your superiors, especially your direct Commanding Officer, there may be opportunities for you to progress, go to school, and improve yourself, including the possibility of getting commissioned.Though branch commissioning in the Air Force is very difficult to get, even harder than getting EC in the army. But still, if it is the Navy or Air Force, I would advise you to consider it.One thing I have noticed about the Air Force is that whenever I go to the base to see some of my coursemates, many of these Air Force personnel have master's degrees and even PhDs, and they are still serving as soldiers.So, if it is the Air Force or Navy you want to join, I could tell you to go ahead, but make sure you continue developing yourself academically. Develop a good rapport with your superiors and conduct yourself properly.You can even put in your papers along the line if you eventually decide that you no longer want the job. People leave the service after some time because they are no longer interested. So, that's my advice for you. if it is the Army, reconsider your options. stretch yourself, You are studying a good course.But if it is the Navy or Air Force you want to join, I could advise you to go ahead. Develop a good rapport with your superiors, especially your commander. Wherever ship you are posted to if you are in the Navy, develop yourself and maintain a good relationship with your superiors.And if you are in the Air Force, wherever you are posted, do the same. As long as you are not in the Regiment, because if you are in the Regiment in the Air Force, it might be more difficult for you to go to school because of operations and many other responsibilities.That's my advice.Pray for direction from God in all. All you need to do is ask him for wisdom and he will show you the way. Goodluck with your choices. If you eventually join the army, try and reach out still. I believe airforce form is currently in sale though.
