title: Affordable UK Universities Nobody Is Talking About !!️
main_content:
Thread Title: Affordable UK Universities Nobody Is Talking About !!️

Main Post: Omo, let’s burst a major myth on this forum today. If you mention "UK Master's degree" in any gathering in Nigeria right now, the first thing people will tell you is: "Forget it, you need at least ₦30 million to ₦40 million to start." Because of this, many brilliant guys have completely folded their arms and killed their dreams.But here is the open secret: while the big-name universities in London will happily drain your life savings, there are still strategic, low-cost options where you can pull off a UK Master's with proper planning. But hold on! "Affordable" in the UK doesn't mean it's a charity organization. If you choose the wrong school just because it's cheap, you will end up with a useless degree, stranded in a town with zero jobs. Let’s look at the actual schools, the real costs, and the hidden traps nobody tells you about.The Affordable List: 10 Universities To Research Right NowBefore you look at these prices, remember that many of these schools offer international scholarships or regional fee reductions (ranging from £1,000 to £3,000) that pull the initial price tag even lower. 1. Teesside University 🇬🇧* The Gist: One of the absolute cheapest options. Fees can range from £10,000 to £17,000 depending on the course. Scholarship:[b] £2000[b] Payment plan:[b] 3 installments * [b]The Catch: Located in Middlesbrough. It’s a smaller town, so you have to hustle harder for part-time student jobs.2. University of Salford Manchester 🇬🇧* The Gist: Fees sit around £12,000 to £18,000. Deposit:[b] £5000[b]Payment plan:[b] 7- 10 installments * [b]The Advantage: It is right next to Manchester! This means you get affordable tuition but enjoy access to a massive city with a booming job market.3. University of Sunderland 🇬🇧* The Gist: Tuition is approximately £12,500 to £18,000. They have a campus in Sunderland and another in London. Scholarship:[b] £1500 - £4500[b]Payment plan:[b] 3 - 7 installments * [b]The Warning: If you choose their London campus, remember your cost of living will double automatically.4. University of Bolton 🇬🇧* The Gist: Highly popular among budget-conscious international students looking for lower-cost postgraduate routes. Close to the Greater Manchester area.5. University of Chester 🇬🇧* The Gist: Known for steady international discounts and flexible internal payment structures that give sponsors room to breathe.6. Arden University 🇬🇧* The Gist: Fees are around £17,500, but they offer highly flexible blended learning and modern payment structures. 7. Regent College London 🇬🇧* The Gist: Around £17,500. A flexible option based right in the heart of London for those who want immediate access to big city opportunities.8. University of Cumbria 🇬🇧* The Gist: Located in a beautiful, lower-cost region of the UK. Excellent for students who want peace of mind and cheap rent.9. University of East London (UEL) 🇬🇧* The Gist: A London-based option that frequently structures affordable payment plans for African postgraduate students.10. Leeds Trinity University 🇬🇧* The Gist: Offers a smaller, highly supportive university environment with relatively lower international tuition baselines.The Ugly Truth: The "Cheap Tuition" TrapBefore you rush to apply to the cheapest school on this list, you must understand how the system can play you. A cheaper university that does not support your long-term goals is an expensive mistake. * The Location vs. Job War: If a school charges £11,000 but is located in a remote area with zero businesses, how will you secure a professional job during your 2-year Graduate Route post-study visa? You might save money on tuition but lose heavily on career growth.* The CAS Deposit Pressure: Some affordable schools will give you an offer letter easily but will demand that you pay 50% of the tuition upfront before they issue your CAS (Visa letter). * The Strict Payment Plan Warning: Do not assume "flexible payment" means you can pay whenever you like. If you miss a school installment deadline while in the UK, they will block your student portal, prevent you from submitting assignments, and eventually report you to the Home Office.5 Rules to Check Before Paying Any Deposit:1. Official Recognition: Is the university fully recognized for your specific professional field (e.g., ACCA, RIBA, BCS)?2. The Real Total Cost: Have you added accommodation, flight, visa, and the heavy IHS medical fee to the tuition?3. Scholarship Terms: Is the scholarship automatic, or do you need to maintain a specific grade to keep it?4. The Rent Reality: Is on-campus accommodation available, or will you be thrown into the expensive private rental market?5. Graduate Outcomes: Do graduates from this specific school actually get employed, or is the certificate ignored by top employers?Who are these affordable options suitable for?* Students who have a strict mid-tier budget and want a recognized UK master's degree without drowning in generational debt.* Independent hustlers who understand they need to study hard while managing their living expectations.Who should avoid them?* People who think "cheap" means they can skip classes to work full-time illegally. The UK monitors attendance aggressively now.* Anyone looking for an automatic, luxury ride into corporate UK without doing heavy local networking.Let’s Map Out Your RouteDon't let the ₦30 million scarecrow stop you from exploring your options, but don't let desperation make you enter a blind trap either. What UK Master's program or specific course are you currently considering? Drop the course name and your realistic target budget below. Let’s look at which of these universities actually fits your profile and career goals perfectly!Let’s discuss!

Your course, location, academic background, family situation, available funds and even the timing can change what makes sense.That's why I don't really like giving people a blanket list of “cheapest UK universities” without looking at the person's actual situation first.If you're currently considering the UK yourself, what's your course/background and rough total budget? title: Ndarani Awards 11 Scholarships To Niger State Indigenes Up To Post-graduate Leve
main_content:
Thread Title: Ndarani Awards 11 Scholarships To Niger State Indigenes Up To Post-graduate Leve

Main Post: By Ebere Agozie A Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Mohammed Ndarani has awarded scholarships to 11 students from Niger state in different universities.Ndarani gave the scholarship awards through his Mohammed Ndarani Humanitarian Foundation when the Council of Students Union Government (SUG) Presidents, Niger state paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja. The learned silk who said he has adopted the students as his sons promised to sponsor them to degree and some at post-graduate levels.He noted that the foundation is a platform for him to give back to the society, making life meaningful for the less privileged at the grassroots and adding value to nation-building which is a collective responsibility."Education is key to some of the nation’s challenges. If given the required attention and funding, education would provide the way out of the most of the country’s problems."The goal is to assist struggling students in the state and combat declining educational performance across the nation."My aim is to encourage our people to acquire education by easing the financial burden on students and parents."So, these scholarships are designed to benefit humanity and advance human capital development which will help the state grow."The senior lawyer who has provided various forms of scholarships to students across the country noted that there is the need to continue to impact the lives of average Nigerians at the grassroots which is why he is giving back to Nigerians.In his response, Comr. Baba Shehu, popularly known as ABS, who is also the Chairman of the SUGs said that they were aware of the numerous humanitarian gestures by Mohammed Ndarani Foundation and expressed delight with his philanthropic nature, urging him to maintain the tempo."We, the student union presidents from different schools in Niger axis under one umbrella came to present an Icon of Students Transformation and Character Building to the learned silk for his efforts in sustainable socio-economic development of the society and we are going home with scholarships."We are overwhelmed with gratitude for this generosity that will not only empower, but will also enable us to empower and uplift others across the country."Shehu noted that Ndarani had sponsored his immediate past president to study law in Newgate University, Minna and also donated the sum of N100 million to Niger State students for scholarship which was why they came on the visit."Well, all I have to say is Alhamdulillah. What we came for was not what we met here. We only came to appreciate him for what he did for our colleague and he just did the same thing for us here now, " Shehu added. The students who promised not to let the SAN down in any capacity they find themselves, added that they will remain good ambassadors of the state."As children emulate good characters of their parents, so from now henceforth, he is our father and we promise him that we are not going to let him down but work for humanity."The Mohammed Ndarani Humanitarian Foundation targets interventions in agriculture and rural development, education, health, as well as youths and women empowerment.

Studying in Germany : What you should knowThis is in response to a FAQ I always get from scholars especially nairalanders.The first point of contact is this website:Daad.de/enThe website above contain almost all the university in Germany and some other sister universities around Germany.Most of the schools in Germany are tuition free even for international students, you only get to pay a certain amount as semester fees say between 100-400 euros and most times the semester fee comes with a semester ticket to aid in transportation in your city or town.However, before you're granted a student visa, you have to prove that you can take care of your living expenses with one of the following means ;1. Block account: The estimated living expenses for a student in a month is 720euros, when you multiply that by 12 months, you get 8640euros. This is the amount you're required to block in an already opened account with either Deutsch bank, Fintiba or Xpatrio. It is called a block account because you will not be able to withdraw everything at once, only 720euros will be released to you every month.2. Sponsorship letter: If you have a relative living and working legally in Germany, they can get you this letter. They'll have to visit the alien office in their city and will be required to provide some documents and pay a certain fee. The letter will be sent to you when they receive it so that you can go with it for your visa interview.3. Scholarship: This is usually the best if you have the scholarship, your visa will be granted in under 2 weeks after interview. So try and look for scholarships you can apply to.Now that you understand the financial situation, let's go into the application process.To search for schools, click on this link[LINK] your search to make it easier, there are English taught courses there.Generally, the very important documents needed to apply to schools in Germany are;1. Transcript2. English Proficiency3. School Certificates (Degree, Waec, etc)However, depending on the school, some other documents needed are as follows.4. Curriculum Vitae5. Motivation letter6. Reference letters7. GRE test8. Etcetera.. Visit your prospective school website and find out the documents they need from you.Note: You don't apply with your original documents, you have to make photocopies of them and Certify them in High court or a Notary public. If you stay in Lagos, you can certify at the German Embassy too. You'll have to book appointment for that.For those planning to go for a Bachelors course, you need a 100level transcript from a university to apply for a BSc program in Germany. WAEC alone will not be enough and No, OND will not do, you need a HND.For the application proper, it is always important to go through the website of the schools you want to apply to, you'll get a lot of information form there concerning how to apply. Some schools do only online applications, some require that you send your application documents to them by post after applying online, while in some you'll send your documents as pdf to their email address and then you get the uni assist crew.Like I said earlier, it is important to go visit and read the websites.When you get your admission letter, open a block account immediately(that is if you don't already have a sponsorship letter) and as soon as you get your account details, send an email to the embassy requesting for a visa interview date.You need these to get an interview date:1. Admission letter2. Block account/sponsorship letter/scholarship letter3. International passport data page(scanned)Then your Full name and Resident address.Prepare for your interviewGo for your interviewCredit:Dokita RoyaltyFor your Academic CV,Statement of Purpose,Research Proposal,Term Paper,Scholarship support ,Call/Chat: [PHONE]

Studying in the US- Important tips1. Firstly prepare for the basic requirements. The US is very serious about it's travel precautions, so you need genuine passport, ids, certificates, transcripts, (Just the basics).2. Transcripts, that the most important. Some schools require official and unofficial transcripts. Most of them require unofficial first and official transcript later. Unofficial transcripts are the transcript given directly to students(student transcript).3. Official ones are one that would be sent directly from your previous institution to you chosen school in US. But first it will be stated clearly if you need official or unofficial transcript for the application process.. (Mostly unofficial though).4. Furthermore,some schools require transcript evaluations.This I must say is a headache because course by course evaluation of transcript cost much.So you have to check the school’s websites if you need a transcript evaluation.5. Until you send your transcript for evaluation to the required institutions, you can’t complete your application. So all I am saying is for you to check on the school website first because most schools also take the pain to evaluate too for themselves.6. If you are here at this point, you are good to apply to schools. Take time go online. Search requirements. Email admission office. Call admission office if you do not get feedback on time.9. American schools unlike UK need you to pay admission fees ranging from 30 to 50 dollars and some a little more. Atleast apply to about 4 schools and try getting in touch with the admission office.10. Applying alone doesn’t guarantee you admission. Just like your previous institution, it is based on merit. If you get admission, your scholarship amount will also be given.. Either full or half. Scholarship talk centered on different countries especially those we are familiar with e.g Canada, USA, Germany,UK and China. We will talk about Canada/US,GERMANY and China.Let's start with Canada because statistically, everyone now wants to go to Canada because of the great opportunities in the country.Getting scholarship abroad is not a one day journey, it's requires continuity, endurance, perseverance, hardwork not neglecting the God factor. The decision to study outside your home country is very enticing but is not always very easy,especially when you are trying to get funds from the school or professor.Canada for instance is a good place to study especially if you would like to stay and work after study. Most schools don't ask for GRE and Toefl especially if you are from Nigeria. To get scholarship/grant in Canada requires great determination and consistency but believe me it is very possible. We have a member of our group (Creative Minds)presently studying in Canada via Research grant. In the year 2017 while he was serving,he chatted me up telling me of his intention to further his study after NYSC. I had to draft his Academic CV and gave him tips but he was more than determined,he did extensive research and did lot's of skype interview with Professors in his field in different parts of the world. He later go a grant and he is presently schooling there while working as a graduate assistant in Canada.The following are the things to put in place before embarking on a scholarship journey1. Prayer2. Get your certificates ready i.e degree certificates plus transcripts. Getting transcript in a Nigerian University maybe a bit tasking because you may be applying to different universities. For every application, you will have to request for your transcript from your University which means your school would charge per transcript per school of application but a good way to solve this issue is to use a travelling agent or the organization you are working with. You can pick the transcript once you school sends it and then you can proceed to making different application to different schools. We have solved the transcript issue right?

For CanadaChoosing your Proposed Course of StudyThe number one thing is for you to choose your proposed Course of Study and also decide on the Research you will like to pursue. I mean your research title e.g “The Impact of Intelligentdude Consult in the Lives of Nigeria Youths”.The world is filled with amazing opportunities; it is now imperative for you to know what exactly you are looking for. Knowing the title of the course and your proposed area of specialization is the first point of call. The next move or task will be to embark on the look-out for where you can get what you want with what you have. Once you make a decision on the field you want to specialize on,take the next step by looking for schools offering your proposed course of study. The next major thing is getting a supervisor. Imagine thousands of applicants who dream of schooling in Canada on a free tuition basis.(You need a 100% commitment and determination if you want to follow the route of grant/scholarship)GRE and TOEFL are not required in some Canadian universities but it is advisable to write TOEFL inorder to have lots of options.Now the big question is: How can I secure a supervisor?Pay a visit to your potential university website.Most of us know: [LINK] Canada has few universities unlike United States of America just for the record.From the University website proceed to the departmental website of your chosen course, e.g environmental science department then look for lecturers that are spearheading research works in your area of interest. (there are various environmental science research, you just need to choose the one that interest you .It is always cool if have firsthand knowledge of the research especially if it's related to your BSc research work or your work experience). There is usually a link on university websites that shows you where to get a University lecturer’s contacts i.e your potential supervisor for your graduate courses. Ensure you go through his or her past and present research areas of interest. They always have one particular research focus unlike what is applicable in our dear country.

In the quest to further our education abroad,there are some preparations which should be made for our desires to be fruitful and one of such preparations is the preparation of our documents.The documents needed are :Academic CV :While applying for further studies,jobs,grants,fellowships and even conferences,you will be required to submit an Academic CV. This document is different from a business CV and has a different format.An academic CV focuses on academic experience and accomplishments. Anything not relevant to this should be considered for omission.There can be more pages in an academic CV compared to a general CV. This is due to the additional sections and information that may be required for academia.The most important thing to keep in mind when writing your academic CV is to tailor it to each position you apply for. You should prioritize the accomplishments that are most important to the intuition/position you are applying for.Statement of Purpose:The Statement of Purpose is the single most important part of your application that will tell the admissions committee who you are, what has influenced your career path so far, your professional interests and where you plan to go from here.The SoP is your chance to talk directly to the admissions committee. To make yourself stand out from among a multitude of similarly qualified candidates. To convince the committee that you have the spark, the thirst for knowledge that could add value to your class.“A statement of purpose should be between 500 and 1,000 words,” says Pierce. He advises that students use a traditional font at a readable size (11- or 12-pt) and leave enough whitespace in the margins to make the statement easy-to-read. Make sure to double-space the statement if the university has requested it, he adds.Study Plan :A study plan is a summary of the subject requirements of your course and indicates when planned subjects should be studied. It indicates the subjects you have completed; are currently enrolled in; plan to study in the future; and those for which you have been granted advanced standing (credit for previous studies).For those applying to Universities in China, this document will come in handy in the course of your application.Here are some of the points you will address when writing your study Plan.1. Why did you choose to study abroad in your accepted program?2. What is your utmost educational objective?3. Why are you not undertaking a similar course in your home country?4. Have done research about studies in your country?5. Will the program you interested in enhancing employment opportunities in your home country?6. What ties you to your country?These are some of the documents you need to prepare while planning for further studies.For more enquiries,feel free to call/chat with Intelligentdude on : [PHONE]We offer the following services for clients :Academic CV Writing,Statement of Purpose(SOP),Personal Statement,Letter of Intent,Letter of Motivation,Study Plan,Term Paper Writing,Research Plan writing, call/chat: [PHONE]. Feel free to send us a mail :[EMAIL][LINK]

Statement of Purpose (SOP)/Motivational Letter (ML)(carries a good scoring,make yours scholastic because this is how they will know whether you know what you want to do or not) .Furthermore, draft your Statement of Purpose/Letter of Intent in a way that will communicate your educational background,experience,passion,interest,the relationship between your undergraduate course of study and you proposed Masters course,your personality,why you choosed the University, why the Lecturer etc .(For your Statement of Purpose, Research Plan, Letter of Intent, Study Plan etc on : [PHONE]).Address the SOP statement of purpose) or ML (Motivation Letter) to the selected supervisors and send it to their respective email addresses; (Note that Foreign Lecturers treat emails seriously unlike our Nigerian lecturers). You can possibly attach some regular documents such as your transcript and resume. If you don’t get a response after five working days you can attempt placing a call to their Office phones or send the email again.( e.g you sent your application tomorrow being Friday, if you don’t get a response from them, send another next week Friday) but avoid bombarding them with emails so they wont see you as nuisance. You can imagine the number of mails these guys receive daily.“Getting a supervisor” is a very important part of the application process because for the majority of universities in Canada,securing a supervisor is almost tantamount to gaining admission. It is always good to get the consent of a supervisor before going ahead with the payment of the application fee; remember application fees varies but is usually 100$. Don't forget to Make Inquiries about the Availability of Research Funding and If you get a response from a Professor and he/she is willing to take you in as his or her student, then you just hit a jackpot and congratulations are in order because you have successfully secured an advisor. You can go ahead to make inquiries from the Professor if it is possible to be a beneficiary of a research funding and work as a research assistant. If you get a positive response as regard the funding, you will be required to work with your supervisor on a specified research topic and this just secured a job for you as a Graduate Research Assistant.(with a mouth watering pay, they call it stipends but it is sometimes around #400k/monthly but the amount varies. Some may even give you Field truck etc.

What to noteStart as early as possible and be well-acquainted with the deadlines for the Winter semester (January), Summer (May) and Fall (September). Also note that "Not all universities have openings in Summer, the predominant entry period for the majority of the courses in universities are Winter and Fall semesters".

title: FG To Give Students 100MB Free Data Daily From October 1
main_content:
Thread Title: FG To Give Students 100MB Free Data Daily From October 1

Main Post: The Federal Government has announced that Nigerian students will start receiving 100MB of free data daily from October 1 under a new initiative aimed at improving access to digital learning.The programme, known as the Zero-Rated Access to Educational Platforms and Content Initiative, was unveiled by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, during its official launch in Abuja. According to the minister, the scheme will initially benefit about five million students, giving them free access to approved educational websites and digital learning platforms without paying for data. Alausa said the initiative is designed to help students, particularly those from low-income families and underserved communities, overcome one of the biggest barriers to online learning: the cost of internet access. The programme will first cover students in senior secondary schools and tertiary institutions, with plans to expand it to other categories of learners in the future. The Federal Government said only approved educational platforms that meet national curriculum standards will qualify for the free-data programme. Authorities also plan to monitor usage to ensure students are using the service for learning purposes. The initiative is being implemented through a partnership involving the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), the Federal Ministry of Education, telecommunications operators and other stakeholders. Officials believe the project could significantly expand access to online education and digital skills training across the country, especially as schools increasingly rely on technology-based learning resources. title: Learn How To Start An Essay Correctly
main_content:
Thread Title: Learn How To Start An Essay Correctly

Main Post: Ever heard of the phrase, the first impression is the last impression?It is important that you make a strong first impression on someone if you want them to like you.The same holds true when you’re writing an essay or any other academic paper. If your opening is strong, the chances of your professor liking the essay and giving you a good grade increase automatically. Because a reader decides whether or not something is worth reading on the basis of the introduction. If they get bored by the introduction, it is highly unlikely that they will want to read further.How you start your essay is an important factor and is something that most students have a hard time with. Unsure of what the perfect way is to open the essay, they keep staring at the blank screen or paper.To avoid this from happening to you, it is essential that you learn the different ways of starting an essay.The introductory paragraph of your essay is one of the most significant parts that serves as a motivator. It is written in such a way that it helps attract the reader and grab their attention, making them want to read till the end.Not just that, your introduction also helps educate the reader about the topic at hand so that it becomes easier for them to understand.A strong essay introduction consists of three important elements – hook sentence, background information and the thesis statement.Here’s how you need to incorporate each of these elements in your writing:Writing a hook sentenceThink of an essay hook as the fisherman's hook that is used to catch fish. A hook sentence is an interesting piece of information regarding the essay topic that grabs the reader’s attention.There are different types of hook sentences that you can choose from, depending on the type of essay and topic.The most commonly used are:Quote – you open your essay with a quotation said by a famous person. Make sure that it is relevant to the topic and came from a reliable source.Question – ask a thought-provoking question that will intrigue the reader making them wanting to know more. Avoid using too obvious or yes/no questions.Statistic – you can start by some shocking statistical facts related to the topic when writing a more informative essay.Anecdote – it is similar to a short, funny story that you can share with the reader. It can be a real story or an imaginative one.Providing background informationOnce you have hooked the reader, the next thing you need to do is introduce the topic that you will tackle. Talk about the main idea of the essay and give them some background information so that it gets easier for them to comprehend. Avoid giving away too much at this point so you don’t bore or scare the reader.Present a strong thesis statementLastly, you need to write a strong thesis statement that highlights the main claim and purpose of the essay. A thesis statement should be clear, arguable and easy to justify.If you still can’t come up with a strong essay introduction, you can look for other options. Get in touch with an expert essay writer to get essay writing help free.

title: Commonwealth Scholarship Open — If You Have This Profile, Don't Waste It!!️
main_content:
Thread Title: Commonwealth Scholarship Open — If You Have This Profile, Don't Waste It!!️

Main Post: Every year, as soon as the Commonwealth Master’s Scholarship opens, Nairaland gets flooded with the same questions. Everyone wants to know if a 2:1 is enough, if their course fits a theme, or if they need to upload an NYSC certificate. But let's be honest. Meeting the requirement is the easy part. If you have a 2:1 or a First Class, some relevant work or volunteer experience, and you found a course that fits one of the six CSC development themes, congratulations—you are officially eligible. You can legally click "submit."But qualifying is not the same thing as being competitive. This is where things get interesting, and this is where I see applicants make mistakes. The biggest misconception people have is assuming: "I qualify, therefore I have a strong application." The truth? The Commonwealth portal is packed with files belonging to people who are just as eligible as you are. They all have the degrees. They all have the grades. They all have a course. Eligibility just gets your file past the automated screening system. It does not make your application compelling. If two applicants are looking at the exact same development theme, with the exact same 2:1 grade, what makes the panel remember one and completely forget the other? It comes down to how you position your story. Here is what actually separates a basic, eligible application from a well-positioned one:1. The Logic Behind the Course SelectionMany eligible applicants pick a UK Master's degree simply because the university is highly ranked or because the course name sounds prestigious. That is a weak strategy.A compelling application demonstrates a tight connection between the proposed Master's and a highly specific development problem in Nigeria. You aren't just choosing a course; you are pitching a specific technical intervention. Why that specific field? Why that particular curriculum? A strong applicant can clearly explain why the modules in that specific UK program provide the exact missing knowledge required to address a concrete local issue.2. A Credible Past-to-Future TrajectoryThe most memorable applications have a completely believable, logical storyline. It connects four specific points:What you have already studied or done professionally.The specific developmental bottleneck you encountered while doing that work.Why the proposed UK Master's is the exact tool needed to solve that bottleneck.What specific, measurable action you intend to take with that knowledge within 5 years of returning to Nigeria.If the panel reads your essays and cannot see a straight, logical line connecting your past experience to your future development plan, the application loses credibility—even if your GPA is perfect.3. Evidence Over Vague ClaimsAnyone can type the words "I am a natural leader" or "I am deeply passionate about impacting my community." In a sea of identical essays, vague claims look like white noise.Strong applicants don't just state their traits; they prove them with specific evidence. They talk about actual projects managed, specific responsibilities handled, measurable outcomes achieved, or distinct organizations they have collaborated with. They focus on specificity, numbers, and verifiable impact. If your essays are full of generic, high-sounding adjectives instead of concrete facts, you are relying on the panel to guess how good you are.4. The Referee Narrative DisconnectThis is a blind spot for many smart applicants. You might spend weeks crafting a brilliant, evidence-based development story, only for your referees to submit a generic letter that reads like a standard template. If your application claims you are a strategic driver of a specific agricultural development project, but your referee simply writes "He was a quiet, disciplined student in my class," your narrative immediately loses its footing. A well-positioned application requires your referees to actively validate and speak to the exact leadership and development traits you have highlighted in your essays.5. Demonstrable Specificity and Local ContextWhat makes an application memorable is an evident, long-term commitment to a specific cause. When someone writes about a development issue with deep local context—citing specific local challenges, policy gaps, or systemic issues—it shows they didn't just spend five minutes reading a Wikipedia page to pass the scholarship essay. It shows they actually understand the landscape they claim they want to change.The Trap Eligible Applicants Fall IntoThe danger for smart, qualified applicants is falling into the "cliché essay" trap. Because they know they have a good profile on paper, they write generic development statements like "I want to return to Nigeria to help my country develop its infrastructure." That means nothing to a selection panel. It lacks specificity, it lacks a personal angle, and it doesn't show any real strategic thinking. Turning a list of solid professional achievements and an eligible degree into a coherent, evidence-based Commonwealth application is an entirely different task than just filling out a form. Ask Yourself These 4 Diagnostic Questions:Before you begin drafting your essays, look at your profile through the eyes of the panel:1. If I remove my name and grades from this application, does my development story sound exactly like every other applicant in my field?2. Can I clearly point to the specific evidence in my past that proves I have the capacity to execute my 5-year post-scholarship plan?3. Is my chosen UK course a logical next step for my career, or does it look like I just picked a random degree to get a fully funded ticket to the UK?4. Are my chosen referees fully aligned with the specific development narrative I am presenting to the committee?The application window for the 2027/2028 academic cycle is open from September 8, 2026, until October 20, 2026. Make sure to carefully verify the official requirements, deadlines, and specific interview guidelines through the official Commonwealth Scholarship Commission (CSC) portal and the appropriate national nominating agencies like the Federal Scholarship Board (FSB).If you already know you meet the basic criteria, but you want to ensure your application strategy, course justification, and development story are positioned to stand out, the contact details are on my Nairaland profile. Let's discuss how you are pitching your development impact. What specific bottleneck in your sector are you targeting with your chosen UK course?

Comments:

A lot of people are asking about the basic eligibility requirements, but that's actually not the part I'd be most worried about.The harder question is:“If 100 other applicants have the same 2:1/First Class as me, why should the panel select MY application?”That's where your course choice, development problem, leadership evidence, career trajectory and 5-year plan become important.And please don't wait until you've written the essays before thinking about this. Your answers should already have a clear direction before you start drafting.If you're applying this year, I'd strongly recommend doing a proper profile check first especially if you're unsure whether your current experience gives you enough evidence for a strong application.

The Commonwealth Mistake Nobody Talks About: Your Essay May Not Be The Problem!!️I've seen applicants spend days worrying about how to write a “powerful” Commonwealth essay.But there's something I'd check before touching the first essay.THE COURSE.Because you can have:• First Class• Strong work experience• Leadership experience• Good references• A beautiful personal statement...and still have a weak application if the proposed Master's doesn't make sense for your career and development story.This is the part people don't talk about enough.The Commonwealth Scholarship isn't simply:“I have good grades + I want to study in the UK.”The panel needs to understand why this particular course is necessary.Imagine two applicants.Applicant A says:“I want to study MSc Environmental Management because I am passionate about environmental sustainability and want to contribute to Nigeria.”Sounds nice.Applicant B says:“I've worked in X area and encountered Y problem. My current training doesn't give me the technical knowledge to address Z. The proposed Master's gives me specific training in A, B and C, which directly connects to the intervention I intend to implement in Nigeria.”Both may be eligible.But their applications are telling completely different stories.And here's the rare part:Sometimes the course you personally like the most is not the course that gives you the strongest scholarship application.You have to separate:“I want to study this.”from“I can convincingly explain why Commonwealth should fund me to study this.”Those are not always the same thing.Before submitting, I'd ask myself:1. What exact problem am I trying to solve?2. Why does my current education/work experience lead naturally to this problem?3. What specific knowledge will this Master's give me that I currently lack?4. Why does this particular course provide that knowledge?5. What am I realistically going to do with it after returning to Nigeria?If you can't answer those questions clearly, changing adjectives in your essay probably won't save the application.Don't start with “How do I write my Commonwealth essay?”Start with:“Does my entire application actually make sense?”Because sometimes the problem isn't the writing.It's the story you're trying to write in the first place.!!️If you're applying for the 2027/28 cycle, I'd genuinely do this check BEFORE submitting anything.What course are you considering, and what development problem are you connecting it to?

title: I Will Never Pay Another Guru To Teach Me Affiliate Marketing Again — Here's Why
main_content:
Thread Title: I Will Never Pay Another Guru To Teach Me Affiliate Marketing Again — Here's Why

Main Post: Let me be honest with you from the very first line.I have been where you are right now.I spent years — not months, years — moving from one so-called guru to the next. Paying for course after course. Sitting through training after training. Taking notes on terminology so big and complicated it made my head spin.Funnels. Conversion rates. Click-through ratios. Split testing. Traffic arbitrage. Re-targeting pixels.Big grammar. Big promises. Big price tags.And after all of it?Not one single sale.Not one commission alert. Not one notification that said — someone bought through your link. Nothing. Zero. Empty.I sat with that emptiness for a long time and I had to ask myself a very honest question: is the problem me — or is the problem the people I have been paying to teach me?The answer changed everything.The problem was never me.The gurus were teaching me theory wrapped in jargon designed to make them sound important — not to make me successful. They needed me to feel confused so I would keep coming back, keep paying, keep depending on them for the next piece of the puzzle they were deliberately withholding.I made a decision.I stopped paying. I stopped listening to people who had never sat in my exact situation — broke, frustrated, passionate, and completely stuck at zero.I slowed down.I started reading on my own. Researching on my own. Testing on my own. Failing on my own terms — which felt completely different from failing while following someone else's expensive instructions.And slowly — because I was finally learning the real thing instead of the packaged version someone was selling me — something shifted.I got my breakthrough.I am not here to tell you the exact amount because this post is not about me showing off. It is about something far more important than that.Here is the thing nobody in this space wants to say out loud:Affiliate marketing is not complicated.It is actually one of the simplest business models that exists. You find a product someone else created. You promote it to people who need it. You earn a commission when they buy. That is it.But here is what makes it feel complicated — and this is the part that broke me for years before I figured it out:Most beginners are making the same 7 mistakes without knowing it. And nobody is telling them. Not the gurus — because if they told you, you would not need them anymore. Not the YouTube videos — because they give you enough information to feel busy but not enough to actually succeed.Those 7 mistakes are the only reason most beginners never make their first sale.Not the economy. Not their location. Not their following size. Not their age or education.Seven mistakes. That is the entire problem.Why I am here on Nairaland today.I know the pain of this thing called affiliate marketing.I know what it feels like to watch other people post commission screenshots while you are sitting there wondering what they know that you do not.I know what it feels like to explain to your family why you have spent so much time on your phone and your laptop — and still have nothing to show for it.I know what it feels like to almost give up on something you genuinely believe in — not because the thing does not work, but because nobody would show you how it actually works.That is why I am here.I want to work with beginners only. Not experienced marketers. Not people who are already making sales and want to scale. Beginners. The people who are exactly where I was — passionate, willing to learn, tired of confusion, and ready for something real.Here is what I want you to understand about affiliate marketing that nobody told me when I started:Everyone does affiliate marketing. Most people just do not get paid for it.Every time you tell a friend about a restaurant you enjoyed — that is affiliate marketing. Every time you recommend a product on WhatsApp — that is affiliate marketing. Every time you share something online that makes someone else want to buy — that is affiliate marketing.The only difference between you doing it for free and you getting paid for it is a system. One simple, honest, tested system.That is what I am here to share.What I am NOT:- I am not a guru. I will never call myself one.- I do not have a N50,000 course to sell you. - I do not have a secret society you need to pay to join. - I do not have a certificate on my wall that makes me qualified to take your money.What I have is a breakthrough that came from years of painful learning — and a genuine desire to compress those years into something a beginner can learn and apply in days.What I AM:- I am someone who failed at this the same way you are failing right now.- I am someone who eventually cracked it — not through a guru, but through patience, reading, research, and refusing to give up on something I believed in.- And I am someone who believes that information that can change a person's financial situation should not be locked behind a paywall that only benefits the person selling it.This is Day 1.I will be posting here regularly — real lessons, real strategies, real answers to real questions.- No hype.- No jargon. - No up-sells hiding behind free content.Just the honest truth about affiliate marketing — from someone who has lived both sides of it.If you are a complete beginner who has been trying to make your first affiliate sale and getting nowhere — follow this thread. Ask your questions. Share your frustrations.You are not alone in this. And you are not as far from your first sale as you think.One last thing before I go.I have written a free guide — completely free, nothing to buy — that exposes the 7 mistakes most beginners are making right now without knowing it. Every mistake has a fix. Every fix has action steps.If you want it, drop a comment below or send me a message and I will share it with you directly.No payment. No form to fill. No trick.Just the information you should have had from day one.Welcome to something different.JM Digital HubLearn • Promote • EarnTo all the gurus reading this:You know who you are. And you know exactly what you have been doing.

PUZZLING SELECTION SINKS NIGERIA'S AFCON QUESTThe stakes could not be higher, but Siasia's odd selection choices robbed the Super Eagles of any flow and rhythm in attack in Alexandria By Solace Chukwu Where once it seemed an aberration to have an Africa Cup of Nations without Nigeria, there is now a sense of resigned inevitability to it. The Fifa ranking cops quite a bit of flak (are Cape Verde really the best team in Africa?) but in the case of the Super Eagles, it may well be overgenerous.One miss might be considered unfortunate, but a repeat serves only to buttress the most uncomfortable of truths: Nigeria are no longer one of Africa’s best 16 teams. The 2013 triumph in South Africa seems now a distant memory, the cruel shadow of a haunting memory tugging away at the back of the mind, fluttering just out of reach and leaving in its wake baleful emptiness.Charged with the task of exorcising that ghost was an eleven that appeared to defy logic and reason; so much so, it became convenient to see method in the madness: perhaps Siasia sought to spring a surprise on the Pharaohs, luring them into the sort of false sense of security that proved their undoing in the epic Biblical tale of Hebrew redemption at the Red Sea.As it turns out, it was Nigeria’s wheels that came unstuck in the end. Far more worrying though than the underwhelming choices and performances of the likes of Aminu Umar and Stanley Amuzie, it was clear that, as a team, there was little conviction to how it sought to create the goal(s) required to remain in contention. Surely, if the idea was to take the game to the hosts from the off, a bit more invention in central areas than either Umar or Ahmed Musa are capable of would have seemed apposite.Did Siasia's selection decisions undermine Nigeria?The effect of both Victor Moses and the CSKA Moscow man taking up narrow positions meant oodles of space on the flank, but yet again – as it was against South Africa in Uyo in 2014 – neither full-back provided width on the overlap. The hosts therefore only had to defend the width of their penalty box, and were largely untroubled against an attack that appeared to feature four (five if you count a neither-fish-nor-fowl Oghenekaro Etebo) strangers uncertain of their collective moments.Shehu Abdullahi at right-back – there’s an experiment that has spontaneously combusted in all our faces – looked totally overawed by the occasion, and was full of errors all game long. His haplessness evinced sympathy, and though it was Amuzie at left-back who was withdrawn at half-time, one gets the impression it was for lack of a proper deputy at right-back.The Borg El Arab Stadium may have lacked the sheer weight of numbers that crammed itself into the Ahmadu Bello Stadium, Kaduna on Friday, but it made up for it with an atmosphere of hissing malevolence and zipping green lasers. It worked; aside captain John Obi Mikel and Daniel Akpeyi, who pulled off two splendid stops in the first period, no one else in green came out of this smelling of roses. If eleven subs were possible, Siasia may well have made them all.There was perhaps no greater indication that he had got his starting line-up wrong than the nature of his substitutions: all broadly like-for-like, each introducing a player who should have started the tie—Elderson Echiejile’s experience at the highest level was surely not something to sniff at; Etebo’s impersonation of a central midfielder, untidy and imprecise as it was, gave way to the smooth Azubuike Okechukwu; while Alex Iwobi, in his 20 minutes, showed more guile and ability to knit the play together than the limited Umar managed in 70.Quite why Siasia thought it wise to keep his powder dry so long, with his team needing a win, is anyone’s guess.He may have saved the fine wine for last, but by the time the changes were made, the Super Eagles were addled, swaying on their feet and pretty much out for the count. It seemed almost mercifully fortunate that Moses’s fizzing shot came off the post and spun out: renewed hope, in this case, would have been little more than prolonging the agony.What this team needs; nay, what Nigerian football needs now, is surgery. [LINK]

Five things to fix Nigeria after failure to reach African Nations CupSamson Siasia, who coached Nigeria at the Beijing Olympics in 2008, will get another crack at a medal next summer in Rio.Samson Siasia has to be allowed to stay in charge.It's the morning after a night of heartbreak. Nigeria's Super Eagles will be missing from a second consecutive African Nations Cup after they lost 1-0 to Egypt in the second leg to crash out of the group 2-1 on aggregate.For a country with a population that dwarfs the majority of others on the continent, which exports the greatest number of football players overseas, and has been consistently on the top tier of African football, it is a stunning confirmation of decline.This recent failure will mark the third time in four editions that Nigeria miss out on Africa's showpiece event. That is the mark of continental minnows and, due to their performances, they really should be considered minnows in African football.Recognising the problem is the first step towards finding a resolution, and here is where Nigeria should start.1. Allow Samson Siasia to continue as bossWhile the troubles within the Nigeria team started much earlier, it came to the boil with the inability to qualify for the 2012 African Nations Cup.Rather than take a step back to assess why the team failed to qualify, and what needed to be done, an immediate quick fix was to fire Siasia. This, despite the fact that he not only got the squad playing an exciting brand of football, but was also scoring a hatful of goals.During the current qualifying series, three coaches, with three contrasting styles and almost three different sets of players were employed. Each coach with three different captains. It all added up to disaster.Siasia may have been appointed as a stand-in coach, but it is time for the Nigerian FA (NFF) to look at the big picture and hand him a long-term contract to continue the process he started.There is no need for a new coach to come in and start a "rebuilding" process that has been going on for the better part of six years.Siasia understands the NFF's constraints. They are well aware of his limitations. Between them, they can find a lasting workaround that serves the best interests of Nigeria.What we saw over 180 minutes against Egypt is a team a that played delightful football, created opportunities, showed promise but were let down for the most part by defensive fragility.Given time, and perhaps with a little help from technical director Shaibu Amodu to help with defensive structure, this is a team that can go far if they keep the manager.2. Football must be unshackledIt is easy enough to dump the blame for this disaster at the door step of the NFF. And, in fairness, as the body charged with administering the game, they should take responsibility. But here's the thing: Nigeria have failed to qualify under three different administrations, so perhaps the issues run a little deeper?Actually, it does. Government shackles are the major reason the federation cannot function properly. Having to wait months for financing, even after budgets have been slashed unrecognizably, does little to help plans and preparations.This has been said so many times it has become hackneyed, but government really has to let go of football. It should not even be up for discussion anymore.3. Players must show their passionNow to the actual football. Back when the Super Eagles were the best team in Africa, the players did not play for the world's biggest clubs. As a matter of fact, some were even clubless. What they did have, however, was a sense of commitment and dedication to the cause.Did they have issues with administrators? Of course. There were all manner of rows and disputes over bonuses, tickets and the likes. But when they stepped on the pitch, they left it all there.And that was what marked the Super Eagles out. These days, players talk of high spirits and confidence, but it's hard to see when they are on the pitch.If Nigeria keep the coach and allow him to build a core team, rather than playing a game of musical chairs where players are not sure if they'll return for the next game or not, that is the first step. Leadership cannot blossom in such an uncertain atmosphere.Odion IghaloOdion Ighalo needs the side to play to his strengths.4. Play to Ighalo's strengthsOne such player is Odion Ighalo. The Watford forward is without doubt Nigeria's hottest striker in Europe. He may have hit a dry patch in the Premier League in the lead up to these qualifiers, but his quality is not in doubt. However, he failed to score over two legs and the question must be asked, did he carry over his dip in form? Or does the system just not suit him?On the evidence of the two games, one would have to go with the system. For long periods, Ighalo looked lonely, sandwiched between two defenders with next to no support. On one occasion, he dropped deep, picked up a ball and played a vertical reverse pass in behind but Ahmed Musa, who had moved into that central space, failed to read it and did not make the run. That was one move that epitomised Ighalo's frustrations.His best moments came when Alex Iwobi came on. The Arsenal teenager's direct running played to the Watford man's strengths and their interplay caused trouble for Egypt.So, it might be time for Siasia to consider tweaking his system to suit the players at his disposal. Many fans are already criticising Ighalo and it would be a big mistake for Siasia to drop him. He needs confidence to deliver and the coach must give him that confidence by backing him.Rashidi Yekini missed tons of chances, but he always had the confidence of a striker who knew his coach and teammates had his back. Right now, that's what Ighalo needs too.5. Sort out the defenceDefence used to be one of Nigeria's strong points. But, in recent years, that has failed to be the case. Stephen Keshi put a patch on it by playing a somewhat conservative style, like his mentor Amodu. It was painful to watch, but it was efficient.Siasia usually takes the opposite route, by going for an all-out attacking approach. When it works, it is beautiful; when the team doesn't score, it can be disastrous.A hybrid solution (only with Siasia's buy-in, of course) would be to get Amodu to join in temporarily and help design and implement a defensive structure for the team.With no Nations Cup on the horizon, that time might be best served plugging the holes. It would also help if the likes of Leon Balogun and Kenneth Omeruo can manage to stay injury free for consistent, protracted periods.[LINK]

10 Reasons Why Super Eagles Failed To Qualify For AFCONCompletesportsnigeria.com’s JOHNNY EDWARD and ADEBOYE AMOSU examine why the Super Eagles failed to qualify for their second straight Africa Cup of Nations. They come up with 10 reasons for this failure...1. POOR SELECTIONSuper Eagles caretaker coach, Samson Siasia, made some blunders in his selection which played a key part in the team’s failure to beat the Pharaohs in both legs of the qualifiers.His decision to start Stanley Amuzie at left-back ahead of the more experienced Elderson Echiejile was a big blunder.Amuzie was disappointing in both games, no wonder he was hauled off at half time in Alexandria.Also his decision to play Oghenekaro Etebo in the holding midfield role when Ogenyi Onazi was available for selection in Alexandria following his suspension for the game in Kaduna was also questionable.Siasia also persisted with Ahmed Musa when it was obvious the duo of Moses Simon and Alex Iwobi would have done a better job. 2. ODION IGHALO’S FAILURE TO REPLICATE CLUB FORMMuch was expected from the Watford man, but he never lived up to expectations over the two legs. His inability to replicate his club form for the Super Eagles has no doubt cost the team a place in Gabon 2017.3. POOR PLANNINGThe Super Eagles were earlier scheduled to travel to Alexandria immediately after the first leg in Kaduna, but the Nigeria Football Federation later altered the plan.Instead the team left the country on Monday and following a two hour delay at the Nnamdi Azikwe Stadium, add that to the two hours they spent on the road from Kaduna to Abuja, it was a long and tortuous journey that affected the performance of the team.Not only were the players unable to train properly after arriving late on Monday, they looked rusty on match day.4. NO CO-ORDINATION BETWEEN MIDFIELD AND ATTACKThe Super Eagles lost the battle in the middle of the park and that contributed to their defeat against the Pharaohs.Captain of the side, Mikel Obi, started the game brightly, but fizzled out afterwards.Watford striker, Odion Ighalo, was left isolated upfront as he didn’t have much support from the midfielders, leaving Victor Moses as the team’s only attacking threat.The defence was also overworked as there was no proper holding midfielder to shield the back four.5. SIASIA LEFT IT TOO LATE WITH HIS SUBSTITUTIONSThough he made a good decision in substituting Stanley Amuzie at the start of the second half, Samson Siasia like he did in the first leg waited too long before bringing in fresh legs in the game.The decision to keep Ahmed Musa and Aminu Umar on the pitch despite their poor performance when there were better options like Alex Iwobi and Moses Simon on the bench backfired at the end of the day.Read Also: Siasia Slams Super Eagles Defenders For Egypt Equaliser6. OVER-RELIANCE ON ODION IGHALOOdion Ighalo going into the fixtures against Egypt had failed to score in seven English Premier League games for Watford and only scored once for the Eagles in his last six games before the game against Egypt.That was a sign for coach Samson Siasia to call up a quality back-up for the 26-year-old that he could bring on when the going got tough.Siasia had in his arsenal Aaron Samuel who wasn’t fully fit and Fanendo Adi who was in the team for the first time.Ighalo was a shadow of himself in both fixtures and he didn’t force any crucial save from the Egyptian goalie in 180 minutes which is a cause for worry going forward.7. PRESSURE ON SIASIA TO GET EAGLES JOB PERMANENLYAfter impressing his handlers with the U-23 job, Samson Siasia allowed himself to be caught up with the pressure of being named the Eagles boss on a permanent basis.So he made some poor decisions, including bringing in too many players from the U-23s who lacked the needed experience to see off Egypt over two legs to qualify for the 2017 Nations Cup.8. SIASIA’S HARD LUCKTwice coach Samson Siasia has taken over from two of his team-mates (Austin Eguavoen in 2011 and (Sunday Oliseh 2016) and failed to qualify for a major tournament.His teams have played decent football but have been rather unlucky. A last-minute equaliser to Egypt in Kaduna, where Victor Moses had a shot cleared off the line, was probably the moment that ultimately eliminated the Eagles.9. FOUR MATCHES, THREE DIFFERENT COACHESStephen Keshi started the qualifiers as head coach, while Samson Siasia ended it. In between, the Eagles had Sunday Oliseh as head coach. These frequent change of coaches meant the line-ups constantly changed as each coach brought in his own men. The changes sometimes led to quality players being dropped for favoured but less talented players, changes in systems, formations and tactics.These changes ended up being detrimental to the team.10. NIGERIA’S POOR AWAY RECORDThe foundations for the Super Eagles’ failure were laid in their first qualifier. In Sunday Oliseh’s first match, the Eagles struggled against Tanzania in Dar Es Salaam and were lucky to escape with a draw.As they were drawing in Tanzania, their major rivals Egypt were spanking Chad away from home, laying down a marker. In the end, Nigeria got a paltry one point from two away matches as their dreams went up in smoke.[LINK]

SAD, SAD DAY FOR NIGERIAN FOOTBALLBy Lolade AdewuyiThe Super Eagles lost to the Pharaohs in Alexandria and will now miss a consecutive Africa Cup of Nations tournamentGOAL COMMENT By Lolade Adewuyi Follow on Twitter Nigerian football plumbed new depths on Tuesday as the Super Eagles failed to qualify for the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations after losing 1-0 to Egypt in Alexandria.Ramadan Sobhy scored the lone goal to send the Pharaohs to Gabon and consign the Super Eagles to missing another tournament after the failure of 2015.The Eagles, under the tutelage of Samson Siasia looked better organized than the previous game in Kaduna but fell to a more compact side in the Pharaohs.Despite all their possession, there was a lack of cutting edge as the hosts blocked out their attacking forays and tactically avoided giving away any fouls.While the Egyptians have just qualified for their first Afcon since 2010, Nigeria will need to ask questions about where it all went wrong.Reigning champions of Africa at U20 and U23, double world champions at U17, there is surely no shortage of talent for the Nigerian senior national team.So why have we failed to reach two consecutive Africa Cup of Nations tournaments and three of the last four?Nigeria’s fate was sealed after the withdrawal of Chad from the qualifying campaign which created a situation where only one team could qualify, as against the original scenario where the second-placed team could go through if it amassed enough points to finish as one of two best second-placed teams.One of the biggest problems was self inflicted. In all the four matches the Super Eagles have played, there were three different coaches in charge of the team – Stephen Keshi, Sunday Oliseh and Siasia.The Nigeria Football Federation’s changing of coaches and the infighting which led to loss of focus under the watchful eye of Mr Amaju Pinnick is one of the causes of our downfall.It is a shame that under Mr Pinnick, Nigeria has failed to qualify two straight times for the Afcon. Twice!In a sane country, Mr Pinnick would announce his resignation and other key members of the NFF would follow suit in order to take the blame for the situation at hand.However, if one can predict their reaction, they will attempt to shift the blame on every other person but themselves.While Mr Pinnick has spent so much money on training back room staff and former players who have had nothing to do with our teams, flying to Europe and back, coaches across the entire national teams as well as players have been regularly owed salaries and bonuses. Yet he wants to hire a European as coach of the Super Eagles.When Mr Pinnick was elected president of the NFF in acrimonious circumstances in 2014, Nigeria had just returned from the World Cup where it reached the Round of 16 and was adjudged the 16th best football playing nation in the world.While Algeria, a fellow African side that reached the same stage in Brazil, have continued to build on that feat and now look unbeatable, we have regressed and consistently dropped below accepted standards.While our boys have shed their sweat and blood to protect our colours, our football administrators seem to wallow in the splendour of underachievement.Once again we will watch the 16 best teams in Africa file out in Gabon in January without our green and white flying at the tournament.We will be onlookers as other teams jostle for the title that our boys lifted in 2013, a moment of great triumph for our nation.We will watch on our TV screens as other young men do their nations proud while ours regret not qualifying.It is a sad, sad day for Nigerian football. [LINK]

Nwabuoku sure of AWCON success [LINK] Super Falcons skipper Evelyn Nwabuoku says that her team will go all out to retain the AfricaWomen’s Cup of Nations trophy when thecompetition kicks off in Cameroon next month. Nigeria, hosts Cameroon and six other countrieswill do battle for Africa’s crown in women'sfootball from 19 November to 3 December in thecities of Yaoundé and Limbe. The Super Falcons are the defending champions of the competition, having won it in 2014, defeating Cameroon 2-0 in the final. Nwabuoku, who now plays for French side EnAvant de Guingamp, says that the team aredetermined to retain the crown to make up forthe disappointment of missing out on Rio 2016. “We have been talking to ourselves and we have vowed to make our fans happy and make up for the disappointment of not qualifying for the Olympic Games,” Nwabuoku told supersport.com. “The team has started preparations already andwe (foreign-based players) will soon join the restof the squad for training ahead of thecompetition. “I must tell you that we are focused on one thing and one thing alone. We want to win the trophy, we want to make our fans happy. “Above all, we want to win for our coaches andmake them proud of us.” Nigeria are drawn in group B of the tournamentalongside Mali, Ghana and Kenya. Banyana wallop Egypt in friendly [LINK] Makhabane © Gallo ImagesBanyana Banyana beat Egypt 3-1 in an entertaining friendly international match playedat Dobsonville on Saturday afternoon. Goals from Mamello Makhabane, Refiloe Jane and substitute Shiwe Nogwanya ensured coachDesiree Ellis began her coaching tenure with animpressive result. Yet, with good finishing Banyana Banyana couldeasily have routed their North African opponentsas they spent most of the afternoon camped inEgypt’s half but had a solitary goal to show fortheir effort in the first opening 45 minutes. But signs that this Banyana Banyana side has the potential to do well at the CAF Women's Afcon championships in Cameroon that begin next month, are there for all to see. Andisiwe Mcgoyi could have given BanyanaBanyana an ideal start in the opening minutesbut she fluffed an open chance after a cross from the left. However, Banyana Banyana were finally rewarded in the 30th minute when Makhabane slotted home a penalty after an Egyptian defender had committed a foul in the box. But Banyana’s joy were short-lived moments after the break when Noha Tarek fired home a low shot that gave Andile Dlamini no chance in the very first minute of the second half. That goal gave Ellis’s charges a wake-up call and they again rallied forward in numbers but failed to convert several chances that came their way. But the industrious Jane was never going to bedenied her moment of joy when she made a maze run through a number of Egyptian defenders before slotting home. It was a brilliant solo goal that lit up Dobsonvillestadium and Egypt were to be on the back footfor the rest of the game. Moments after her goal, Jane tried an audaciousshot from outside the box, but her attempt hitthe crossbar with the Egyptian goalkeeper MahaEl Demerdash stranded. Subsitute Shiwe Nogwanya then made it 3-1 forBanyana Banyana with almost the very last kick of the match as the hosts romped home 3-1. Source: [LINK]

Swedish-Based Stars Chikwelu, Okobi & Ikidi Happy To Represent Nigeria At AWCON [LINK] Three Swedish-based Nigerian stars, who play in the top league Damallsvenskan, are set to represent the Super Falcons at the 2016 Africa Women Cup of Nations in Cameroon next month. They include Faith Ikidi (Piteå), Rita Chikwelu (Umeå IK) and Ngozi Sonia Okobi (Vittsjo), and the trio expressed their happiness at being called to the national team. Rita Chikwelu was out in the international wilderness until she was invited to the Super Falcons squad that tackled Senegal in April. “I’m very happy to have the opportunity to play with the Super Falcons again. It is a great honor for me. For various reasons I have not had the chance to play in the National Team since 2012 in the Nations Cup, except for two qualifying matches against Senegal in April. “We will have a good team traveling to Cameroon, I know our coaches will prepare the team and the players in the best way for the tournament. “We professionals abroad have been playing a long season and we are all in great shape,” Chikwelu told allnigeriasoccer.com. She added : “Faith Ikidi has as usual had a very good season in Piteå as a central defender, Okobi has trained hard and played many good matches. “I believe in our team and it’s a good mix of players from Nigeria and professionals. ” In Sweden, the Nigerian players in Damallsvenskan are: Faith ikidi (Piteå), Rita Chikwelu (Umeå IK), Sonia Okobi (Vittsjö), Josephine Chukwunonye (Vittsjo), Ogonna Chukwudi (Orebro) and Sarah Michael (Orebro). All the players are important for their teams and Nigerians should all be proud of them. Rita Chikwelu had again a very good season. Her team Umea has been hit by injuries but Rita has carried the team on her shoulders. She has been one of the best midfielders in Damallsvenskan this year. Faith Ikidi was voted Defensive Player of the Year 2015 in Sweden, a prize that she could have had even several times before. She has caught the eyes of many in her games and is a role model for many Swedish footballers. Okobi has worked hard in the midfield in a new tough league. Her physical status has never been better and her great technical skills are improving. Source: [LINK]

AWC Title Won't Elude Nigeria,Omagbemi Promises Super Falcons coach, Florence Omagbemi, haspromised that the team would do everythingpossible to retain the African Women Championship (AWC) title in Cameroun. For the first time since the AWC started in 1998, the Issa Hayatou country is playing host to the championship, which Nigeria had hosted on three occasions, 1998, 2002 and 2006. The Falcons have won the title seven times (nine times overall), including their triumph in Namibia two years ago. The US-based Omagbemi, who captained theSuper Falcons for 14 years, winning the title onfive occasions (1991, 1995, 1998, 2000, 2002), told The Guardian that she would use Cameroon 2016 to announce her arrival as head coach. She said that all invited home-based playerscurrently battling for shirts in the Abuja camphave shown signs of determination, adding thather squad for the championship is graduallytaking shape. Omagbemi revealed that she was in constanttouch with all the invited professional players,saying: "I speak with them on daily basis andthey are eager to join us as quickly as possible." She waved aside media reports that the playerswere threatening to boycott the AWC Championship in Cameroun over the inability ofthe Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) to settletheir allowances for the qualifier against Senegal. "Someone told me about the report but there isnothing of such in our camp. I am sure somepeople just want to distract us but we will notallow that," Omagbemi said. Meanwhile, all invited foreign-based players have been given up till November 7 to report to camp in Abuja or forget the championship. Omagbemi is taking charge of the team alongside former goalkeeper, Ann Chiejine and ex-captain, Perpetua Nkwocha. The 2016 AWC will run from November 19 toDecember 3, with the Super Falcons pitchedagainst their arch-rivals, the Black Queens ofGhana, in Group B, which also has Kenya andMali.The hosts, Lionesses of Cameroun, are in Group A with South Africa, Zimbabwe and Egypt.Source: [LINK]

main_content:
Thread Title: Taiwo Awoniyi Bags Postgraduate Diploma In Football Directorship

Main Post: Taiwo Awoniyi has earned a diploma in global football sports directorship from the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Business School in the UK. The Ilorin-born striker was part of the initiative’s 2026 cohort and graduated on Monday. He had previously acquired a degree in business management from Buckinghamshire New University, Wycombe, UK, in 2022.According to the institution’s website, the global football sports directorship is a postgraduate diploma, with Andoni Zubizarreta, former Manchester City sporting director, and Les Reed, former vice-president of Southampton FC, as programme coordinators.“This programme aims to provide aspiring sporting directors with specialised training in the most complex and technical subjects that have never been covered in any training programme previously. Its ultimate goal is to prepare future sporting directors for the challenges that the football industry presents on a global scale,” the programme summary reads.Awoniyi has spent over four years in the UK since joining Nottingham Forest for a then-club-record £17.2 million.He moved to Coventry City last month for a reported fee of £17 million. The 29-year-old’s early days at his new club have been unimpressive, and he was sent off last weekend in their 5-0 loss to Brighton in the English Premier League (EPL).[LINK]

The tournament is being played across four Polish host cities: Bielsko-Biała, Katowice, Łódź and Sosnowiec. title: Conor Benn Releases First Statement After Ryan Garcia Loss
main_content:
Thread Title: Conor Benn Releases First Statement After Ryan Garcia Loss

Main Post: Conor Benn has broken his silence following his devastating loss to Ryan Garcia and revealed that he plans to step away from boxing for some time.Benn challenged Garcia for the WBC welterweight title on Saturday, but the fight quickly turned into a nightmare for the British boxer. Garcia stopped Benn in the second round, ending their long-running rivalry and handing him the first knockout loss of his professional career.Now, Conor Benn releases first statement since the defeat, and the former welterweight contender has made it clear that he wants to spend some time with his family before deciding what comes next.“If you’d asked the 19-year-old version of me whether I thought I’d be standing here ten years later, having lived through everything I have, I’d have told you that you were crazy.“I train hard. I sacrifice. I’ve given this game 110% every time I’ve stepped through those ropes. I’ve wanted to give people unforgettable nights and entertain. That’s what this has always been about for me.”“People spend their hard-earned money to come and watch guys like us fight. I’ve never taken that for granted. I’ve always wanted to be a servant of the public and give everything I have when it matters.But giving everything comes at a cost."And the people who have paid that cost more than anyone are my family and my kids. They’ve sacrificed time with their Dad so I could chase this dream. They’ve had to share me with this sport their entire lives.“So when people ask me what’s next for Conor Benn, right now the answer is simple. Time with my kids.”Benn also thanked the fans who travelled to Las Vegas and stayed up to watch the fight, despite the disappointing result.“Fight fans, thank you. Those who travelled to Vegas, those who stayed up until the early hours. I will never take your support for granted, especially on those nights things don’t go to plan.”The loss came after Benn entered the fight with plenty of momentum. He had picked up impressive victories over Chris Eubank Jr. and Regis Prograis before facing Garcia, but he struggled to match Garcia’s speed and aggression.Garcia capitalized on those problems and stopped Benn in the second round, putting a decisive end to their rivalry.The defeat also marked Benn and Garcia’s Zuffa Boxing debuts under Dana White’s new boxing promotion, adding another layer to what was already a highly anticipated matchup.Despite the setback, Benn’s career is far from over. The second-generation boxer remains one of Britain’s biggest names in the sport, but for now, he appears more interested in stepping away from the ring and spending time with his children.Benn is the son of former two-division world champion Nigel Benn and has built much of his career around the rivalry with fellow second-generation boxer Chris Eubank Jr. The pair split their two fights in 2025.For now, however, Conor Benn releases first statement with no clear answer about his next fight. After years of training, sacrifice and putting boxing ahead of almost everything else, the 29-year-old appears ready to put his family first.
