title: 5 Coaching Principles Zorawar Kohli Swears By
main_content:
Thread Title: 5 Coaching Principles Zorawar Kohli Swears By

Main Post: Football coaching is often reduced to drills, formations, and matchday instructions. But for Zorawar Kohli, the real work happens long before a whistle is blown. Over years of working with players at different stages of development, he's built a coaching philosophy around a small set of principles he returns to again and again — ideas that shape not just how his teams play, but how his players grow as people.Here are five principles that define his approach.1. Character Comes Before SkillZorawar Kohli believes technical ability can always be taught, but discipline, humility, and work ethic are far harder to instill once a player reaches a certain age. That's why character-building sits at the center of his coaching, not on the sidelines of it.Why This MattersPlayers with strong character adapt faster to setbacksDiscipline off the field often shows up as consistency on itTeams built on trust and accountability outperform teams built on raw talent aloneFor Kohli, a player who shows up early, listens actively, and takes feedback without ego is already ahead — regardless of their current skill level. Technical training is layered on top of that foundation, not used as a substitute for it.2. Every Player Develops on a Different TimelineOne of the most repeated lessons in Kohli's coaching sessions is patience — both from the coach and the player. He resists the temptation to compare players against each other, especially at younger age groups where physical and mental development varies widely.How He Applies ThisIndividualized feedback instead of blanket instructions for the whole squadTracking a player's progress against their own baseline, not their teammates'Avoiding early labels like "not talented enough," which can shape a player's confidence long-termThis principle is especially important in youth football, where a late developer can easily be written off too soon. Kohli's approach gives players room to grow without the pressure of constant comparison.3. Game Intelligence Matters as Much as Physical SkillSpeed, strength, and technical skill will only take a player so far. Kohli places heavy emphasis on decision-making — reading the game, anticipating movement, and understanding space — as a core part of training, not an afterthought.Building Game IntelligenceSmall-sided games that force quick decision-making under pressureVideo analysis sessions to help players understand positioning mistakesEncouraging players to explain their own decisions during training, not just execute instructionsHe often points out that two players with similar physical ability can have very different impacts on a match, and the difference usually comes down to awareness and decision-making rather than raw athleticism.4. Pressure Should Be Practiced, Not AvoidedRather than shielding players from high-pressure situations, Kohli builds pressure into training deliberately. He believes players who only experience pressure for the first time on matchday are set up to struggle.Practical Ways He Does ThisSimulating scoreline pressure during practice matchesSetting up drills with time constraints and consequences for mistakesEncouraging players to talk through nerves rather than suppress themThis principle extends beyond the pitch. Kohli often works with young players on handling pressure from parents, peers, and their own expectations — treating mental resilience as a skill that can be trained, just like passing or shooting.5. Communication Is a Two-Way StreetPerhaps the principle Kohli talks about most is communication — not just giving instructions, but genuinely listening to players. He treats feedback as a dialogue rather than a one-directional flow of commands from coach to player.What This Looks Like in PracticeRegular one-on-one check-ins outside of group trainingAsking players what they think went wrong before offering his own analysisCreating an environment where players feel comfortable asking questions or disagreeing respectfullyKohli has noted that players who feel heard tend to take ownership of their development, rather than simply following instructions without understanding the reasoning behind them. This buy-in, he argues, is often the difference between a player who improves steadily and one who plateaus.Bringing It All TogetherNone of these principles function in isolation. Character shapes how a player responds to individualized feedback. Patience with development timelines allows game intelligence to be built gradually rather than rushed. Practicing pressure only works in an environment where communication is strong enough for players to be honest about their struggles.For Zorawar Kohli, coaching isn't about applying a rigid system to every player. It's about creating the conditions — patience, communication, mental resilience, and character — under which each player can develop in their own way and at their own pace.Why This Approach Stands OutMany coaching philosophies focus heavily on tactics and physical conditioning, treating the mental and personal side of development as secondary. Kohli's approach flips that emphasis. He sees tactical understanding as something that's absorbed more effectively once a player has the character, confidence, and communication skills to engage with it fully.This is particularly relevant in youth and grassroots football, where the gap between a player's potential and their eventual performance often comes down to factors outside pure skill — confidence, mindset, and the ability to handle setbacks.Coaches who adopt even a few of these principles often find that improvements in these behavioral areas carry over into performance on the pitch as well.Final ThoughtsZorawar Kohli's five principles — character first, individualized development, game intelligence, practiced pressure, and two-way communication — form a coaching philosophy that treats players as complete individuals, not just athletes executing a game plan. It's an approach that requires more patience and attention than a purely tactical system, but one that Kohli believes produces more well-rounded, resilient players in the long run.For anyone involved in coaching at any level, these principles offer a useful reminder: the fundamentals of good coaching often have less to do with the sport itself and more to do with how well you understand the people playing it.

title: It's 50 Years Since IICC And Rangers Dominated CAF Competitions (Videos)
main_content:
Thread Title: It's 50 Years Since IICC And Rangers Dominated CAF Competitions (Videos)

Main Post: It's 50 Years Since IICC Shooting Stars of Ibadan and Rangers International of Enugu Dominated CAF Club Competitions1975 to 1977 was the Nigerian Era in African club football.In 1975 Rangers International of Enugu got to the final of the African Cup of Champion Clubs, but lost to Hafia of Guinea.In 1976 IICC Shooting Stars of Ibadan defeated Tonerre Kalara of Cameroon to win the African Cup Winners Cup.In 1977 Rangers International of Enugu defeated Canon Yaounde to win the African Cup Winners Cup.In fact, IICC Shooting Stars of Ibadan played against Rangers International of Enugu in the semi-finals of the 1977 African Cup Winners Cup. It was dubbed the Brothers Clash.African Cup Winners Cup Final (1st leg): IICC Shooting Stars 4-1 Tonnerre Kalala | November 1976.Sunday, November 28th 1976. IICC Shooting Stars of Ibadan defeat the Cameroonian side Tonnerre Kalala of Yaounde by four goals to one in the first leg of the African Cup Winners Cup Final. Held at Nigeria's National Stadium in the Surulere district of Lagos, the lead proved to be an insurmountable one, and Shooting Stars became the first Nigerian team to win an African football club competition when they lost by a single goal in the second leg. Among the players are Segun Odegbami who scored the first goal for Shooting Stars and Tonnerre's Roger Milla, who would later become a World Cup hero for Cameroon. Source: Reuters. [LINK] 1) Chairman Christian ChukwuPhoto 2) Mathematical Segun Odegbami

Comments:

IICC Shooting Stars were also runners up in the African Cup of Champion Clubs (the forerunner of the African Champions League) in 1984 and 1996. They were beaten by Zamalek of Egypt in the final on both occasions.They won the first ever edition of the CAF Cup in 1992.They got to the semi-finals of the African Cup Winners Cup in 1977 and the quarter-finals in 1980.African Cup Winners Cup Final (2nd leg): IICC Shooting Stars 0-1 Tonnerre Kalala | December 1976Sunday, December 12th 1976. IICC "Shooting Stars" of Ibadan lost 1-0 away in the second leg of the African Cup Winners Cup final, but their home win a fortnight earlier made it 4-2 on aggregate. The Cameroon team, the defending champions scored a goal which the referee subsequently disallowed. But Roger Milla scored from a penalty in the 76th minute of play. But one goal wasn't enough and the cup was presented to Sam Ojebode, the captain of the Nigerian side by President Ahmadou Ahidjo. Source: Reuters News. [LINK]

CLASH OF THE BROTHERS,1977.(Igbos vs their Yorubas brothers)By Remigius Akinbinu.'Clash of the brothers'; that, exactly, was the way the Nigerian press tagged the tie, back then. It was the way they wanted Nigerians to see it regardless of which of the two major tribes involved you're from.But in truth and naturally so, vast majority of Igbos and Yorubas rooted for the club from their own side of the divide in a titanic clash that captured the attention of the entire country while it lasted.It was the 1977 African Cup Winners Cup first semi-final between Rangers International Football Club of Enugu and the Industrial Investment Credit Corporation (IICC) Shooting Stars Football Club of Ibadan.That time, I was only an 11-year-old boy in my first year in the secondary school but (without being boastful) with an unimaginable interest in the round leather game.In June that year, my father, a school teacher bought the family's first television set. It was black and white of 'National' brand. This kindled my interest in football the more because, from following via radio commentaries and newspapers, I graduated into watching live and repeat telecast of matches on NTV Ibadan. This afforded me the opportunity of watching continental club football and following the Super Eagles' Argentina '78 World Cup qualifiers against Ivory Coast, Senegal, Egypt and Tunisia on TV.In our house,that time, the clash -of-brothers tag actually played out for the Rangers/IICC tie as my immediate elder brother and my immediate younger brother,for reasons I found difficult to understand, were all out in support of Rangers while I, like virtually all other boys on the street (except my good friend, Christopher Ifeanyichukwu Okanu and his housemates) rooted for Shooting Stars. I still remember my elder brother, Basil, threatening to beat me if Shooting Stars managed to beat Rangers.The tension that gripped the Nation's football family before and after the first leg was made more intense by the boastfulness of the promoters and fans of the two top Nigerian clubs.Defending champions, IICC which the previous year became the first to win a continental trophy for Nigeria were asking Rangers fans to go and inquire about them from their quarter final victims, FC Stade de Abidjan while Rangers felt it was tougher for them getting rid of Senegal Police FC in their own quarter final tie.To qualify for the semi-final, IICC pulled up all the tricks in their Pandora box to overcome a two-nil deficit suffered in Abidjan to outscore Stade by three first half goals. A Garuba Umoru brace and a Segun Odegbami header sealed it for the Oluyole warriors at the Liberty Stadium Ibadan.The starting line-ups of IICC that year looked more like this; (1) Best Ogedegbe 2. Joe Appiah 3. Sam Ojebode (C) 4. Muda Lawal 5.Idowu Otubusin 6. Sam Asante 7. Segun Odegbami 8. Phillip Boamah/Nathaniel Adewole 9.Moses Otolorin 10. Garuba Umoru/Dauda Ladipo 11. Kunle Awesu.If IICC had it tough qualifying for the semis, Rangers literally went through hell before making it to the semis. The first leg which was played at the National stadium,Surulere Lagos was almost uneventful as it ended goalless as the team from Senegal 'packed the bus' and frustrated the Chairman Chukwu led side.In the 2nd leg played at the filled-to-capacity Sedar Senghor stadium in Dakar, the home crowd never bargained for what hit them for they had thought after holding Rangers to a draw in Lagos,they will easily trash the visiting coal city Boys.First half ended one-nil in favour of Senegal Police (who scored through a controversial penalty kick) and it remained so until the 75th minute or thereabout when Rangers struck.Coach Roberto had just replaced the injured Stanley Okoronkwo with Chimezie Ngadi who with his first touch of the ball raced past three Senegalese defenders before silencing the home crowd with a deft volley. Before the home team could come to terms with what hit them, Ngadi struck again when it was about five minutes to the end.Two-one it ended and all hell was let loose in Dakar. Rangers' players and officials were stoned and beaten by the disappointed Senegal Police FC supporters. Several players sustained various degrees of injuries and I can still remember Emmanuel Okala recounting his experience and claiming the stonning actually started before the final whistle as he tried to use the net as cover to no avail. An apologetic President of Senegal, Leopold Sedar Senghor (One of my favorite African poets) had to visit Nigeria to apologise to the then head of state, General Olusegun Obasanjo and the Nigerian people. Senegal Police FC was suspended from playing on the Continent for a number of years by CAF.The typical starting line-up for Rangers that year looked like this: (1) Emmanuel Okala 2.Charles Adimorah 3.Ignatius Ilechukwu 4. Christian Madu 5. Christian Chukwu 6. Nnamdi Anyafo 7. Stanley Okoronkwo 8.Ogidinma Ibeabuchi/Chimezie Ngadi 9. Emeka Onyedika 10. Alloy Atuegbu. 11. Nwachukwu Onyekwelo .The Nigerian National team, the Green Eagles was dominated by players from these two clubs. Coach 'Father' Tiko that year invited four each from the two clubs for the World Cup qualifiers. From IICC were Segun Odegbami, Mudashiru Lawal, Sam Ojebode and Best Ogedegbe. While Rangers had Christian Chukwu, Emmanuel Okala, Aloysius Atuegbu and Ignatius Ilechukwu invited.The typical starting line-up of the Green Eagles side which at the the National stadium surulere Lagos, beat Ivory Coast 4-0, beat Senegal 3-0, beat Egypt 4-0 and lost 0-1 to Tunisia in 1977 was as follows: 1. Emma Okala (Rangers) 2. Pat Ekeji (Vasco) 3. Sam Ojebode (IICC) 4. Muda Lawal (IICC) 5. Christian Chukwu (Rangers) 6. Godwin Odiye (National Bank) 7. Segun Odegbami (IICC) 8. Adokiye Amiesimaka (Sharks) 9. Thompson Usiyen (USA) 10. Aloysius Atuegbu (Rangers) 11. Godwin Uwelumo (ACB Lagos)The first leg of the clash of the brothers was played in Lagos and it ended goalless. The return leg two weeks later which was played at the Ahmadu Bello Stadium Kaduna also ended goalless. Allan Hawks-tutored IICC appeared to be the better side that day but couldn't score because of the water tight Rangers' defence marshalled by Chairman Chukwu who ensured that Nnamdi Anyafo man marked the dangerous Odegbami through out the game. I remember the words of Earnest Okonkwo the legendary radio commentator "Nnamdi 'the Policeman' Anyafo effectively policed Segun 'the mathematician' Odegbami."Rangers International won the penalty shoot-out that ensued 4-2 to qualify for the final of the 1977 African Cup Winners Cup which they won after beating Canon Sportive of Yaounde Cameroon 5-1 on aggregate.The first leg was played in Lagos and Rangers won 4-1 with goals from Christian Chukwu,Christian Madu (penalties) Alloy Atuegbu and Emeka Onyedika. Canon's only goal was scored by Eugene Imbida who also scored the indomitable Lions equalizer against Italy at Espana '82 World Cup.The return leg in Yaounde ended 1-1. Eugene Oley Oley put Canon up in the first half while Ibeabuchi silenced the Cameroonians with a back breaking equalizer in the 2nd half.That day, in Yaunde Cameroon, Enugu Rangers lifted the 1977 African Cup Winners Cup thereby becoming the second Nigeria club to do so after IICC which beat Zamalek of Egypt to emerge winners in 1976.(C) Remigius Akinbinu.Second picture from right to left) "Man Mountain" Emmanuel Okala", "Mathematical" Segun Odegbami, "Chairman" Christian Chukwu (Captain of the Green Eagles and Captain of Rangers International) and Sam Ojebode (Assistant Captain of the Green Eagles and Captain of IICC Shooting Stars).

Picture 1) The Head of State, Lieutenant General Olusegun Obasanjo, the Chief of Staff, Supreme Headquarters, Brigadier Shehu Musa Yar'Adua, the Captain of Rangers International, Christian Chukwu, the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, A.A. Fashina-Thomas, the Team Manager of Rangers International, Chief Egwu and Chief Alex Nwokedi (Chief Press Secretary to the Head of State).Look at the way General Obasanjo is looking up at Man Mountain Emmanuel Okala in the lower part of the picture.This was at State House, Dodan Barracks when Rangers International went to present the 1977 African Cup Winners Cup trophy to the Head of State.

Rangers also got to the quarter finals of the 1971 African Cup of Champion Clubs (the forerunner of the African Champions League). They got to the semi-final of the competition in 1976, 1978 and 1982.They got to the semi-finals of the CAF Cup in 2003 and got to the quarter-final of the Cup Winners Cup in 1984.African Cup of Champions Clubs Quarter-Final (2nd Leg): Rangers 2-1 Green Buffalos F.C. | Sept. 1975Saturday, September 27th 1975.Footage of Nigerian team Enugu Rangers defeating Green Buffalos of Zambia 2-1 in the second leg of a quarter-final match of the African Cup of Champions Clubs tournament.Rangers came from a goal down and went through to the semi-final having drawn 2-2 with their Zambian opponents two weeks earlier in Lusaka.The first goal of the match came in the 70th minute of the second half courtesy of the Buffalos skipper Lonesome Katiwa, who capitalised on a defensive error by Rangers captain, Christian Chukwu. But right-winger, Emeka Onyedika scored the equaliser a few minutes later. Foster Ikeagwu made it 2-1 in the 81st minute. [LINK]

African Cup of Champions Clubs Final (2nd Leg): Rangers 1-2 Hafia F.C. | December 1975Saturday, December 20th 1975.Hafia F. C. defeated Enugu Rangers 2-1 away in the second leg of the African Cup of Champions Clubs Final, making the aggregate score 3-1.A capacity crowd of 70,000 filled the National Stadium in Lagos to watch the match.Rangers took the lead after 19 minutes when inside-left Mathias Obianika scored from the penalty spot.Haifa's defence absorbed Rangers' pressure. and on occasion took the opportunity to turn defence into attack with a series of sweeping pick-up moves against the Rangers' goal.Haifa came close to scoring in the twenty-fourth minute, but Emmanuel Okala, the Rangers & Nigerian national goalkeeper, made a superb save to stop Ibrahim Sory Keita.The visitors began the second half by taking all the initiative in midfield with some top-quality attacking soccer. It was only thanks to the sterling efforts of goalkeeper Okala and captain Christian Chukwu that Rangers kept the score level.Haifa equalised in the 57th minute when Keita managed to put the ball past Okala. It gave the Guineans a 2-1 lead on aggregate.Rangers made two team changes, bringing on Francis Nwosu to replace Emeka Onyedika in attack, and Stanley Okonkwo as substitute for the injured Kenneth Ilodogwe. But the replacements did little to affect the match.With only minutes to go, Cherif Souleymane scored the goal that ensured Haifa's success. His penalty made the score 2-1. [LINK]

Canon Yaoundé vs Enugu Rangers 1977 | The Rained-Out African FinalA flooded pitch, a midnight flight, and a historic victory! Rangers' Midnight Flight: The Bizarre 1977 Cup Winners' Cup Final. Nigeria vs Cameroon 1977: The Unforgettable Flooded Football Final. In December 1977, the second leg of the African Cup Winners' Cup final between Cameroon's Canon Yaoundé and Nigeria's Enugu Rangers was played at the Ahmadou Ahidjo Stadium.The match was halted by an unusual, heavy downpour that completely flooded the pitch, forcing the game to be postponed until the following day.In a display of determination and caution, the Enugu Rangers refused to spend the night in Cameroon. Instead, the team made the extraordinary decision to fly back to Nigeria immediately and return the next day to play the match.When the game was finally played, it ended in a 1-1 draw. However, the Enugu Rangers secured the title on a dominant 5-2 aggregate score, thanks to their commanding 4-1 victory in the first leg in Nigeria. The cup was later presented by former President Ahmadou Ahidjo. [LINK]

title: Nigerian-American Ugo Ugochukwu Crowned 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champion
main_content:
Thread Title: Nigerian-American Ugo Ugochukwu Crowned 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champion

Main Post: Nigerian-American racing driver Ugo Ugochukwu has been crowned the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champion after finishing second in the final race of the season in Madrid, Spain.The 19-year-old secured the championship on Sunday at the newly built Madring circuit, driving for Campos Racing, and became the first American to win the FIA Formula 3 title.Nigerian-American racing driver Ugo Ugochukwu has been crowned the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Champion after finishing second in the final race of the season in Madrid, Spain.The 19-year-old secured the championship on Sunday at the newly built Madring circuit, driving for Campos Racing, and became the first American to win the FIA Formula 3 title.Ugochukwu entered the final race level on points with British driver Freddie Slater after a dramatic championship battle throughout the season.While Finland’s Tuukka Taponen won the Madrid Feature Race, Ugochukwu’s second-place finish was enough to secure the title. Slater finished eighth, leaving Ugochukwu 14 points clear at the top of the championship standings.Who is Ugo Ugochukwu?Born in New York, Ugochukwu is a Nigerian-American racing driver who has risen through the junior single-seater ranks with ambitions of reaching Formula 1.He previously belonged to the McLaren Driver Development Programme, making him one of the young drivers identified by the British Formula 1 team as a potential future star.His 2026 campaign was contested with Campos Racing in FIA Formula 3.Ugochukwu began the season strongly, claiming his maiden Formula 3 victory in the Melbourne Feature Race in March.He later added another victory at Silverstone, where he dominated the Sprint Race by winning by 17 seconds.A dramatic title fightUgochukwu’s championship success was not straightforward.British driver Freddie Slater took the championship lead after the Budapest round in July, where he defeated Ugochukwu in the Feature Race and opened an eight-point advantage going into the summer break.The title race went down to the final weekend in Madrid.Before the final round, Slater had a 15-point advantage over Ugochukwu. However, Ugochukwu produced a strong qualifying performance while Slater struggled in the opening session, setting up a tense finale.Ugochukwu ultimately delivered when it mattered most, finishing second in the final race to overturn the deficit and claim the championship.FIRST AMERICAN FIA FORMULA 3 CHAMPIONThe victory makes Ugochukwu the first driver representing the United States to win the FIA Formula 3 Championship.He now joins a list of former Formula 3 champions who have progressed to Formula 1, including Oscar Piastri and Gabriel Bortoleto.His championship also represents another significant step in a career that could eventually take him to the highest level of motorsport.Formula 3 is regarded as an important pathway to Formula 2 and, ultimately, Formula 1.For Ugochukwu, the 2026 title caps a breakthrough season in which he transformed himself from a title contender into a champion.At just 19, the Nigerian-American driver now has an FIA Formula 3 championship on his résumé — and a potential future in Formula 1 ahead of him.Source:[LINK]

title: FIFA CAF Delegation Meet Shehu Dikko For Nigeria Football Reform Talk For Abuja
main_content:
Thread Title: FIFA CAF Delegation Meet Shehu Dikko For Nigeria Football Reform Talk For Abuja

Main Post: FIFA/CAF Delegation Don Meet Shehu Dikko As Dem Start Nigeria Football Reform Assessment For AbujaABUJA — National Sports Commission (NSC) on Monday, 14 September 2026, receive joint FIFA and CAF delegation for NSC Headquarters for Abuja.Di working engagement with NSC Chairman, Mallam Shehu Dikko, na di official start of di FIFA/CAF assessment team visit to Nigeria.Talk for di meeting focus on comprehensive reforms wey go reset Nigeria football ecosystem. Matters wey dem discuss include legal structures, governance, development, stakeholder collaboration and practical solutions wey go strengthen Nigerian football generally.Chairman Dikko talk say collaboration among Government, FIFA, CAF, Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) and other stakeholders dey very important if di game go grow for Nigeria.FIFA representative, Rolf Tanner, explain say di mission of di delegation na simply to listen to stakeholders through broad-based engagement, look di proposed reforms roadmap and assess di current situation before dem carry dia findings go back to FIFA leadership.Di engagement give room for dialogue and constructive talk on di way forward for Nigerian football. All di parties wey dey there agree say continued collaboration dey important for di interest of di game.During di visit, di FIFA/CAF team go still meet NFF administration, representatives of NFF members (State FAs, leagues, players, coaches, referees and others), plus other key stakeholders like former NFF Presidents and General Secretaries, club owners, sponsors and experts, so dat dem fit gather all relevant views and suggestions.FIFA go hold final technical meeting with NSC representatives on Tuesday, 15 September 2026, to close di visit.READ MORE STORIES @[LINK]

title: Tom Aspinall Vacates Heavyweight Title Amid Ongoing Eye Injury Nightmare
main_content:
Thread Title: Tom Aspinall Vacates Heavyweight Title Amid Ongoing Eye Injury Nightmare

Main Post: Tom Aspinall has officially stepped away from the UFC heavyweight throne, bringing months of uncertainty surrounding his future to an end.The British star announced that he has vacated the title due to ongoing eye complications that have prevented him from receiving medical clearance to compete. The decision comes nearly a year after his heavyweight title defense against Ciryl Gane ended in a no contest following a series of eye pokes that left Aspinall dealing with serious health issues.The news marks a significant moment for the heavyweight division, with Tom Aspinall vacates heavyweight now becoming one of the biggest stories in MMA.In a statement shared on social media, Aspinall explained that despite exhausting every available option, his recovery remains incomplete."Anything you read in the media is simply noise. People are creating their own narratives. This is the truth," Aspinall wrote. "Ongoing complications with my eyes mean I cannot get medically cleared to fight right now. I've had multiple surgeries, accidents and infections, and done everything possible to get back to competing."Aspinall revealed that he had previously agreed to a fight date and had returned to sparring while preparing for a comeback. However, another accident caused additional damage to his right eye, forcing him back to the sidelines."I had previously agreed to a fight date and was back sparring, feeling great and ready to compete when an accident caused further damage to my right eye. This means more time away from the sport, and right now, the timing of my return is unclear."The former champion also addressed questions surrounding his prolonged silence, explaining that he chose to follow medical advice and work closely with the UFC throughout his rehabilitation process."I know there have been questions about why I've been quiet. I've always followed the advice of the UFC and focused on my recovery while we've tried to make this happen."Rather than continue holding up the division, Aspinall decided it was time to relinquish the belt and allow the heavyweight title picture to move forward."I've now made the decision to vacate the heavyweight title. I've asked the UFC to allow me to make this statement because I don't want to hold the heavyweight division up."I know what it's like to have your career put on hold and I want the other fighters to have the opportunity to compete for the title."The 32-year-old also emphasized that the UFC remained fully informed throughout his recovery journey and had access to all of his medical records, tests and specialist consultations."The UFC and Hunter have been informed every step of the way and have seen the tests, procedures and medical information relating to my eyes."We have worked closely with different doctors and specialists to try and make my return happen, but unfortunately, it's simply not possible right now."While the decision was clearly emotional, Aspinall insisted that giving up the title does not signal the end of his fighting career."I'm absolutely gutted. I've chased this dream since I was 10 years old. I'm not done. Stepping away from the title is not stepping away from the sport or the dream. I'll continue doing everything I can to get healthy, get cleared and get back to competing as soon as possible."Aspinall also pointed to the circumstances that led to his current situation, noting that many of the issues he continues to face stem from fouls suffered inside the cage."What makes this particularly difficult is that many of the complications I'm dealing with are a result of fouls that changed the course of my career."Fighters rely on officials to enforce the rules and protect us in those moments, and it's hard to still be dealing with the consequences today."For now, the heavyweight division moves on without its champion. However, Aspinall remains determined to return once his health improves."Thank you to everyone who has supported me throughout this absolute nightmare. I'll be back as soon as I'm medically able to be."With Tom Aspinall vacates heavyweight title now official, the UFC heavyweight division enters a new chapter, while one of the sport's most talented big men continues the fight to save his career and eventually reclaim his place at the top.

Main Post: U20WWC: Falconets thrash New Caledonia 10-1 to reach Round of 16U20WWC: Falconets thrash New Caledonia 10-1 to reach Round of 16Nigeria’s Falconets produced a record-breaking performance at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, hammering New Caledonia 10-1 to secure their place in the Round of 16.The emphatic victory marked the biggest-ever win for Nigeria at the U-20 Women’s World Cup, as the Falconets finished second in Group F and advanced to the knockout stage.Nigeria took control of the match from the opening stages, scoring four goals in the first 27 minutes.Ramotalahi Kareem opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 17th minute before Rebecca Adegbemile doubled the advantage two minutes later.Janet Seimeyeha Akekoromowei added a third in the 23rd minute, while Kareem struck again in the 27th minute to give Nigeria a commanding 4-0 lead.The Falconets continued their dominance after the break, with Winner Onajite David making it 5-0 in the 60th minute.Kareem completed her hat-trick four minutes later, before Tosin Rafiu added another in the 70th minute.Adegbemile scored her second of the match in the 74th minute, while David added two more goals in the 75th and 90+4th minutes to complete her hat-trick.New Caledonia managed a consolation goal through Joceline Kourevi in the 89th minute, but Nigeria had already established an unassailable lead.The final whistle confirmed a 10-1 victory for the Falconets, with three Nigerian players finishing the match with multiple goals.Kareem and David both registered hat-tricks, while Adegbemile scored a brace.The result also confirmed Nigeria’s progression to the Round of 16, with the Falconets finishing second in Group F.Mynd44 mukina2 honeric01 [LINK]

title: 1xcup 2026 Draw: Adedapo Reveals Over 30 Players Have Progressed To Pro Football
main_content:
Thread Title: 1xcup 2026 Draw: Adedapo Reveals Over 30 Players Have Progressed To Pro Football

Main Post: Dimeji Adedapo, General Manager of 1xCUP Nigeria, has revealed that more than 30 players who featured in previous editions of the grassroots football tournament have progressed to professional clubs in Nigeria, other African countries and Europe.Adedapo made the disclosure in Lagos while speaking at the 1xCUP 2026 final group-stage draw, where 24 teams were drawn into six groups as the race for the competition’s ₦20 million total prize pool entered its decisive phase.The draw, held at The Providence Hotel, Ikeja GRA, marked another milestone in the fourth edition of the competition, which began with 100 grassroots teams battling for 24 places in the group stage.The group-stage matches are scheduled to begin on Tuesday, September 15, and run until October 8, with the grand final set for October 31 at Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Lagos.For Adedapo, however, the competition represents more than the pursuit of trophies and prize money.He said 1xCUP was created in 2023 as a way for 1xBet to give back to society while providing talented young footballers with an opportunity to showcase their abilities.“This competition started in 2023 as an experiment by the brand 1xBet, and it is an answer to: what can we give back to the society where we operate?” Adedapo said.He explained that the organisers noticed the abundance of young football talents across Lagos and decided to create a platform where they could be seen by a wider football audience.“We saw that there are lots of young guys out there who have this talent to play football. We see them every day and we decided: let’s create the platform for them to showcase their talents, and whatever happens next is fine,” he said.According to Adedapo, the initiative has recorded significant progress since its launch, with more than 30 players from previous editions now playing professional football.“We have over 30 players that have played in the 1xCUP playing in the professional league, either in Nigeria, Africa or Europe. For us, it has been a success,” he said.From ₦1m Prize to ₦20mAdedapo recalled that when the competition started in 2023, it was designed as an experiment with a ₦1 million grand prize.The inaugural edition took teams across different locations in Lagos, including Ikorodu, Epe, Badagry and Oshodi, before Shomolu Bariga FC emerged as the first champions.He said the organisers increased the prize structure after witnessing the response to the competition and the quality of players participating.“In 2024, after we saw the reception of the competition by the teams and what these young talents can do, we upped the grand prize from ₦1 million to ₦20 million,” Adedapo said.The current prize structure provides ₦10 million for the champions, ₦5 million for the runners-up and ₦3 million for the third-placed team, with additional prizes for outstanding individual performances.These include awards for the Most Valuable Player, highest goal scorer, best goalkeeper and best coach, among others.Adedapo said the organisers also recognise discipline, with a prize for the most well-behaved team.Adedapo: ‘We Spend Months Preparing’The 1xCUP general manager also offered an insight into the scale of work required to organise the tournament, saying preparations typically take several months.“Putting this kind of event together is not easy. Every year, we spend three, four months to make sure we achieve it,” he said.According to him, the 2026 qualification round started on July 23 and ended on September 4, with 100 teams taking part over a 20-day period.Adedapo said the organisers have continued to improve the quality of the competition, particularly in the area of video production.He explained that the video content provides players with materials that can be presented to scouts and professional clubs.“We know that many of these young talents and grassroots football teams, when there’s an opportunity to sell their players, don’t have what to show to scouts,” he said.“But when you go to the 1xCUP Nigeria Bet YouTube platform, you can pick a lot of clips. We even do individual clips for fantastic players.”Adedapo Appeals to 24 Teams the 24 teams prepare for the group stage, Adedapo urged them to understand the value of the opportunity and cooperate fully with the organisers.He identified punctuality and team organisation as some of the major challenges encountered during previous editions.According to him, some teams have arrived late for matches despite receiving their schedules in advance, while others have struggled to present their full squads.He recalled instances where technical walkovers had to be awarded after teams failed to honour scheduled matches.Adedapo said such situations were particularly disappointing because substantial resources had already been committed to venues, logistics, officials, vendors and video production.“It is not encouraging. Teams should realise that the only thing they can give back to us in the competition is their cooperation,” he said.He stressed that the competition is completely free for participating teams.“It is a 100 per cent free competition. We are not taking registration fees from anyone. Even after the competition, if you win, you get ₦10 million without paying a dime, and they have a good platform — everything,” he said.Adedapo therefore appealed to the 24 teams that qualified for the 2026 group stage to respect the tournament’s rules and schedules.“I am using this opportunity to appeal to the 24 teams in this year’s competition to please adhere to time and enjoy the tournament,” he said.24 Teams Drawn Into Six GroupsThe draw produced six groups of four teams.Group A: Vido SC, Emiloju FC, JP Young Stars FC, BYT Academicals FC.Group B: NewHope Naija FC, Divine Praise FC, Kiraa FA, Crusaders FC.Group C: Ajuwa FC, Tonic FC, Joy Cometh FC, Mega 22 FC.Group D: 36 Lions, Ighalo Football Academy, Maryland United FC, Crystal FC.Group E: Inspire Sports Academy, Young Strikers FC, Dynamic FC, AMA Smile FC.Group F: Collins Edwin Sports Club, ECAs FC, Elite Stars FC, AUX FC.Under the competition format, the top two teams in each group will qualify automatically for the next round, producing 12 teams.They will be joined by the four best third-placed teams to complete the 16-team knockout stage.The draw ceremony was attended by Nigerian football legend Mutiu Adepoju, sports veteran Dimeji Lawal, sports analyst Biola Kazeem and other stakeholders from government, sports and youth development.Also present was Geraldine Ibeanusi, Managing Director of 1xBet Nigeria, who congratulated the 24 teams that made it through the qualification stage and urged them to approach the competition with determination, discipline and respect for their opponents.With the group-stage draw now completed, Adedapo said the focus would shift to ensuring that the latest edition continues the tournament’s record of identifying young footballers and providing them with opportunities to pursue professional careers.For the 24 teams, the journey now moves from qualification to competition, with the ₦20 million prize pool, the 1xCUP title and the possibility of attracting professional football opportunities all within reach.

Thread Title: Ezenwoke, Okafor, Amata Emerge Champions at 2nd Umudioka Open T/Tennis Tourney

Main Post: Ezenwoke, Okafor, Amata Emerge Champions at 2nd Umudioka-Awka Open Table Tennis ChampionshipBy Ikenna NwokediThe trio of Ezenwoke Ifechidere Greg-Michael, Sochima Okafor and Ruth Amata have emerged champions in the Under-13, Under-15 and Under-18 categories respectively at the second edition of the Umudioka-Awka Open Table Tennis Competition.The competition, which served off on Monday, 7th September, 2026, climaxed with a colourful closing ceremony held at the Ndi Ichie Hall, Umudioka Village, Awka.In the U-13 category, Greg-Michael defeated Akachukwu Ezigbo to claim gold, with Ezigbo settling for silver. Uchenna Ifeanyi and Odinaka Okafor won bronze medals.In the U-15 category, defending champion Sochima Okafor retained his title with a convincing win over Desmond Ugochukwu, who took silver. Victor Raphael and Mohammed Bello claimed bronze.In the U-18 category, Ruth Amata defeated Ifeanyi Nwosu to clinch gold, while Mezie Eze and Emmanuel Nwosu settled for bronze.The gold medalists received trophies, while all participants were presented with table tennis training kits, educational materials, medals and certificates of participation.Reacting after the event, the facilitator, Chief Anayo Obiakor, commended the teenagers for their impressive performances.Obiakor assured that the competition has come to stay and will be improved upon in subsequent editions.He thanked the sponsor, Chief Engr. Anene Ebeze, and supporters including Stadod Global Links, Platinum World Creation Ltd, Onyeka Investment Ltd, Dr. Tochukwu Ejikeme, Medical Director of King David's Specialist Hospital, Awka, Chief Okey Igbokwe and Chief Barr. Harris Eze, CEO of Awka Museum, for their support.He also eulogized the South-East Zonal Coordinator of the Nigeria Table Tennis Federation, Bonny Akunna, and the Anambra State Table Tennis Coach, Ogonna Ibeh, for their technical input towards the success of the championship.

Main Post: Kaduna State has recorded an impressive performance at the North-West Zonal Elimination of the National Intermediate Games, held from September 9 to 12, 2026 at Murtala Muhammed Square, Kaduna, securing qualification in six team-sport disciplines.The competition, hosted by Kaduna State under the administration of Governor Senator Uba Sani, CON, through the Ministry of Sports Development, brought together five North-West states: Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Sokoto and Zamfara.Kaduna finished first in Beach Volleyball (Male and Female), Volleyball Female, Handball Male, Cricket (Male and Female), Hockey and Basketball, while placing second in Volleyball Male.The strong performance underscores Kaduna’s growing strength in grassroots sports and the State Government’s commitment to talent identification, athlete development and welfare.Speaking on the achievement, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Sports Development, Mrs. Dorcas Inti Benjamin Tanko, commended Governor Uba Sani, CON, for his commitment to sports development, noting that his administration has strengthened sporting infrastructure and support for athletes and coaches.She highlighted the completion of the upgrade of Kaduna Township Stadium, the reconstruction of Ahmadu Bello Stadium, which will increase its capacity from 16,000 to 33,000 spectators, as well as the provision for performance allowances for athletes and coaches in the 2026 approved State budget, as major interventions supporting sports development.She said the investments are creating a stronger foundation for identifying, nurturing and developing young sporting talents, while improving the conditions for athletes and coaches to prepare and compete effectively.The successful hosting of the zonal elimination at Murtala Muhammed Square further reinforces Kaduna’s growing status as a regional sporting hub. title: Falconets Seek Redemption Against China In 2nd Match After Spain's Defeat.
main_content:
Thread Title: Falconets Seek Redemption Against China In 2nd Match After Spain's Defeat.

Main Post: Following their 2-0 defeat against Spain in their opening match of the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, Nigeria’s Falconets will seek redemption when they face China in their second Group F game on Thursday (today), PUNCH Sports Extra reports.The two-time silver medallists return to the Stadion Sosnowiec for the second time, knowing another defeat could severely dent their hopes of progressing to the knockout stage.China, meanwhile, are highly motivated after thrashing New Caledonia 5-0 in their opening game, a result that put them top of Group F ahead of 2022 champions Spain on goal difference.Nigeria and China have met twice previously at the FIFA U-20 Women’s. In 2006 in Russia, at the tournament where the competition was renamed the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup after the first two editions were staged as the U-19 World Championship, China defeated the Falconets 3-0 in a group-stage match at the Podmoskovie Stadium.In 2018 in France, a late own goal by a Chinese defender earned Nigeria a 1-1 draw in Dinan-Léhon, a result that sent the Falconets into the quarter-finals. Ahead of Thursday’s encounter, Falconets coach Moses Aduku remains confident his players can bounce back from their opening-day defeat to Spain.“We have put the match against Spain behind us and are focusing totally on the clash with China. The players are ready to come out stronger for the match against China,” Aduku said.A win against China today will brighten their chances of advancing from the group, as the runners-up in 2010 and 2014 will be aiming to go a step further in Poland and secure the country’s first-ever FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup title.The Falconets, Brazil and the United States are the only three countries to have featured in every edition of the tournament, following Germany’s failure to qualify for this year’s competition.[LINK] THREAD;"Nigeria lose to Spain in first game at U-20 women’s World Cup." [LINK] Falconets of Nigeria have lost 2-0 to Spain in their first match at the FIFA women’s Under-20 World Cup in Poland on Monday. In the Group F encounter at Sosnowiec Stadium, the reigning European champions swept aside the Nigerian ladies with a goal in each half, scored by Marisa Garcia and Alba Cerrato.Spain dictated the tempo from the start and, with the Nigerian players not pressing from the top, put together a passing move that ended with Garcia arriving in the six-yard box to slot home the cutback and take a 1-0 lead.The Moses Aduku ladies were well contained by Spain’s possession and aggressive pressing, and waited until the 37th minute for their first attempt on goal through Kafayat Mafisere; the midfielder shot wide from distance.Precious Oscar and Victory Lucky both came on at the start of the second half, but it was Spain that doubled their lead with the second goal in the 73rd minute, pouncing on a poor clearance. The Spaniards put together a three-pass sequence to reach the six-yard box where Cerrato steadied herself and slotted the ball into goalkeeper Christiana Uzoma’s near post to seal the well deserved victory.Spain are second in the group on inferior goal difference behind China PR, who won their opening fixture 5-0, and will face the Falconets in their second group match on Thursday.[LINK]

title: NFF Set To Name New Super Falcons Coach
main_content:
Thread Title: NFF Set To Name New Super Falcons Coach

Main Post: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) is expected to announce a new head coach for the Super Falcons on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, as preparations begin for the team’s 2028 Olympic qualifying campaign.The appointment has become a priority with Nigeria facing a crucial Olympic qualifier, according to a senior source at the National Sports Commission (NSC).“We have an important Olympic qualifier ahead, so we need a new coach, who will be announced any moment now,” the source told Punch.An NFF official also confirmed that the announcement was close but could not say whether the incoming coach would be formally unveiled on the same day.“The NSC is in charge, and I am not sure if there will be an unveiling, but an announcement is imminent,” the official said.The identity of the new coach has not been made public, although reports indicate that all necessary procedures for the appointment have been concluded.The development comes after the NFF and the NSC parted ways with Justine Madugu and his technical crew following the Super Falcons’ disappointing outing at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morocco.Nigeria progressed to the quarter-finals of the tournament but were eliminated after a 1-0 defeat to Cameroon. The loss also ended the Falcons’ hopes of securing a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.Following the setback, the football authorities intensified efforts to appoint a new coach capable of rebuilding the team ahead of the next major qualification challenge.Several names have reportedly been linked with the vacant position, including former Super Falcons coach Thomas Dennerby and Florence Omagbemi, who guided Nigeria to the 2016 WAFCON title.American coach Randy Waldrum has also been mentioned among the possible candidates, while former Nigeria assistant coach Imama Amapakabo has reportedly expressed interest in the position.The incoming coach will be expected to rebuild the squad and guide the Super Falcons through the 2028 Olympic qualifying campaign.Nigeria have not participated in the women’s football event at the Olympic Games since the 2008 edition in Beijing.[LINK]

title: From Grassroots To Pro Football: 24 Teams Enter 1xcup 2026 Final Battle
main_content:
Thread Title: From Grassroots To Pro Football: 24 Teams Enter 1xcup 2026 Final Battle

Main Post: The journey from grassroots football to the professional game will take centre stage on Friday as 24 teams that survived a 100-team field gather for the final group draw of the 2026 1xCup competition in Lagos.The draw, scheduled for 12 noon at The Providence Hotel, Ikeja GRA, will determine the groups for the next phase of the fourth season of the grassroots football tournament, with the surviving teams set to compete for the ultimate ₦20 million prize.Rather than simply being another football competition, the 1xCup has positioned itself as a platform for young players seeking an opportunity to move beyond grassroots football.Tournament management says more than 30 players from previous editions have progressed to professional clubs in Nigeria, other African countries and lower divisions in Europe, providing evidence of a pathway that extends beyond the competition itself.The 2026 edition began with 100 teams, but only 24 have made it through the qualification stage.Those teams will now be divided into six groups of four, with the group-stage matches scheduled to run from September 15 to October 8.The best-performing sides will subsequently advance to the knockout stage as the competition narrows towards the grand finale.The final is scheduled for October 31 at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Lagos, where the eventual champion will claim the ₦20 million prize.More than a trophyFor the young footballers involved, the competition offers more than the chance to win a major cash prize.The organisers say the central objective of 1xCup is to identify promising players at the grassroots level and create opportunities for them to attract the attention of professional clubs, scouts and other football stakeholders.The progression of more than 30 players from previous editions into professional football has consequently become one of the tournament's major talking points.The development also underscores the growing importance of structured grassroots competitions in providing talented players with visibility beyond their immediate communities.Adedapo to speak on the next phaseThe General Manager of 1xCup Nigeria, Dimeji Adedapo, will serve as the principal spokesperson at the draw.Adedapo, who has been involved in the tournament across previous seasons, oversees its coordination and works with participating teams, players, technical officials, contractors and sponsors.He is expected to speak on the group-stage format, the tournament's grassroots development objectives and plans to strengthen the pathway between grassroots football and professional clubs.Football heavyweights expectedThe event is also expected to attract prominent personalities from Nigerian football, sports, government and youth development.Former Super Eagles star Mutiu Adepoju, a 1994 Africa Cup of Nations winner and member of Nigeria's gold medal-winning team at the 1996 Olympic Games, is among the invited guests. Adepoju is also a LaLiga Ambassador.Other invited personalities include Nigerian sports veteran Dimeji Lawal and sports analyst and commentator Biola Kazeem, who has been involved in grassroots football.Representatives of the Lagos State Government are also expected, including Jubril Gawat, representing the Governor's Office in New Media/Digital Media.Other invited guests include Alabi Opeyemi, representing youth affairs; Folorunsho Michael, representing the Sustainable Development Goals; and Sandra Omoniyi, League Commissioner at Lagos Liga and Founder of Asem Sport Management.24 teams, one destinationFor the 24 teams that have made it through the qualification stage, the draw represents the beginning of a new challenge.They will discover their group opponents before embarking on a group campaign that will determine who remains in contention for the knockout rounds.With the group stage running from September 15 to October 8, every match will bring the teams closer to either elimination or the ultimate prize.The journey will culminate at Mobolaji Johnson Arena on October 31, when the final two teams meet for the 1xCup 2026 title.But while one team will eventually lift the trophy and collect the ₦20 million prize, the organisers believe the bigger victory will be measured by how many young footballers use the platform to take the next step in their careers.From 100 teams to 24, from grassroots pitches to a professional pathway, the 1xCup 2026 campaign is entering its defining phase.

Thread Title: The Renovation Of The Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium, Enugu (Photos, Video)

Main Post: Enugu Gov Begins Restoration Of Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium[LINK] pic.twitter.com/BZy9KtVC8z— Channels Television ([USERNAME]) September 3, 2026The stadium will now be an all-seater, all-covered stadium.Photo 1) How the stadium will look when the renovation is completed.Photos 2 to 4) How the stadium looked before the renovation.

Construction of the Liberty Stadium, Ibadan began in 1958 and it was opened in 1960 to mark Nigeria's independence. It was the biggest stadium in Nigeria at the time and major events like Dick Tiger's world title fights, were held there. It was built by the Western Region Government but it was later taken over by the Federal Government. President Goodluck Jonathan renamed it the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium in 2010.The Enugu Township Stadium was built and opened by the Railway Corporation in 1959. It was later taken over by the Eastern Region Government. The stadium was renovated in 1970 and it became the home of Rangers International football club. It was renovated again in 1986 and renamed the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium.The Ahmadu Bello Stadium was built by the Northern Region Government and opened in 1965.There were 4 national stadiums when I was a kid. These were ⚫️ The National Stadium, Lagos⚫️ Liberty Stadium, Ibadan⚫️ Ahmadu Bello Stadium, Kaduna⚫️ Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium, Enugu.These were the stadiums that the Nigerian national teams played their matches. They were the biggest and most prestigious stadiums in Nigeria.Then came democracy in 1999. Unlike military governments, civilian governments did not need to use sports to gain legitimacy.The civilian governments knew that they had enormous responsibilities and so they did not have any money to use to maintain these big national stadiums. Besides, the Abuja National Stadium was built.The 4 national stadiums fell into disuse. They were in bad states.The Federal Government developed a programme of transferring these stadiums to state governments. The Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium was transferred to the Enugu State Government.The Ahmadu Bello Stadium was transferred to the Kaduna State Government.There were plans to transfer the National Stadium to the Lagos State Government (the Fashola Administration expressed willingness to take it over), but there was a problem.The Federal Government wanted the Lagos State Government to pay it in order to take over the stadium. The Lagos State Government refused to pay. It believed that the stadium was in a very bad state and that it would be helping the Federal Government by fixing it. It could not pay the Federal Government and then spend more money to fix it.Today the National Stadium Lagos and the Liberty Stadium Ibadan (which President Jonathan renamed the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium) are in very bad shape.The Kaduna State Government has demolished the Ahmadu Bello Stadium in order to build a new and befitting stadium on the site.The Enugu State Government is currently upgrading the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium. They are going to make it an all covered stadium.This is why Rangers International is playing its home games at the MKO Abiola Stadium, Abeokuta.

Types of stadiums in Nigeria.Anybody that has lived in Nigeria automatically knows the various types of stadiums in Nigeria (that's why I said that those people are not being serious). In this post I will limit myself to the relevant types.A) Sports cities: There are many stadiums in Nigeria that are what I call sports cities. They have a main bowl that consists of a football pitch and an athletics track and they also have other sports facilities, most notably a sports hall that is used for basketball and other indoor sports and an aquatic centre.Some people complain about these sports cities because they do not understand why there's a track around the football pitch. They watch the English Premier League and other European football competitions and they don't see athletics tracks around the pitches and so they wonder why there are tracks around the pitches at these sports cities.This issue isn't new to me, but I assumed that everybody understood it, however, I discovered on Nairaland in the early 2010s that not everybody understands the issue.The answer is very simple. These sports cities were built by government. Governments want to develop multiple sports in order to improve the chances of their citizens winning medals at multi-sports events. They need to have the facilities in which to train these athletes. Some governments also hope to host events like the Nations Sports Festival, the National School Sports Festival, Youth Games, All Africa Games, Commonwealth Games, the Olympics, etc. It is more cost effective and efficient to build a sports city than to build separate football stadiums and athletics stadiums. This is the reason that governments build the sports cities. Track and Field Athletics was once Nigeria's second sport, it is the one sport that every school takes part in and there must be facilities to host such competitions.The football stadiums that you see being used in the English Premiership and similar competitions are owned by wealthy football clubs. They have no responsibility to develop track and field athletics and they want to ensure that their fans can get very close to the action by having the seats/stands very close to the pitch.Examples of sports cities include the National Stadium Lagos, the National Stadium Abuja, Liberty Stadium Ibadan, Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium Enugu and the Ahmadu Bello Stadium Kaduna.B) Single use stadiums: There are also single use stadiums in Nigeria. When I say "single use" I mean that the stadium comprises just a football pitch, although that same pitch can be used for association football, rugby and American football.Most of the single use stadiums are the older stadiums like the Onikan Stadium in Lagos, Sharks Stadium in Port Harcourt and the Kano Pillars Stadium. Most of these stadia are associated with a particular football club and it is not the club's responsibility to develop other sports like track and field athletics or swimming. Besides, most of these older stadia are smaller than the sports cities and there's no space to put an athletics track.C) Mini stadiums: Mini stadiums are very small stadiums that are designed to be used by a community. Most of these stadiums are not used by any professional sports team, rather they are used by the youths in the area.Mini stadiums are built to provide an outlet for youths in the area, so that they can hone their skills, to provide them with something to do and keep them away from crimes and other vices.Mini stadiums also serve as a community centre. They are a place where schools can hold their inter-house sports competitions, nearby companies can have bonding sessions, etc.A great example of a mini stadium is the Campos Square Mini Stadium. It was basically just a playground once upon a time. There were no stands and there was no grass (it was just sand). People played football there, it was used as a prayerground during Eid and some people had parties there. In 1987 a part of the square was partitioned off and converted into a school.However, Governor Babatunde Fashola converted it into a mini stadium with stands, an electronic scoreboard and an outdoor basketball court.Nowadays there are activities at the stadium every day. It is used by the Lagos State Government to train primary and secondary school students, teams of youths rent the stadium for their football matches and it was the site of the Channels Television primary school football competition.D) Playgrounds: What I call playgrounds are community sports facilities that have no stands, in some cases they have no grass, but they are used by youths in the area to play football in the evenings and at weekends. They are also used for social occasions like parties and for political gatherings. A good example of a playground is the old Campos Square.

Ordinarily, Enugu should have built a new stadium on the outskirts of the city rather than continuing to concentrate a major sports facility in what has effectively become downtown Enugu.The city has outgrown the current location of the sports complex. What may have been an appropriate site decades ago is no longer suitable for a modern stadium serving a rapidly expanding urban population. The present location offers little or no adequate space for vehicle parking, pedestrian circulation or crowd management. More seriously, in the event of a stampede or other major emergency, the lack of sufficient open space and escape routes could turn a potentially manageable situation into a serious public-safety disaster, putting not only spectators at risk but also the residential and commercial buildings immediately surrounding the facility.The problem becomes particularly obvious on match days. The large volume of vehicles and pedestrians leaving the stadium and emptying onto Ogui Road creates severe traffic congestion and places enormous pressure on an already constrained urban corridor. This kind of gridlock should not be an inevitable feature of match days in a properly planned and forward-looking city like Enugu.A modern stadium should be more than a football pitch surrounded by stands. Its location must take into account traffic management, parking capacity, pedestrian movement, emergency access, crowd safety, environmental impact and the future expansion of the city.Ideally, the state government should have relocated the facility to an area with sufficient land to accommodate these requirements. Centenary City, Emene, or the New Enugu axis would have been far more logical choices. Such locations would provide room for adequate parking, wider access roads, proper pedestrian infrastructure, emergency evacuation routes and future expansion, while significantly reducing the environmental and traffic pressures imposed on the existing Enugu urban core.Enugu is a city with a proud history of urban planning. Its sporting infrastructure should reflect the city it is becoming, not the city it was several decades ago.The issue is not simply where to put a stadium. It is whether we are planning Enugu for today, or building for the city we know it will become tomorrow.

title: Photos And Videos Of The Renovation Of Teslim Balogun Stadium, Lagos
main_content:
Thread Title: Photos And Videos Of The Renovation Of Teslim Balogun Stadium, Lagos

Main Post: The UAC Stadium in Surulere was the venue of many epic Principals Cup finals and Ramat Cup competitions in the 1970s and early 1980s.The Principals Cup was the competition between teams of male secondary schools in Lagos. It was a big deal in the 1970s and early 1980s. Matches were broadcast live on Radio Nigeria and teams seemed to represent more than their schools, they represented the communities that the schools were in. The CMS Grammar School team (Bariga Bombers) were like the national team of Bariga, the St Finbarr's team were the national team of Akoka, the St Gregory's team was the national team of Obalende, etc.The Ramat Cup (which was named after General Murtala Ramat Muhammad) was organised by the Youth Sports Federation of Nigeria (YSFON) and it was used to discover players for the national under 21 and under 16 teams.UAC Stadium was demolished in the mid-1980s and a new and bigger stadium was to be built on the site. It was to be called the Teslim Balogun Stadium.Construction of the Teslim Balogun Stadium began in 1987, during the administration of Governor Mike Akhigbe. However, the project stalled soon after due to the economic crisis of the 1980s. It was abandoned for decades.The project was revived by the administration of Governor Bola Tinubu. It was completed and commissioned in 2007, just before Tinubu handed over to Fashola.A lot of the facilities and design of the stadium are outdated. What is happening right now is an upgrade to bring it into the modern era.For example, only the State Box was covered originally. Now they are converting it into an all-covered stadium.There were no hospitality suites. Now hospitality suites are being created.It had no facade, but now a facade is being put in place.The flood lights were on poles that were outside the stadium, now they will be on the roof.Basically it was a 1987 type stadium and it is being converted into a 2026 type stadium.However critics have complained about the slow pace of work. The project started in 2024 and it has still not been completed.The government says that it will soon be completed and that it will host the Intermediate Games this month (September 2026). Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu inspected the site a few weeks ago and he has promised that it will be completed on time.This video of the stadium was shot five days ago. [LINK] of the stadium from 5 days ago.

Comments:

Getting set, Teslim Balogun Stadium. The work has gone far ahead of this, just showing you how it was when Governor [USERNAME] visited. [LINK] pic.twitter.com/sJK6bKDIw5— Jubril A. Gawat ([USERNAME]) September 3, 2026This is what the stadium looked like before the renovation.

The UAC Stadium in Surulere was the venue of many epic Principals Cup finals and Ramat Cup competitions in the 1970s and early 1980s.The Principals Cup was the competition between teams of male secondary schools in Lagos. It was a big deal in the 1970s and early 1980s. Types of stadiums in Nigeria.Anybody that has lived in Nigeria automatically knows the various types of stadiums in Nigeria (that's why I said that those people are not being serious). In this post I will limit myself to the relevant types.A) Sports cities: There are many stadiums in Nigeria that are what I call sports cities. They have a main bowl that consists of a football pitch and an athletics track and they also have other sports facilities, most notably a sports hall that is used for basketball and other indoor sports and an aquatic centre.Some people complain about these sports cities because they do not understand why there's a track around the football pitch. They watch the English Premier League and other European football competitions and they don't see athletics tracks around the pitches and so they wonder why there are tracks around the pitches at these sports cities.This issue isn't new to me, but I assumed that everybody understood it, however, I discovered on Nairaland in the early 2010s that not everybody understands the issue.The answer is very simple. These sports cities were built by government. Governments want to develop multiple sports in order to improve the chances of their citizens winning medals at multi-sports events. They need to have the facilities in which to train these athletes. Some governments also hope to host events like the Nations Sports Festival, the National School Sports Festival, Youth Games, All Africa Games, Commonwealth Games, the Olympics, etc. It is more cost effective and efficient to build a sports city than to build separate football stadiums and athletics stadiums. This is the reason that governments build the sports cities. Track and Field Athletics was once Nigeria's second sport, it is the one sport that every school takes part in and there must be facilities to host such competitions.The football stadiums that you see being used in the English Premiership and similar competitions are owned by wealthy football clubs. They have no responsibility to develop track and field athletics and they want to ensure that their fans can get very close to the action by having the seats/stands very close to the pitch.Examples of sports cities include the National Stadium Lagos, the National Stadium Abuja, Liberty Stadium Ibadan, Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium Enugu and the Ahmadu Bello Stadium Kaduna.B) Single use stadiums: There are also single use stadiums in Nigeria. When I say "single use" I mean that the stadium comprises just a football pitch, although that same pitch can be used for association football, rugby and American football.Most of the single use stadiums are the older stadiums like the Onikan Stadium in Lagos, Sharks Stadium in Port Harcourt and the Kano Pillars Stadium. Most of these stadia are associated with a particular football club and it is not the club's responsibility to develop other sports like track and field athletics or swimming. Besides, most of these older stadia are smaller than the sports cities and there's no space to put an athletics track.C) Mini stadiums: Mini stadiums are very small stadiums that are designed to be used by a community. Most of these stadiums are not used by any professional sports team, rather they are used by the youths in the area.Mini stadiums are built to provide an outlet for youths in the area, so that they can hone their skills, to provide them with something to do and keep them away from crimes and other vices.Mini stadiums also serve as a community centre. They are a place where schools can hold their inter-house sports competitions, nearby companies can have bonding sessions, etc.A great example of a mini stadium is the Campos Square Mini Stadium. It was basically just a playground once upon a time. There were no stands and there was no grass (it was just sand). People played football there, it was used as a prayerground during Eid and some people had parties there. In 1987 a part of the square was partitioned off and converted into a school.However, Governor Babatunde Fashola converted it into a mini stadium with stands, an electronic scoreboard and an outdoor basketball court.Nowadays there are activities at the stadium every day. It is used by the Lagos State Government to train primary and secondary school students, teams of youths rent the stadium for their football matches and it was the site of the Channels Television primary school football competition.D) Playgrounds: What I call playgrounds are community sports facilities that have no stands, in some cases they have no grass, but they are used by youths in the area to play football in the evenings and at weekends. They are also used for social occasions like parties and for political gatherings. A good example of a playground is the old Campos Square.

title: King Oyo: London-based Goalie, Kamurasi Chosen As Next Ruler Of Uganda Kingdom

Thread Title: King Oyo: London-based Goalie, Kamurasi Chosen As Next Ruler Of Uganda Kingdom

Main Post: The goalkeeper of a non-league side in London, SE Dons, George Kamurasi, has been chosen as the next king of the Tooro people in Uganda.At 36 years old, Kamurasi plays in the ninth tier of the English football and was selected by a committee to take over from his late cousin, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV.King Oyo, who was 34, passed away while undergoing treatment for cancer, leading the Tooro Kingdom into a transitional phase.Known as “Big G,” Kamurasi is a British citizen and currently serves as the captain of SE Dons in the Southern Counties East League Premier Division located in southeast London.He is recognized at his club for his enthusiastic and authoritative demeanor, with video evidence showcasing his intense team talks to fellow players.Despite being chosen as the next monarch, Kamurasi is said to be hesitant about leaving London, where he resides with his wife and son, to assume the royal role in Uganda.His selection has sparked mixed reactions in Uganda; some individuals appreciate his straightforward personality, while others question whether someone raised in the UK can truly represent the Tooro people.The funeral for King Oyo, who ascended to the throne at the tender age of three in 1995, is set to occur this weekend.Kamurasi hails from a distinguished royal lineage. His grandfather, King George Rukidi III, famously welcomed the late Queen Elizabeth during her visit to Uganda in 1954.In an unexpected turn of events, Kamurasi may miss the late king’s funeral due to a scheduling conflict with a cup match involving his football club.SE Dons participate in the Southern Counties East League Premier Division, which is positioned at Level 9 within the English football structure.Kamurasi now faces a huge decision between pursuing his life and football career in London or embracing his family’s royal duties in Uganda.[LINK]

title: NFF Reforms: Tinubu & FIFA Orders Comprehensive Reform For Nigerian Football
main_content:
Thread Title: NFF Reforms: Tinubu & FIFA Orders Comprehensive Reform For Nigerian Football

Main Post: President Bola Tinubu has ordered “comprehensive reforms” for Nigerian football. The directive could not have come at a better time. For years, the Nigeria Football Federation has been stuck in cycles of poor performances, crisis, litigation, and distrust. If we are serious about fixing the house, we must start with the foundation: the NFF Congress. Good that the National Sports Commission has got the nod from FIFA to set up an Interim Management Committee after the resignation of the Gusau-led board. There is now enough time to set our bed neatly for a proper respite. This must be the first job of the Interim Management Committee after FIFA’s nod this week.The Congress is the highest decision-making body of the NFF. It elects the President. It amends the statutes. It approves budgets. In short, whoever controls the Congress controls Nigerian football. That is why reforming its composition is not optional. It is urgent.The current Congress structure, with 37 FA Chairmen as a voting bloc, has created a culture of “delegate democracy” where loyalty is traded for development. One man, one vote, one state has produced 37 kingmakers and left the real stakeholders of the game as spectators.As stakeholders prepare their minds ahead of the reforms, here is a concrete proposal for a new NFF Congress that is representative, equitable, and development-focused. It reduces politics and increases expertise.To ensure legitimacy, the various associations and constituencies shall hold elections to provide representatives at least 60 days to the Congress to pick its representatives. This will guarantee transparency and give all stakeholders time to participate in the process.My opinion:The Old NFF Is Gone — So What Happens Next?Nigerian football has entered a new chapter following the major shake-up and reforms of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).But the biggest question now is: what happens next?Is this the beginning of a new era for Nigerian football, or will the same problems return under a different structure?What do you think about the NFF reforms? Share your opinion in the comments.[LINK]

title: Eguavoen Named Interim Super Falcons Coach Ahead Of Olympic Qualifiers
main_content:
Thread Title: Eguavoen Named Interim Super Falcons Coach Ahead Of Olympic Qualifiers

Main Post: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has appointed former Super Eagles head coach Augustine Eguavoen as interim coach of the Super Falcons ahead of their 2028 Olympic Games qualifying fixtures against Comoros in October.Eguavoen, popularly known as ‘Cerezo’, will take charge of the team on an interim basis as the search for a substantive head coach continues.The former Nigeria international brings considerable coaching experience to the assignment, having worked at the highest level of international football. He led the Super Eagles to a bronze medal finish at the 2006 Africa Cup of Nations in Egypt.Eguavoen will be assisted by Christopher Danjuma, the current head coach of Nigeria Women’s Football League side Nasarawa Amazons. Danjuma has extensive experience with Nigeria’s women’s national teams, including leading the Falconets at the 2024 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Costa Rica.Former Super Eagles goalkeeper trainer Olatunji Baruwa will serve as goalkeeper trainer. Baruwa has worked with several of Nigeria’s national teams, including the Super Eagles, CHAN Eagles, Flying Eagles and Golden Eaglets.Former Super Falcons defender and coach Ayisat Yusuf will also serve as one of the assistant coaches.Yusuf earned 68 international caps for Nigeria and represented the country at four Women’s Africa Cup of Nations tournaments, three FIFA Women’s World Cups and the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing.The 10-time African champions will begin their Olympic qualifying campaign in the second round against Comoros, with both legs scheduled for the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne-Remo on 9 and 13 October.The Super Falcons received a bye into the second round as one of the three highest-ranked teams in the qualifying competition. Comoros advanced after defeating Sudan 30-0 on aggregate.If they overcome Comoros, the Super Falcons will advance to the third round, scheduled for 23 February to 6 March, 2027, where they will face either the Democratic Republic of Congo or Morocco.A place in the fourth round would see Nigeria face either Tunisia, Senegal, Benin Republic or Mali between 4 and 12 October, 2027.The final round of the qualifying race is scheduled for 23 November to 4 December 2027. Nigeria could face one of Guinea, Cameroon, Democratic Republic of Congo, Côte d’Ivoire, Central African Republic, Algeria or Burkina Faso at that stage.[LINK]
