12 Types Of Verb Tenses And How To Use ThemWhat Is A Verb Tense? 12 Types Of Tenses Past Tenses Present Tenses Future Tenses Rely On Grammar CoachIf you’re familiar with basic English grammar, we bet you can describe a verb and perhaps name a tense or two. In the sentences the boy walks and the girl ran, the words walks and ran are the verbs.Did you also recognize that walks is in the present tense, or that ran is in the past tense? Whether you did or didn’t, we’re here to review verb tenses with you and also astound you with the fact that there are 12—count them, 12—verb tenses in all!What is a verb tense?Generally speaking, verb tenses identify the time period when an action occurs. The verb walks communicates not only how many people completed the action (it’s singular), but also when it occurred. In this case, the tense is present. The person walks right now.Interestingly, not all languages treat verb tenses the same way. In English, the ending on a verb communicates what tense it’s in. (Walk becomes walks and walked.) In some cases, an auxiliary verb (also known as a helping verb, like will or need) is required as well. In Chinese languages, for example, a verb doesn’t change its spelling depending on the tense. A separate word (or particle) is combined with the verb to explain when it occurred.12 types of verb tensesThe simple tenses (past, present, and future) are the most basic forms, but there are 12 major verb tenses in English in all. We’ll review the tenses here.Past tensesThe past tenses use verbs to say that something happened in the past, meaning any time before this moment right now. There are four variations of past tenses:Simple past: describes events that began and ended in the past.Past continuous: describes events that began in the past, continued for a length of time, and ended in the past.Past perfect: describes a past event that occurred before another past event.Past perfect continuous: describes an event that began in the past, continued for a length of time, and was in progress when another past event happened.Simple pastThe simple past tense describes events that have already happened and are completely finished. Most verbs can be made past tense by adding -ed, –d, or sometimes the variant –t at the end of a present tense verb, as in liked and watched.However, many irregular verbs have unique past tense forms. For example, go becomes went, and think becomes thought.Simple past is usually used to write about historical events, like so:Galileo observed the stars.In this example, the verb tense indicates that the astronomer Galileo completely finished the act of observing the stars at some point in the past.Past continuousThe past continuous tense describes an ongoing activity that occurred in the past. It is formed by combining the past tense verb to be (which must be correctly conjugated to agree with the subject) and the present participle of a verb (ending in –ing):The planet was moving along an elliptical orbit.In this example, the verb tense says that the planet began moving sometime in the past and continued to do so for a period of time (in the past).Establish the different times to use was vs. were so you won’t have any mistakes again.Past perfectThe perfect tenses involve more complex time relationships. They build upon simple tenses by combining a verb with has, have, or had.The past perfect tense, also called the pluperfect tense, describes a past event in relation to another event that occurs closer to the present. It is formed by combining had and the past participle of the verb.The girl bought the telescope her teacher had recommended to her.The girl bought (simple past) what the teacher had recommended (past perfect tense). One action occurred (had recommended) before the other (bought).Past perfect continuousThe past perfect continuous tense describes an ongoing action that—like the past perfect—was performed in relation to another event that occurs closer to the present. It is formed by combining had been with the present participle of the verb.He had been studying for his astronomy final when the doorbell rang.The above example uses the verb tense to indicate that he was studying for a length of time before another event (the doorbell ringing) interrupted or stopped his act of studying.Present tensesGenerally speaking, we use the present tenses to say that an event is happening right now in the present time. Like the past tenses, there are four variations of present tenses:Simple present: Describes an event as happening in the present.Present continuous: Describes an event as being in progress in the present and likely continuing into the future.Present perfect: Describes an event that occurred in the past but has some connection to the present.Present perfect continuous: Describes an event that began in the past but still continues to happen in the present.Simple presentThe simple present tense describes events happening now. It’s also useful for describing a direct action that’s not exclusive to the past or 4future.Sentences in present tense often have the most straightforward structure because they use the root form of the verb or a conjugation of the verb to be. The root form of the verb is the form you will find if you look up a verb in our dictionary.We often use the simple present tense to state facts:Cats eat mice and birds.In this sentence, the simple present tense is used to state the fact that cats regularly eat mice and birds.When you use the verb be in the simple present tense, it must agree with the subject of the sentence. For example:I am tall.You are my best friend.She is my older sister.We are hungry.They are late for work.Present continuousThe present continuous tense describes an ongoing activity that is happening now, in the present. It is formed by combining the verb to be and the present participle of the verb (ending in –ing):The baby is laughing at Shelly’s monkey puppet.In this example, the verb tense is used to state that the baby is currently in the process of laughing at Shelly’s silly puppet and will likely continue to do so for a while yet.Present perfectThe present perfect tense describes a past event that’s still happening in the present. It is formed by combining the word has or have (depending on the subject) with the past 5participle of the verb.Let’s look at this sentence:The baby has played this game before.In this example, the verb tense states that a past event is related to the present. In this case, the sentence is saying that the baby is currently playing a game that they have also played at another time in the past.Present perfect continuous:The present perfect continuous tense describes an ongoing action that began in the past and is still occurring in the present.4t It is formed by combining the phrase has been or have been (depending on the subject) with the present participle of the verb.Shelly has been babysitting for years.In this example, the verb tense is used to say that Shelly started babysitting children in the past, continued to babysit for years, and still continues to babysit now.Future tensesWe use the future tenses to say that an event will happen sometime in the future. Like past and present tenses, there are four variations of future tenses:Simple future: Describes an event that will begin and end in the future.Future continuous: Describes an event that will begin in the future and continue for a length of time.Future perfect: Describes a future event that will happen before another future event.Future perfect continuous: Describes a future event that will begin, continue for a length of time, and still be in progress when another future event occurs.Simple futureThe simple future tense describes events that haven’t happened yet. It’s useful for describing an intended action or a prediction. It’s typically formed by combining the word will or, less commonly, shall with a root verb.For example:Molly will finish her chores when she has time.We shall travel to France next summer.The word will is an auxiliary verb, and finish is the root verb. Together, they explain that Molly4 intends to do her chores at a later point in time.Learn more about auxiliary verbs and the verbs they help out, here.Future continuous tenseThe future continuous tense describes an activity that will extend over a period of time and will happen in the future. It is formed by combining the phrase will be and the present participle of the verb (ending in –ing):I will be working all afternoon, so I can’t help Olivia with her report.In this sentence, the verb tense is used to say that I plan to work for a period of time in the future.Future perfect tenseThe future perfect tense describes an upcoming action in relation to another event farther in the future. It is formed by combining the phrase will have and the past participle of the verb:By tomorrow afternoon, Olivia will have finished her report.This sentence uses the future perfect tense to say that Olivia’s report is incomplete right now, but it will be finished before tomorrow afternoon.Future perfect continuousThe future perfect continuous tense describes an action that will extend over a period of time and will be performed in relation to another future event. It is formed by combining the phrase will have been with the present participle of the verb (ending in –ing):When this show ends, Molly will have been watching TV for three hours.This sentence uses the future perfect continuous tense to say that, in the future, Molly will be watching TV for three hours when this show ends (which will also happen in the future). By using the future perfect continuous tense, this sentence also implies that Molly may still continue to watch TV even after the show is over.Perfect grammar has never been easierTo avoid confusion, you should use one consistent tense whenever possible.❌ Incorrect: The crowd claps and laughed at the comedian.✅ Correct: The crowd clapped and laughed at the comedian.The incorrect example contains both a present tense verb (claps) and a past tense verb (laughed). This can be confusing. If both actions are past or present, both verbs should have the same tense.-----------------------------------------------Looking for where to attend adult education lesson, learn how to read, write, speak and spell in Lagos, Nigeria, Gbagada, Ikeja, Lekki, Ikoyi, Ajah, Surulere, Oshodi, Victoria Island, Ketu, Ojota, Ojodu-Berger, Mowe, Ikorodu, Islolo, Festac, Agege, Orile, Obalende, Lagos-Island, Apapa, Songo, etc.#adulteducation #readandwrite #spelling #learnhowtospellandspeak #learnhowtoreadandwrite #adultschoollagos #adultlearningcenter CONTACT:Symmetric Adult Education.

title: Why Understanding Risk Is More Important Than Chasing High Returns
main_content:
Thread Title: Why Understanding Risk Is More Important Than Chasing High Returns

Main Post: As digital investment services continue to expand across Sweden, more individuals are exploring opportunities in global financial markets. While access to investing has become easier than ever, experienced investors often emphasize that long-term success depends less on finding the highest possible returns and more on understanding the risks involved in every financial decision.Successful investing is built on preparation, discipline, and informed analysis rather than short-term excitement.Every Investment Carries RiskRegardless of the financial instrument—whether stocks, commodities, currencies, or other assets—market prices fluctuate in response to economic conditions, corporate developments, monetary policy, and global events.Recognizing that uncertainty is a natural part of investing helps individuals develop more realistic expectations and avoid emotional decision-making during periods of market volatility.Understanding potential risks is often just as important as identifying potential opportunities.Information Should Be Verified Before Decisions Are MadeOne of the most effective ways to evaluate an investment platform is to begin with official information provided directly by the company. Official websites typically explain available services, supported asset classes, educational resources, platform features, and account functionality.For example, Expedition Investment Management PTE LTD presents information about its digital investment platform, available analytical tools, and financial services through expeditioninv.com. Reviewing these publicly available materials allows prospective users to gain a clearer understanding of the platform before making any decisions.Research Tools Support Better Market AnalysisToday's investment platforms increasingly combine multiple analytical resources into a single environment. Interactive charts, economic calendars, financial news, market reports, and educational materials allow users to examine financial markets from different perspectives.According to publicly available information, Expedition Investment Management PTE LTD provides analytical features designed to help users monitor financial markets and access relevant market information. Additional details regarding these resources are available on expeditioninv.com.Diversification Is About Managing UncertaintyMany investors view diversification as one of the fundamental principles of long-term portfolio management. Rather than relying on a single asset or market, diversification involves spreading exposure across different investment categories.While diversification cannot eliminate investment risk entirely, it may help reduce the impact of unexpected developments affecting a specific sector or asset class. Building a balanced portfolio requires thoughtful planning and periodic review as market conditions evolve.Knowledge Remains the Strongest Long-Term AssetTechnology continues to transform the investment industry, offering investors faster access to financial markets and increasingly sophisticated analytical tools. However, technology alone cannot replace financial knowledge, independent research, and responsible decision-making.Whether someone is considering Expedition Investment Management PTE LTD or another investment platform, reviewing official information, understanding available analytical resources, and continuously improving financial literacy remain valuable steps toward making informed and responsible investment decisions over time.

title: Support Of The Olodo Uprising
main_content:
Thread Title: Support Of The Olodo Uprising

Main Post: Support of the Olodo UprisingIn Support of the Olodo Uprising: A Movement for the Boldly UninformedBy a Concerned Citizen of the Federal Republic of OlodoniaHistory has celebrated many revolutions—the Industrial Revolution, the Digital Revolution, and now, at long last, the Olodo Uprising. It is time we stopped mocking the confidently incorrect and instead recognized their courage. After all, it takes remarkable bravery to argue with facts while having absolutely none.For too long, society has unfairly rewarded people who "read books," "verify information," and "know what they're talking about." Meanwhile, the average Olodo has been dismissed simply for believing that Australia is in Europe or that 12 × 9 equals "whatever the calculator says."This discrimination must end.The Olodo Uprising stands for three sacred principles:1. Confidence over competence.2. Volume over validity.3. If you're corrected, argue harder.Critics claim the movement is anti-intellectual. That is completely false. Many members love education—they just prefer it from WhatsApp broadcasts, voice notes beginning with "My uncle works in government...", and Facebook posts written entirely in capital letters.The movement has already proposed several groundbreaking national reforms:Replace WAEC exams with multiple-choice questions where every option is correct.Abolish dictionaries because "words should mean whatever you feel they mean."Introduce a new school grading system:A – Almost CorrectB – Believed ItC – ConfidenceD – Didn't CheckF – Facts Were Against MeSupporters also insist that every debate should end after someone says, "Go and verify it yourself," regardless of whether there is anything to verify.The Olodo Uprising is also demanding equal respect in everyday conversations. They argue that saying "I don't know" is outdated. Instead, every Nigerian should confidently provide an answer—even if the topic is quantum physics, rocket science, or why the office Wi-Fi stopped working.Their campaign slogan says it all: "Wrong today, wrong tomorrow, but never in doubt!"The movement has even introduced a national anthem:"We move, we no dey reason,Confidence is our season.If the facts begin to bite,We'll just say Google isn't right!"Whether the Olodo Uprising succeeds remains to be seen. But one thing is certain: no matter what happens, its members will confidently declare victory—even if they accidentally celebrate the wrong result.Disclaimer: This is a work of satire intended for humor. It is not meant to encourage ignorance or ridicule any individual or group. Knowledge is valuable—but it's also healthy to laugh at those moments when confidence outruns correctness.

Main Post: My fellow citizens,This administration has observed that, during disagreements, some individuals do not rely on logic, evidence, or good manners.Instead, they simply arrive... looking like they could bench-press a motorcycle.Accordingly, the Government hereby establishes the National Body Mass Observation Programme—not because being big is a crime, but because looking like you could accidentally end an argument by standing up deserves a second look.Section 1 — Observation Threshold1. Any citizen whose body weight exceeds 120 kilograms or whose physical build is deemed exceptionally imposing may be invited for a routine Public Presence Assessment.2. This assessment shall not be a criminal investigation and shall not imply guilt.3. It simply means the Government would like to confirm that your greatest strength is your character, not just your shoulders.Section 2 — No Automatic Suspicion1. Citizens shall not be presumed dangerous because of their size.2. However, where an individual's physical presence is routinely used to intimidate, bully, threaten, or coerce others, appropriate legal action shall follow.3. Being large is not an offence. Weaponising your size against others is.Section 3 — Public Responsibility1. Citizens blessed with extraordinary physiques are encouraged to use them responsibly.2. Society has enough problems already; it does not need "Do you know who I am?" delivered by someone who blocks the entire doorway.Section 4 — Effective DateThis Directive takes effect immediately upon publication.Issued under the Seal of the President Akogun Republic,for the protection of public peace, personal space, and doorframes across the Republic.And finally:The Government has no issue with your size.It only requests that your manners grow faster than your muscles.

MAJOR FOOD MARKETS IN LAGOS AND WHAT THEY SPECIALIZE INMajor food markets in LagosMajor food markets across Lagos sell a wide variety of food items, however, every market has its own food "specialty" - This just basically means the foods you can buy from there in bulk quantities and at wholesale prices.This means you are more likely to get a good bargain when you visit a particular market to buy what it is known for (its specialty). For instance, Idi-oro market is known for plantain, yellow gari and farm snails while Daleko market is known for rice; So if you are buying say 50bags of rice, I will say buy it from Daleko market, not Mile 12 and if you are buying dozens of plantain bunches, I will say, buy it from Idi-oro market not Oyingbo (hope this makes sense).However, it won't make "business" sense to visit Mile 12 and Daleko market in one day, just because you want to buy a basket of tomatoes and a bag of rice. You can simply buy both from Mile 12 since you are not buying in very large quantities......Here's a list of Markets in Lagos and their food "specialty"1. Iddo marketThis market is just after oyingbo; Adjacent to the Lagos Terminus building (click for directions) and opposite the Iddo BRT bus-stop. This market is known for Bags of rice, beans, corn, groundnut and kegs of vegetable oil.2. White sand marketThis market is situated between Iddo and Oyingbo . It is known for egusi (the different types), ogbono, dry peppers, crayfish, different types of smoked fish, stockfish (different cuts). If you desire to buy these food items in wholesale quantities, you can a get good bargain here.3. Oyingbo marketThis market is situated at Oyingbo bus-stop (click for directions), close to Ebute Metta. Some parts of the market operate only early in the mornings. For wholesale purchase, this is a good place to source for Snails, red crayfish (okporo), vegetables ( ugu , utazi, uziza, afang, ewedu, okro, shoko,tete, bitterleaf), spices and condiments for local soups , periwinkles, bonga fish, smoked catfish, cocoyam.4. Idi-oro marketIts right beside the LIRS (click or directions) office in Mushin, off Agege motor road, Idi-oro bus-stop, Mushin. In this market , food items you can majorly source for include - plantain (lots of it!), yellow gari , Palmoil and farm snails. The best time to buy from here is in the morning.5. Oju iwoye market/ AlasalatuThis market is in mushin, it is the home of groceries; as a food retailer, this is one of the best places in Lagos to source for groceries in wholesale quantities and at very good prices. You can have your fish (or any other seafood) you buy cleaned and smoked . Oke-arin market (click for directions)This market is inside Lagos Island market, you can go in through Apongbon; Major Distributors of most food products have shops in this market so it's a really great place to buy in bulk quantities and at wholesale prices. title: A Joke With A Meaning & Message! Ajani.
main_content:
Thread Title: A Joke With A Meaning & Message! Ajani.

Main Post: On a certain Tuesday in a certain year in a certain town in Nigeria, was an incident that shook the neighborhood like an earthquake had suddenly erupted. Let me share the details of this incident. There live a man named Ajani and he was a hunter. He was known for hunting wild bush meat and sharing it to the underprivileged people in shokolokobangoshey community. On that faithful day, Ajani had gone into the thick forrest to retrieve his traps which had been placed the previous day, in hopes that wild bush animals would be caught in them. When he got to one of the traps, the large rodent known as grasscutter was partially caught in the hook of his trap. When he tried to reach down and grab the ears if the rodent, it swerved its head to the left (to the left, to the left. Everything...) as if it had been planning to deal with Ajani for catching and cooking several of its furry rodent relatives! So, Ajani's hands got caught in the sharp, pointy and curved hook of the trap, causing a deep slash wound on his right hand. Blood starte to gush out from a torn Ajani forearm. He screamed out saying; ' Yaay! E ba mi oh! E ba mi! 'The gray-coloured giant rodent stuck out his tongue at a terrified Ajani and mysteriously and surprisingly uttered words like a human being, saying; Nmeh! Ntor! Oleburuku ni sha. Today the bushmeat done catch the unter! (the letter " H " sound appeared to be silent, as the south-western intonation was even evident in the bushmeat's accent). Staying true to its roots. Ajani, upon hearing this strange utterance, with the pupils in his eyes now widened, took to his heels, with his heels touching the back of his cone head. " No be juju be dat ? " He yelled out, nobody else in sight. No one to save him. Even his favourite god, Ogun, was having his afternoon tea party and foot massage with the goddess Osun and her maidens in a secluded realm. So, at a time like that there was no picking of any earth-dwelling human's calls for heavenly help and intervention. " We are busy right now but you can leave a voicemail message after the tone " was the message Ajani got. Fleeing back to the township of shokolokobangoshey, Ajani was panting heavily like the black panter that he is. He's black in complexion, and was panting at that moment, which qualifies him being referred to as a black panter. When his friend, Awo, caught up to him, he noticed the deep wound in Ajani's arm and screamed out in shock!Awo: ' Ah! It's serious oh! Oti serious gan! Blood is rushing! '' Band it! ( Put a bandage on it, or, get the wound banded to stop the loss of blood, he meant)Band it! Awo: I say, band it, ooooh! Hurry! 'When several groups of little children, youths and elders had been trekking close by and heard those words " band it " being yelled three times, they mistook it to mean " bandits ". They immediately went into panick mode, and all ran off in different directions, with most of them abandoning their farm produce , their school notebooks, their fetched jerrycans of water, their agidi and other belongings 😱. Fear had overwhelmed them due to the constant security threats of banditry attacks. 🤣 & 😞This calls for concern and Thanks for reading my lengthy joke. 😊✊It's a joke with a message that suits the times we are currently living in! 🇳🇬Stay safe.

title: You Rejected Him, So Why Are You Angry That He Moved On?
main_content:
Thread Title: You Rejected Him, So Why Are You Angry That He Moved On?

Main Post: Let us be honest about something because I think we have started misunderstanding what rejection actually means.If someone approaches you for a date, a relationship, sex or anything romantic and you said no, you have every right to reject them. Nobody should pressure you into accepting an advance you do not want.At the same time, the person you rejected has every right to accept your answer and remove himself from the situation. He can stop calling, stop replying to your messages, stop checking on you, or even block you if staying in contact makes it harder for him to move on. He can eventually find somebody else too.None of these automatically means he cannot handle rejection.Sometimes handling rejection is exactly that: accepting the rejection and moving on.A friend once told me about a guy who had been admiring her for a while. He eventually asked her out and she told him she was not ready for a relationship. He accepted it. About three months later, he asked again, but she still refused, explaining that she had a lot going on in her life.The guy simply said, “Okay, I will let you deal with those things.”The guy moved on and about 2 months later, a lady who is mutual friend of mind invited me her birthday party. It was when i got there that i got to find out her boyfriend was the guy that was rejected my friend. Days later while we were gisting I told that my friend that her former crush had finally found someone else, then she became angry.“But I told him I needed time,” she said. “Is that why he stopped replying to my messages?”She tried calling his number and discovered that he had even blocked her. Her conclusion was that the guy could not handle rejection.I asked her one simple question:“What exactly do you think handling rejection means?”I never got an answer.If you tell a guy that you are not interested in dating him, what exactly is he supposed to do afterwards? Remain emotionally available while you decide whether you might eventually change your mind? Keep checking on you, listening to your problems, complimenting you and behaving like your unofficial boyfriend while you repeatedly remind him that we are “just friends”?My sister, you did not have friends before he came along? There is nothing wrong with genuine friendship after rejection. If both people can honestly move on and become friends without one person secretly waiting for the other to change their mind, fine.The problem is when “let us just be friends” really means, “I do not want a relationship with you, but I still want your attention, validation, emotional support and availability.”Some people enjoy being wanted even when they do not want the person back. They like knowing somebody is always there. When that person finally gets tired and walks away, they suddenly become wicked, proud or accuse the other party of not being able to handle rejection.But you rejected him and He accepted it.What exactly did you want him to do?I have even heard ladies say that when someone disappears immediately after being rejected, it proves they only wanted their body.Maybe he did but you still said no.Why should he remain interested after you have told him you are not interested in him?If a man wants a relationship with a woman and she says no, he is not obligated to become her best friend instead. The same applies to women. If a woman is rejected, she is also free to walk away and find someone who wants her.There is a difference between rejection and disrespect. Rejecting someone is not disrespectful. Moving on after rejection is not disrespectful. Harassing, insulting, threatening or trying to punish someone for saying no or moving on after being turned down is when it becomes disrespectful.You are entitled to reject me. I am entitled to move on.Your “no” should be respected, but my decision to leave should also be respected.Sometimes the person who disappears after you reject them is not bitter.They have simply understood the assignment. You said no. They heard you. Now let them go and find their own yes.Dey your dey. I go dey my dey.

title: The Lucky Gold Digger....a True Life Story
main_content:
Thread Title: The Lucky Gold Digger....a True Life Story

Main Post: The Lucky Gold Digger....A true life story Emeka was born into hardship. The second of four children in a small compound in Imo State, he grew up knowing what it meant to be diligent and to lack. School fees were a monthly crisis, but fate intervened through his maternal uncle, Chief Ibe — a respected trader in medical supplies at Onitsha Head Bridge Market. With Chief Ibe’s support, Emeka completed secondary school and went on to study Psychology at a federal university. He was the family’s hope. Then, in his final year, Chief Ibe died in a road accident. The safety net was gone.After graduation, Emeka served his NYSC in Lagos, posted to a private secondary school in Ajah. When service ended, the school kept him on as a full-time teacher. The salary was meagre, the rent was not. For three years he taught, saved, and watched Lagos move ahead of him. Hope began to feel like a debt he couldn’t repay.It was in that frustration that Emeka made a decision he would later call “the only way out.” He joined a WhatsApp group where young men connected with older, wealthy women seeking companionship. His first arrangement ended in disaster. He was linked with a woman on Lagos Island who paid him ₦100,000 for the night. The encounter was degrading and physically overwhelming. He was pressured to drink to cope, and the experience left him shaken and hospitalized. In the days that followed, he vowed never to return to that life.He disappeared for a while to recover. A friend later invited him to a large Pentecostal church in Lagos, one attended mostly by working-class professional women. Emeka threw himself into the church. He served, he showed up early, he was dependable. The head pastor noticed.Through the pastor’s introduction, Emeka met Ms. Chioma, a Director at MTN Nigeria. She was in her late 40s, successful, and had been praying for a partner. With the pastor’s blessing and guidance, a relationship formed quickly. Emeka was careful, humble, and attentive. Within a year, they were married.The marriage changed everything. Chioma, who had struggled with fibroids and the possibility of children, decided to seek treatment in India. Tragically, she did not survive the surgery. In her will — prepared with the pastor’s counsel — she left her properties in both the Island and Mainland to Emeka. MTN also offered him a role in her department as part of her benefits package. Against the objections of Chioma’s family, Emeka became the legal beneficiary of her estate and began a new life.Six months later, now financially secure and employed, Emeka returned to his village. He was no longer the struggling teacher from Ajah. He had status, a car, and a future he could plan. There, he met a young woman his own age — someone he said he truly wanted to build with. He married her. And that, as people in the village now say, “is where the story started.”many people in the village and some of his old friends now call him the lucky Gold digger Written by greatiyk4u Mutum BiyuTaraba state.

In Yoruba culture, you don’t just marry an individual—you marry a family. That was very different from what I was used to, but I quickly understood why marriages here are often stronger. title: Best Dating Apps: What To Look For Before You Sign Up
main_content:
Thread Title: Best Dating Apps: What To Look For Before You Sign Up

Main Post: Choosing among the best dating apps is not simply about downloading the one with the most users. A dating app can look impressive at first glance but still be a poor fit if its members, features, safety tools, or relationship culture do not match what you want. Taking a few minutes to evaluate an app before creating an account can save time and help you make more informed decisions.Whether you want a serious relationship, casual dating, or simply to meet new people, the right platform should make your goals clear and give you reasonable control over your dating experience.Start With Your Dating GoalBefore comparing the best online dating apps, decide what you actually want from dating.Different platforms can attract people with very different expectations. Someone looking for marriage may have little in common with someone interested only in casual conversations.Ask yourself:Am I looking for a committed relationship?Do I prefer casual dating?Would I like to meet people with similar professional or lifestyle interests?Am I open to long-distance connections?How much time do I want to spend using an app?This matters because dating apps for relationships often provide features designed to encourage more detailed profiles and intentional matching.Look at How Profiles WorkA useful profile system should give people enough room to explain who they are beyond photographs.Check whether an app allows users to include interests, values, lifestyle preferences, relationship intentions, and other meaningful information. More profile detail does not automatically mean better matches, but it can give you more context before starting a conversation.Check Whether the App Fits Your PreferencesOne of the biggest mistakes people make is choosing an app based only on popularity.Instead, investigate the type of community it serves.For example, an app may be more suitable for:Professionals with demanding schedulesPeople seeking long-term relationshipsOlder adultsPeople interested in specific lifestylesSingles who prefer detailed matchmakingPeople who want a broader dating poolThe best dating apps 2026 will not necessarily be identical for everyone. The better question is, "Which app is most suitable for my goals and preferences?"Pay Attention to Safety and PrivacySafety should be one of your first checks, not an afterthought.Before signing up, review the app's privacy policy and safety features. Look for practical tools that allow users to control unwanted interactions.Useful features can include:Blocking and reportingProfile verificationPrivacy controlsOptions to control who can contact youGuidance for reporting suspicious behaviorClear community standardsThe Federal Trade Commission advises consumers to be cautious about online romance scams and warns against sending money to someone met through an online dating service.You should also avoid sharing sensitive information too quickly. A new match does not need your home address, financial information, workplace security details, or account passwords.Watch for Suspicious BehaviorTechnology can help with safety, but your own judgment remains important.Be cautious if someone:Quickly declares intense feelingsAvoids reasonable questions about their identityConsistently refuses to video chat or meet safelyCreates pressure to move conversations elsewhereRequests money or financial assistanceTells elaborate stories about an emergencyA dating app should give you tools to report concerning behavior, but you should still make decisions carefully.Understand the Matching SystemMatching systems vary considerably.Some apps rely heavily on location and basic preferences. Others use questionnaires, interests, compatibility information, or behavioral signals.Before choosing an app, ask:Does the matching system actually help me find the type of person I want to meet?For instance, if you value shared interests and relationship intentions, an app based primarily on rapid swiping may not feel as useful as one that provides more information about potential matches.There is no universal formula for finding dating apps that work. Success depends partly on whether the platform attracts people whose expectations align with yours.Review the Free and Paid FeaturesYou do not necessarily need to pay for a dating app, but you should understand what the free version provides.Look at:Number of daily interactionsMessaging restrictionsSearch or filtering optionsProfile visibility controlsPremium matching featuresSubscription pricesCancellation termsDo not subscribe simply because a feature sounds impressive. First determine whether it solves a problem you actually have.For example, if you rarely use the app, paying for additional visibility may not provide much value.Evaluate the Quality of ConversationsA dating app is ultimately a tool for helping people communicate. Even sophisticated matching features cannot replace genuine interaction.Once you have a few potential matches, pay attention to how conversations develop.A healthy conversation usually involves some balance. Both people ask questions, respond thoughtfully, and respect boundaries.Consider moving beyond repetitive questions such as "What do you do?" Try discussing hobbies, travel preferences, personal goals, books, food, or something interesting from the person's profile.For example, instead of sending "Hey," you could ask about a hiking trip mentioned in their profile. It creates a natural starting point and shows that you actually read what they wrote.Give the App a Trial PeriodYou do not have to decide immediately whether an app is right for you.Give it a reasonable trial period and assess the actual experience.After a couple of weeks, consider:Am I meeting people who share my goals?Are profiles genuine and detailed?Do conversations feel respectful?Is the app easy to use?Are there too many irrelevant matches?Do I feel comfortable with its privacy controls?Is the paid version worth considering?This practical test can tell you more than advertisements or app-store ratings alone.Make Your Own Profile Part of the EvaluationRemember that your results are influenced by the profile you create.Use recent photographs that accurately represent you. Write a short description that gives potential matches something specific to respond to. Be honest about what you are looking for.If you want a serious relationship, saying so clearly can help reduce confusion.At the same time, avoid turning your profile into a list of demands. Explain your interests and values rather than creating an unrealistic checklist for potential partners.ConclusionThe best dating apps are not necessarily the most popular ones. The right choice depends on your relationship goals, preferred community, safety expectations, matching preferences, and budget.Before signing up, investigate how profiles work, review privacy and safety tools, understand the payment structure, and consider whether the people using the platform are looking for something similar to you. Platforms such as Favor can be part of that comparison, but your personal goals should remain the deciding factor.A thoughtful choice at the beginning can make online dating more focused and less frustrating.

title: How To Know If Your Partner Is Talking To Someone Else
main_content:
Thread Title: How To Know If Your Partner Is Talking To Someone Else

Main Post: Trust is one of the foundations of a healthy relationship.But sometimes, changes in a partner’s behaviour can leave someone wondering whether there is another person involved.It is important to remember that no single sign proves a partner is talking to someone else. People can become distant for many reasons, including work stress, family problems or personal struggles.However, certain changes may be worth paying attention to.They suddenly become secretive with their phoneMost people value privacy.But if your partner suddenly starts hiding their screen, changing passwords frequently or taking calls in private when they never used to, it could raise questions.A sudden change in behaviour is often more important than the behaviour itself.Their communication changesA partner who once replied quickly may suddenly become unavailable for long periods without explanation.They may seem distracted during conversations or less interested in talking than before.They become emotionally distantWhen people invest emotional energy elsewhere, they sometimes become less emotionally available in their current relationship.Full story here: [LINK]

Comments:

Trust is one of the foundations of a healthy relationship.But sometimes, changes in a partner’s behaviour can leave someone wondering whether there is another person involved.It is important to remember that no single sign proves a partner is talking to someone else. People can become distant for many reasons, including work stress, family problems or personal struggles.However, certain changes may be worth paying attention to.They suddenly become secretive with their phoneMost people value privacy.But if your partner suddenly starts hiding their screen, changing passwords frequently or taking calls in private when they never used to, it could raise questions.A sudden change in behaviour is often more important than the behaviour itself.Their communication changesA partner who once replied quickly may suddenly become unavailable for long periods without explanation.They may seem distracted during conversations or less interested in talking than before.They become emotionally distantWhen people invest emotional energy elsewhere, they sometimes become less emotionally available in their current relationship.Full story here: [LINK] I'll help you out. Here's the rest of the article:Conversations become shorter.Affection decreases.The connection starts to feel different.They are always online but slow to respondMany people notice this sign first.You see your partner active on social media or messaging apps, but your messages go unanswered for hours.While this alone proves nothing, a consistent pattern can create concerns.They become defensive over simple questionsIf asking normal questions about their day suddenly leads to irritation or arguments, something may have changed.Defensiveness does not automatically mean guilt, but it can signal discomfort.They compare you to someone elseA partner who frequently talks about a particular person, praises them excessively or compares you to them may be revealing where their attention is focused.Their routine changes without explanationNew habits, unexplained outings or frequent absences can sometimes create suspicion, especially when reasonable explanations are not provided.They show less interest in the relationshipOne of the strongest warning signs is a noticeable drop in effort.They stop planning activities together.They show less affection.They seem less interested in your life and feelings.What should you do?Avoid rushing to conclusions based on suspicion alone.Instead of spying, accusing or checking phones secretly, have an honest conversation.Ask questions calmly.Listen carefully.A healthy relationship depends on communication and trust, not assumptions.ConclusionThe biggest clue is often not a single action but a pattern of changes over time.If your partner’s behaviour has changed significantly, it is worth discussing your concerns openly.The goal should not be to catch someone doing something wrong but to understand what is happening in the relationship and whether both people remain committed to it.

Main Post: "If you are my boyfriend..." — Lady says she won't cook or clean when she visits his houseA lady has sparked discussion online after revealing that she would not cook, wash clothes or clean whenever she visits her boyfriend’s home.The lady, whose identity was not disclosed, made the comments while explaining the kind of arrangement she expects in a relationship.According to her, visiting a boyfriend should not automatically mean taking on domestic responsibilities, particularly when she is not living in his home.The lady said, “If you are my boyfriend and I come to your place I’m not going to do anything. I’m not going to wash cloth, I’m not going to cook, I’m not going to clean. I will not do anything.”Lady explains her preferred living arrangementShe further suggested that her boyfriend would need to have a spacious home because of her temperament.The lady added, “You must have like two to three bedroom flat because I have short temper so a room is not even possible.”Her comments have drawn attention to differing expectations surrounding domestic duties in modern relationships, especially when couples spend time at each other’s homes.For some people, cooking or helping with housework when visiting a partner may be viewed as a natural gesture of affection. Others believe such responsibilities should be discussed and agreed upon rather than automatically expected.Statement sparks conversation onlineThe lady’s remarks have therefore opened up another conversation about boundaries, gender roles and expectations in romantic relationships.While some may interpret her position as setting clear boundaries, others could view it as an unwillingness to contribute to a shared domestic environment.The discussion highlights how couples can have significantly different expectations about what partners should do for each other, even in seemingly ordinary situations such as visiting one another’s homes.Watch the video below...“If you are my boyfriend and I come to your place, have it in mind that I won’t cook, clean, or do anything. title: She Was The Most Beautiful Girl In My Set. 22 Years Later, She Is Still Single
main_content:
Thread Title: She Was The Most Beautiful Girl In My Set. 22 Years Later, She Is Still Single

Main Post: I attended a very expensive private secondary school in Ibadan. Previously, I attended a public school. I remember my father took out a loan to pay my first term's school fees. The man literally showed me the money, in raw cash, while in the company of my mother.My parents were just middle-level civil servants. When I got to my new school, I saw this dark-skinned girl who was unique in her own way. She was of average height, slim, quiet and very neat. She had a high sense of maturity. She never played rough. Her school uniform was always very neat and clean. Her spoken English was very good. She had a smile that could heal a wounded soul.What stood out about her was her confidence. The way she carried herself wasn't loud or intimidating, but it sent a message: “I know my worth.” Everyone easily talked about her. Her parents were well-to-do, and they were based in Lagos State while she schooled as a boarder in an Ibadan school. Historically, Ibadan-based people have always had a huge respect for Lagosians. That was another plus for her.She was a girl who could lighten your mood just by talking to you at school. Many boys in my set, the 2004 class, believed she liked them simply because they had spoken a few times or she smiled at them. As a shy person from a civil servant home, I didn't stand a chance, like Atiku Abubakar in the next presidential election. I simply admired and observed from a distance.A couple of boys were linked to her romantically, but it was more talk than action, no hands-on. Her body was like a sanctuary she never wanted to defile. Her influence was so powerful that a handsome boy who got very close to dating her actually failed and repeated a class. He dropped her name as an excuse for his failure, claiming she affected his academic focus. Guess what? She passed and did so well. The guy in question is a popular Christian cleric in Ibadan, Nigeria, today. Life is interesting.She was never short of suitors. After one school holiday, rumours swirled around the school that a boy from a wealthy family, well-travelled across the world, had driven a Mercedes-Benz to her house in the highbrow Island area of Lagos to woo her. She said NO!The news spread around the school, with nobody verifying whether it was true or false. It nevertheless further boosted her reputation. Many said she got a job with one of the top tech companies in the world, and the pay was monstrous. Things got better, and she also moved abroad. It appears suitors never stopped coming. Maybe she felt nobody deserved her. Or perhaps life simply took her in a different direction. Twenty-two years later, she is still single. She is about 40 now.Marriage isn't a big deal, women always say, but that argument becomes more complicated when an African woman is involved. In many African societies, marriage still carries enormous social and family expectations. Beauty can be a blessing, but perhaps it can also become a curse. There is an interesting phenomenon involving beautiful single women. Some suitors assume they are not really single. Others believe their standards are too high or that there will be too much competition involved in winning their hearts. Some men simply assume that a woman who looks that good must already have several men fighting for her attention. Others believe she might never be submissive in marriage.It is almost like buying a vehicle that requires high maintenance. You admire it from a distance, but you convince yourself that owning it will be too expensive or complicated. In the end, a beautiful woman can find herself alone, not necessarily because nobody wants her, but because many people assume somebody else already has her. Some may eventually have relationships that are casual and convenient, with men who come, do the work and sail off until their services are needed again. Life can be such a humbler.On a personal note, I don't believe marriage is for everybody. The earlier Africans face this reality, the better. Some people are genuinely better off being alone. Several people are marking marriage anniversaries with very limited happy moments behind the photographs and celebrations.But that is a topic for another day.[LINK]

title: Different Nigerian Men You Will Meet When They Ask You Out
main_content:
Thread Title: Different Nigerian Men You Will Meet When They Ask You Out

Main Post: But there is another funny side of dating in Nigeria that we should talk about: the Nigerian man you meet after collecting your number. 😂Because sometimes, the problem was never getting the number. The real test begins after he gets it.You will meet the man who says, “I’m a very simple person. I don’t like spending unnecessarily.”Translation: romance must be powered by prayer. 😂1. THE STINGY MANHe can afford it, but every outing suddenly becomes a financial audit.“Why don't we just sit at home?”“Food is expensive outside.”“Can you cook?”Sir, you invited her out. 😭2. THE UNROMANTIC MANYou send him a beautiful message in the morning.“Good morning, my love ❤️. I hope you slept well.”His reply:“Morning.”That's all.You start wondering if you are dating a man or customer-care chatbot.3. THE “I DON'T DO BIRTHDAY” MANYour birthday comes and he says:“Happy birthday, dear. God bless you.”Meanwhile, he just bought himself a new phone three weeks ago.You ask about your gift and he says:“I'm the gift.”Brother, please. 😭😂4. THE “COME TO MY HOUSE” MANEvery date invitation somehow leads to his house.Restaurant? No.Cinema? Too expensive.Beach? Too far.“Come over, let's just chill.”At some point, madam will start asking herself whether she is in a relationship or has been employed as a part-time visitor.5. THE LOW-EFFORT ROMANTICHe wants all the benefits of a relationship but puts zero effort into maintaining it.No flowers.No thoughtful surprises.No planned dates.No random “I saw this and thought of you.”But when you complain, he says:“Women are too demanding these days.”Nobody asked you to buy a helicopter. Sometimes even a ₦2,000 thoughtful gesture can mean more than a ₦200,000 gift given without affection.6. THE “MY EX DIDN'T ASK FOR THIS” MANYou ask for basic emotional effort and suddenly your request becomes unreasonable.“My ex never complained.”Maybe that's why she's your ex, sir. 😂7. THE MAN WHO THINKS PROVIDING MONEY IS THE ENTIRE PERSONALITYYes, financial responsibility matters. But money alone doesn't make someone romantic.A woman can appreciate a man who provides and still want affection, attention, communication, compliments, quality time and intentionality.Being financially responsible is not an excuse to be emotionally unavailable.8. THE “I'M NOT A ROMANTIC PERSON” MANSome men proudly announce this as if romance is a genetic condition.Bro, romance is not necessarily about expensive gifts. Learn your woman's love language. Listen to her. Remember important dates. Check on her. Plan something occasionally. Give her a genuine compliment.You don't need to become Shakespeare overnight.At the end of the day, women are not necessarily asking Nigerian men to spend their entire salaries on them.Most women simply want to feel considered, appreciated and intentionally loved.Because just as men should learn that collecting a woman's number doesn't mean she likes them, women also need to understand that a man's financial capacity, personality and approach to romance will differ.But please, Nigerian men...If you have money and you are still stingy, that's a character issue.And if you have little money but you are thoughtful, intentional and romantic, you can still make a woman feel special without bankrupting yourself.No be every romance matter require POS transfer. Sometimes na effort. 😂❤️

title: Was l Wrong In Blocking Her?

Thread Title: Was l Wrong In Blocking Her?

Main Post: So l'm not a particular fan of bringing every relationship dilemma here. But let me just do it for once to catch the feel of it at least. So my girl knows too well that as a script writer, that l'm always busy working online throughout the day and that l normally chat with her towards the evening after work. But this early morning, she sent me some texts on WhatsApp, just the normal morning greetings, nothing much. But l wasn't in the mood for chatting at all, cus l was still going through some severe Monday Morning Hangover(My fellow bros that love the green bottle can relate better here.) Besides, l was also preparing to start my working day, so l ignored her. So this afternoon, eight or nine hours after her text, she started calling me on WhatsApp call, while l was working on a script for my main client. So l ignored the calls at first, but she kept calling and calling. So l was forced to send her a text on WhatsApp that l was working at the moment and will talk to her later. But she kept on calling and calling and even sent me a text that "this is my punishment for ignoring her since morning" That was the point l got a bit angry cus her persistent calls were interfering with my work, and l needed to fully concentrate on the script l was writing. And honestly, that was the whole point of my ignoring her chats, cus l really needed to focus on the script. Now, most people don't really know what it takes to succeed in script writing. I mean like, you need to concentrate 1000% on the script you're writing, cus any single mistake in grammar or tone or diction or any hole in the story, your client, who of course is a more experienced writer than you, will surely call you out on it later. And even if he/she doesn't catch the mistake, the editors higher up the channel's hierarchy, who are mostly Americans will definitely catch the mistake and call out your client, who of course will definitely turn up the heat on you. And you do have to spend extra time correcting the mistake. So l really needed to concentrate to avoid all that. So l texted her that she should better stop that nonsense else l block her. She kept calling and calling and even texted me "Oya block me na." So l blocked her. And she has never directly called since then. So l know she's hurt already. Now, this girl is just 22, and l'm 30. So she's definitely acting her age. But l honestly love her and l know she loves me too. But even at that, l still want to strongly pass that message across to her that "My Work Comes First Before Any Other Thing!" So l'm thinking about not unblocking her till after a week at most. But even at that, l still don't want to hurt her so much cus she just lost her Airport Attendant job last week and l know she needs me to be there for her at the moment. Besides, she was right there for me two years ago when l passed through the worst period of my life. So l'm really in a kinda dilemma right now and needs some mature advice. Update: l was planning to unblock her in the evening like most senior bros here adviced me. But she chatted me with her second line early this morning. So we are good.Thanks for all your mature advices. I really appreciate!

Should she say it?You really need wisdom when talking about your bad past. It is good to talk about your bad past, but you need wisdom.You really need wisdom when talking about your bad past.I believe serious relationships should be built on honesty, especially when marriage is involved. If there are things in your past that could materially affect your partner's decision to marry you, don't deliberately hide them.However, being honest doesn't mean giving someone a graphic documentary of everything you've ever done. There is a difference between transparency and unnecessary details. Tell the truth, take responsibility for your actions, explain what you've learned, and allow the other person to make an informed decision.For example, if a lady has had several abortions, I wouldn't advise her to keep it secret simply because she's afraid her fiancé might leave. If she is serious about marrying him, he deserves to know and decide whether he can genuinely accept that part of her history. But she also doesn't need to go into unnecessary intimate details.And if you're the person hearing someone's difficult past, don't immediately reduce them to their mistakes. Ask yourself who they are today, what changed, and whether they have genuinely taken responsibility.The greatest danger is not necessarily having a bad past; it's entering marriage with a hidden past that eventually becomes a weapon in the marriage.Tell the truth. Tell it wisely. Don't glorify the past, don't hide what matters, and don't use someone's past to punish them forever.Marriage needs honesty, but it also needs grace, maturity and the ability to leave yesterday where it belongs.

NoDon't have a bad pasthnkYes—tell your fiancé/fiancée about the past that could reasonably affect their decision to marry you, but do it with wisdom, timing, honesty, and responsibility. The goal is not to confess every detail of your history; it is to build a marriage on truth rather than hidden information.For example, if a woman has had several abortions, I would advise her not to casually hide it simply because she is afraid of being rejected. If the relationship is seriously heading toward marriage, that is significant personal history that her future husband may consider important. She should tell him herself, privately and respectfully, rather than allowing him to discover it later from someone else.But there is a difference between honesty and unnecessary graphic details. She can explain what happened, acknowledge her responsibility, talk about what she has learned, and explain where she stands now. She doesn't necessarily need to narrate every circumstance or provide intimate details.Most importantly, the man should understand that someone's past is not automatically their present character. People make serious mistakes, sometimes repeatedly, and genuinely change. The question should be: Who is this person today? What has she learned? What values does she now live by?At the same time, the person receiving the confession must also have the maturity to decide whether they can genuinely accept that history. Don't pressure someone to "forgive" you into marriage, and don't marry someone while secretly planning to punish them for their past.

title: The Stigmatisation Of Players And The Error Of Pick-up Lines
main_content:
Thread Title: The Stigmatisation Of Players And The Error Of Pick-up Lines

Main Post: The Stigmatisation of Players and the error of Pickup lines1) Everyone play games. 2) Pick-up lines are an effect, and not a causeThe 2 points above are the core of this post and I'll expand on them so as to bring insight to you1) What is a game?As seen on the video games you play, one can understand that a game is anything with these:a) A clear objectiveb) Rules on how to playc) Prizes to be won if played welld) Consequences to be suffered if you don't play your game wellThose who play games are called Play-erFrom the understanding of what a game is, I'd call myself a player.Why? Well that's because unknowingly, I played a game while in the university. "Unknowingly" in the sense that I didn't realize I played a game until later. I had an objective to want to graduate with a second class upper or lower in the university and these were my blueprintsMy rules: Try boost my continuous assessment so that I can fail comfortably in my exam, being that I wasn't the smartest in the room, neither did the education format I received in the university sit well with me. My CA was 30%, while exams was 70%. If I could manage to get at least a 20% in my CA, I could comfortably fail to a 35-40% in exams, which would bring my total to 55-60%. I'd call this a nice result.Rule no 2: I tried as much as possible to not upset my lecturers, and I also avoided friends that'd distract me from my objective.Following this blueprint, I'd later graduate with a second class upper. But trust me, brain alone did not give me that result. So it's this story that I flash back to whenever I call myself a player, and it's from the insight of this story that I dare to call all humans playersAll humans want to live long, even the masochists. At least one has to be alive to inflict pain on themselves. Even those that plan wars are found nowhere around the warzone because they selfishly want to be alive to plan more wars. For a human to want to be alive for long is an objective, and distancing themselves from disruption, even the ones they cause is one of their rules. The price to be won is the chaos they seek and the consequences for them playing a wrong game is unfulfillment. If only you know the joy that war mongers derive when their planned wars is going as they want and the sadness they feel when it isn't. A man that wants a successful marriage is also a player by virtue of having an objective of wanting a successful marriage or relationship, and he could attempt to play a game of being honest, caring/attentive and non-judgmental in his words and actions toward the desires of his better half. A love-vendor plays a game of emotional manipulation, amongst other tactics to keep his girls.As long as one has an objective in mind, they become players-- playing games for their objective to come to fruition.With a thorough digest of the above content, you can begin to understand that playing games isn't a bad thing, neither should it be viewed as negative. It all depends on what kind of game you as a player decides to play. Now you know why they say that life is a game. Ready player 1 Anyone who plays games must believe in the objective of their game and how they plan to achieve their objective. If not, why even play? This leads us to the second partThe Error of Pick-up linesPick-up lines are an effect, and not a cause. You might get confused and I can understand. it took me a while to understand what I'm writing too.See it this way: Night time comes with the urge to sleep, but that doesn't mean one cannot sleep in the afternoon under the hot sun, but you all reading this would agree with me that the feeling that comes with a night sleep triumphs that of sleeping in the afternoon.Flowing in pick-up lines, especially towards girls, enough to make them trip and drip, are an effect of primarily seeing girls as your complementary equal. You don't flow in pick-up lines by reading or cramming it from a book. "Baby, does your father sell okra, because you draw my attention" lolIf you don't believe the pick-up lines that you read in a relationship guide or book, you'll face a lot of resistance expressing those lines by word of mouth because they're not true to you. Because you don't believe them. And the lady listening to these pick-up lines off your lips is likely to sense through feeling, how awkward you sound, even if you're just meeting her for the first time. For instance, how can a man comfortably call a girl "baby girl" when he's enforces in his mindset that all girls have to work a 9-5 job, mostly a masculine kind of job, and also take care of himself and the children.Do babies prepare their milk and change their diapers themselves? Parents serve their babies, and not the other way around. How can he call a girl "baby girl" when he constantly flares at her for getting 'things' wrong, instead of putting things in place where she's no longer in charge of that section, and is taken to a section that compliments her strength as a woman. A baby girl is a "baby" first. if he doesn't believe that babies can make mistakes repeatedly, how can he comfortably consider a grown up lady as a baby girl, when he's always analysing and reminding her of all her mistakes and weaknesses.How can he use the same lips he has used to call other girls profane names, only to now use those lips to try to spill sweet names to another set of girls?How can he treat girls in a masculine manner and still have the guts to call that newly converted masculine woman a 'baby girl"So you see that the ability to flow in pick-up lines are an effect of understanding both sexes and not by cramming pick-up lines when your foundation is faulty. Seek to truly know people (and be as non-judgmental as you can) before any attempt to drop lines. I can't stress this enough. If you don't know the person you're about to flirt with, how can you tailor your lines to this specific person? What works for miss Funke won't always work for miss Ada. For one to be loved, one has to be vulnerable, especially to the right people. You can only love the people that you genuinely know. If I don't like onions in my food, and I reveal this weakness to you, then you can know how to show love to me by cooking food without onions in it whenever you invite me over to come eat.

title: Unconditional Love: One Step To Love Without Attachments Or Conditions
main_content:
Thread Title: Unconditional Love: One Step To Love Without Attachments Or Conditions

Main Post: 1) Conditional love leads to unconditional loveThe path of conditional love leads to unconditional love, same way childhood leads to adulthood. But this is not an excuse to stay stuck there at conditional love. The same way we suffer when we try to physically restrict the growth of a child to adulthood (if ever possible), is the same way we suffer when we try to hinder our non-physical growth. Growth occurs physically and also non-physically too, and you might have heard of the non-physical growth — you likely call it 'Maturity' or use it in sentences like 'he acts and speaks maturely even for his age'Stagnation in growth leads to suffering, and stagnating doesn't mean not progressing from point A to B, it also mean dwelling at point A and egoistically thinking that it's the growth ceiling.By proper definition, if conditional love is one with conditions, then what truly is unconditional love and how best do we practice this form of love necessary for our growth?Unconditional love simply means loving without attachments, and it can genuinely be expressed when we learn to give exactly what we can afford to lose. For example, if you have #2000 and the amount you can afford to give is #20, do so shamelessly and lovingly without judging yourself on the amount you're giving. 'Shamelessly' in the sense that the amount you're giving might seem little to others, but it's what you can afford to give and sleep well at night. The price for authenticity is attachment because if you really want to live your truth and convictions, you must be willing to lose relationships or attachments which doesn't support the new you. That's the price to pay for being a new you Conditional love occurs in a scenario where you have #2000 and you feel subtly ego compelled to give #500, an amount far greater than what you can can to lose. That #480 difference (compared to the first example of #20) is the price you paid for your suffering of attachments to the outcome of your giving That's where expectations such as “She didn't even thank me enough for helping her with my money” or“I hope he's spending my hard-earned money well and not wasting my sweat!” or“I hope I finally get the respect of my colleague by spending this much in the bar for their drinks” or “I hope he'll love me forever after giving him my virginity” Expectations/ attachments such as these creeps up in our minds when we give more than we genuinely can afford to lose. You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction." —Bhagavad GitaDon't give what you can't afford to lose, because I've learnt from my experience and from that of the people around me, that by so doing, it creates attachments to the expectation that you hope to get from your giving, which then leads to tension and hurt, especially when your expectation(s) doesn't come to fruition. And when such category of givers get hurt because their giving wasn't appreciated, even with a simple “thank you”, they lash out and build a wall of defense around themselves, telling themselves that no one will ever see them so vulnerable again. You likely term this "see finish" This leads to the birth of Pride in them, a situation where people who are capable of giving and receiving love, prevent themselves from giving and receiving love all because they're scared of getting hurt or being underappreciatedThis is the real definition of Pride.[LINK] unconditional love to yourself or to others isn't limited to physical cash alone. You could also learn to invest the time that you can afford to lose on someone(relationship) or a project and not feel regret. Same goes for trust, tolerance and other non physical goodsNow this brings us to a twistIf unconditional love means expressing love to others or to yourself, without expecting anything in return, then the best set of people to practice your unconditional love of giving are towards stingy people or people who find it difficult to say a "thank you" for the help you've rendered to them. It's not primarily for you to wake the up from their slumber of ungratefulness but for you to feel happy to have been of genuine help to those who need it.The joy on the face of a person you've helped or the thought of you being a factor to reduce someone's suffering should be enough reward for you, as a genuine giver. The act itself should be your reward.The best set of people to express your unconditional love of non-sexual attention to, especially as a man, are physically non-attractive ladies, or beautiful girls who are in very serious relationships with other men.If you, as a man, can still love a physically attractive girl who is in a very serious relationship with another man, with no expectation of a thank-you-sex from her as a payment for the "unconditional love" you just expressed towards her, therein lies your growth.Love that security that cannot offer you an appointment letter to aso rock. Love that your cleaner that cannot even help you with job connects.Little wonder why Jesus said, "love your enemies"This is because our enemies are the people who can't reciprocate our love. Instead, they'd even repay us with hate. Lol. A form of repayment which shouldn't bother a true giver. Learn to discern what that meansBy giving what we can genuinely afford to lose, we remain at peace with ourselves regardless of the outcome of our giving. To summarize, a) Give what you can afford to lose b) Increase your capacity for giving, because that's how you grow and not stagnate (Probably you could achieve this with the understanding that all that can be taken away will be taken away from you in time, so they're not your identity. Your identity is what remains when all that can be taken away from you is taken away from you (surname, religion, family, skin color, tribe, gadgets etc)One love

title: Dear Single Mothers, Let’s Talk About Marriage Again.
main_content:
Thread Title: Dear Single Mothers, Let’s Talk About Marriage Again.

Main Post: DEAR SINGLE MOTHERS, LET’S TALK ABOUT MARRIAGE AGAIN.There is a conversation we need to have honestly.Imagine a 34-year-old woman with three children. Her first child is 17, the second is 11, and the last is 5. Unfortunately, the three children have different fathers.She now says, “I am a lover girl. I want a serious relationship. I want to settle down and get married.”Immediately, some people will say:“Three children for three different men? Forget marriage.”Some men have even made it a personal rule:“Once a woman has three children for different men, I can never marry her.”But should we really judge every woman based on the worst examples we have seen?A woman having three children from three different relationships tells us something about her past. It doesn't automatically tell us everything about who she is today.At the same time, let's be honest with ourselves.A woman who has children from different fathers must be prepared to answer serious questions about her past. What happened in those relationships? What choices did she make? What has she learned? Has she taken responsibility for her decisions? Is she emotionally stable? What kind of relationship does she want now?And a man considering her for marriage has every right to ask those questions.He also has every right to say, “This isn't the family situation I want.”That's his choice.But there is a difference between saying “I don't want this situation” and saying “No woman in this situation deserves marriage.”Those are two completely different things.SINGLE MOMS, PLEASE DON'T LOSE YOURSELF TRYING TO PROVE SOMETHING.If you genuinely want marriage, don't allow desperation to make you accept any man simply because he is willing to date you.You don't need to convince every man that you're marriage material.You need to become the kind of woman who is emotionally mature, responsible, self-aware and ready for a healthy partnership.Your children also matter.The man you choose isn't just becoming your boyfriend or husband. He is potentially becoming part of your children's lives. Choose carefully.And please, don't enter another relationship thinking:“At least this one will finally marry me.”That mindset can make you ignore red flags just because you are afraid of starting over.AND TO THE MEN...You are allowed to have standards.You are allowed to say you don't want to marry a woman with children from previous relationships.But if you meet a single mother, judge the woman in front of you, not every single mother you've heard stories about.There are responsible single mothers.There are irresponsible single mothers.There are women who made terrible relationship choices and genuinely changed.There are also women who continue making the same mistakes.Just like there are responsible men, irresponsible men, faithful men, unfaithful men, mature men and immature men.One bad example should not become the standard for everybody.MOST IMPORTANTLY, SINGLE MOMS...Don't let society convince you that because you have children, you must settle for the first man who shows interest.You still deserve respect.You still deserve companionship.You still deserve a healthy relationship.But remember:Wanting marriage is not enough. You must also be ready for a healthy marriage.And sometimes, the most important relationship you need to fix first is the relationship you have with yourself.Your past may explain you.It does not have to permanently define you.

As for me even if I had kid's outside I can never marry a single mother that's why I'm a king in my lane I chose and control how I live my life.

Yes, I see the point you’re making.You’re talking about a 34-year-old woman with three children, each having a different father—the first child is 17, the second is 11, and the last is 5. She describes herself as a “lover girl” and says she wants a serious relationship and eventually marriage.Your argument is that some Nigerian men may reject her automatically because of her history, with comments like “If you already have three children for three different men, I can’t marry you.” Yet, you’re questioning whether it is fair to use one person’s experience—or the behaviour of a minority of women—to judge all single mothers.I also understand the point about priorities in Nigerian relationships: rather than simply judging a woman by the number of children she has or the number of fathers involved, a man considering marriage should look at her character, emotional maturity, accountability, relationship history, parenting, values, financial responsibility, and what she has learned from her past.At the same time, there is another side: a man is also entitled to decide that raising or accepting responsibility for three children from three previous relationships is not the family structure he wants. That preference doesn't automatically make him wicked or judgmental.The strongest version of your argument, therefore, isn't “men must marry women with three children.” It's: Don't turn one person's complicated relationship history into a universal verdict on every single mother. Assess the individual before you.And yes—the “one in a hundred” being used to judge the other 99 is the heart of what you're saying.

I always feel guilty when I hurt a soul ..What you are describing is actually something worth taking seriously—not because you are destined to become a bad husband, but because you are already aware of the danger of becoming hardened by past experiences.Being hurt repeatedly can make a caring person swing from one extreme to another:“I will do anything for a woman” → “Women can never be trusted.”Both extremes can hurt you.TikTok relationship content can teach you useful things about boundaries and manipulation, but be careful not to let algorithms convince you that the worst behaviour of some women represents women generally. You already know how to love.The test is whether you can love her without making her pay for the wounds of your past.And if you're genuinely God-fearing, then don't let bitterness become your new god.
